title: The Nameless Hero and the Exiled Prince
author: Clarke (Ackivili)
tags: Phainon is Down Bad (Honkai: Star Rail)
summary: Like the downfall of many civilizations, traitors within the royal inner circles poison the minds of kings and queens. Castrum Kremnos was no exception. It has steadily declined over the years. King Eurypon's madness has pushed the kingdom to the brink of collapse, and the ongoing armed conflict with the Ohkeman Kingdom was accelerating their destruction. In desperation, the mighty kingdom called for an armistice—not merely a ceasefire, but a resolution to end the conflict altogether. They proposed an alliance between their kingdoms. News of this spread throughout Amphoreus overnight. Two of the strongest kingdoms were forming an alliance that would significantly alter the course of history. An agreement of blood needed to be established between the two kingdoms. Castrum Kremnos was required to offer up a bride from their royal family to be married to another royal family member in Ohkema. Phainon, a collateral member of the royal family adopted from the fallen Aedes Elysiae territory, was tasked with selecting the bride. His choice shocked the entire world: he chose not from the offered brides but instead pointed to Mydeimos, the crown prince of Castrum Kremnos.

chapters.title: Chapter 1: The Exiled Prince
chapters.html:
Everything was moving in a blur. Mydei hardly had a moment to consider his next steps before even more chaos erupted around him. He had just returned back to Castrum Kremnos after his time in exile. At first, he was all set to take action and seize the throne, even if it meant putting an end to his father's life. No celebrations. No festivities. No homecomimg.

And indeed there was no time for it. Because beyond their gates had come a royal dromas carriage from the Ohkeman Kingdom. There was tension in the air, and Mydei couldn’t comprehend what was happening.

Why were they standing by while their enemy nation strolled right into their gates? Not a single spear was raised in revolt.

“Just what had happened while we were away?” Mydei furrowed his brows in thought. He ordered his retainers to quickly figure out the details of the current situation.

Castrum Kremnos was a barbaric land to most of the people of Amphoreus, but this was a far cry from how they truly were. Outsiders had never entered their gates this easily, and so it was such a surprising and beautiful sight to these foreigners when seeing the true magnificence of the kingdom.

The Ohkeman ambassadors arrived to verify the identities of the brides and draft the details of the marriage contract. As it was no secret that this was to become a political engagement, both parties needed to have a fair and equitable agreement.

Advisors of the Royal Kremnoan court welcomed and ushered them into the palace. As soon as the large imposing doors of the palace closed, the residents watching finally released their bated breaths. Many of them returned their attention to the returning prince, congratulating him for successfully overcoming all the trials that were set against him.

The royal guards urged the prince to finish speaking with the townsfolk and promptly receive the king's orders. One of his retainers returned and whispered to him a brief explanation of events that transpired days before their return.

A peace alliance was being formed between Castrum Kremnos and Ohkema, a statement that Mydei would have never believed if it weren’t happening right now. This just did not make sense as Kremnoans were known to be extremely prideful and it was outrageous to allow anyone to become their equals.

Mydei had just returned from his lifelong exile. The place before him felt unfamiliar, and the cheerful smiles of the village folk seemed insincere to him. He longed to experience the warmth of coming home, but instead, this place served as a constant reminder that he was not truly wanted. Or rather, a reminder that he needed to endure significant trauma before he could ever feel deserving of belonging here.

He could not remember how it all began: his father's madness. There had been a time in his childhood when he was a happy prince, wandering through the corridors of Castrum Kremnos. He was a prince like any other, raised with a strict upbringing but still granted enough freedom to feel like a true child. However, everything changed when he was abruptly cast aside by his father, King Eurypon. He was forced to live independently outside the palace walls, without servants or guardians to care for him. He was expected to learn how to survive on his own and train as a warrior without any assistance. At just five years old, he was torn from his mother’s arms and thrown into the sea of souls.

His mother, Queen Gorgo, would not stand for it. She went so far as to challenge his father to a duel, which in Kremnoan tradition meant a battle to the death. Gorgo was the fiercest warrior this kingdom had ever known, which was precisely why Eurypon chose her to be queen in the first place. Everyone knew Eurypon would not stand a chance against her.

However, on the day of the duel, onlookers noted something strange about Gorgo. She appeared sluggish and weakened even before the fight had started. It was later discovered that poison was eating away at her life, and that was how Eurypon dealt with her. Even within the most honorable customs of their kingdom, Eurypon chose the coward's way.

As Mydei was still a child at that time, no one could bring themselves to tell the poor boy that his mother had been slain by his own father. For years, he remained unaware of the events unfolding within the kingdom and channeled all his energy into becoming stronger. In his early teens, when Mydei's natural charisma attracted many followers, an elderly lady he recognized approached him. She was his mother's handmaiden and handed him a letter that appeared worn from years of being kept hidden away. It was a letter from his mother.

The first thing Gorgo wrote in the letter was, "By the time you read this, I have already passed away. But I know that you will make it through, my sweet Mydeimos."

In the letter were the many wishes and dreams she held for her brave little son. She wanted him to know that there was not a day she didn’t worry for him as he was forced away from the kingdom. She wouldn’t defend her husband's actions and regretted not noticing the signs sooner. A challenge for a duel had been made to his father, and despite her weakening state, she refused to back down and succumb to inaction. She was prepared to put everything on the line if it meant there was a chance to bring her son home.

"Never forget your father, Mydeimos. Never forget this despicable, weak, and spineless fool. May the lance of fury guide you to success, my child. And may you finish what I started—what I wish I could have ended."

The young Mydeimos, who had never shed a tear since the day he was cast out of the kingdom, felt his whole body freeze with realization. It had been years since his mother's passing. For years, he had strived to steel himself and become stronger in hopes of reuniting with his family, foolishly believing that one day his father would recognize his strength and welcome him back as the crown prince. He was never going to be welcomed back. All the assassination attempts against him over the years were not challenges posed by his father; the king only wanted him dead.

That night he learned of his mother's passing, he sought solitude in a quiet wheat field enveloped by darkness. For the first time since childhood, he wept, albeit quietly. He didn't want anyone to see or hear him. This was a moment of weakness he would not reveal to any of his father's mercenaries. He simply wanted to mourn his mother properly and contemplate his next steps. Returning as the dutiful crown prince of Castrum Kremnos was no longer an option for him. An intense loneliness washed over him, as if no one in this world wanted him anymore. He was only 12 years old.

He felt sudden rustling around him, and his senses immediately kicked in as he thrust a blade toward the intruder who had approached him. A loud clank and a pained cry erupted from the visitor. A young boy, about his age and with snowy white hair, stumbled onto his backside, his flimsy little shield now bearing a large gash along its side.

Mydei froze, realizing he had nearly harmed an innocent child. In a panic, he quickly covered the boy's mouth, fearing he might scream for help. However, the boy looked up at him with bright blue eyes, filled with awe. Mydei slowly removed his hand, unsure of what to say.

"Wow! You're really strong!" The white-haired boy beamed up at him with a toothy grin. Mydei was taken aback, not expecting such a response after almost harming him. He suddenly remembered the tears he had shed earlier and quickly wiped them away, feeling embarrassed about his emotional state.

"I didn't mean to startle you. I thought I heard a chimera whimpering nearby and wanted to check if they were in danger." The boy stood up and brushed off his shorts. "My mom can make us some pancakes! They’re sure to lift our spirits. Oh, I’m sorry! I forgot to ask for your name. My name is Khaslana! What’s yours?"

Mydei couldn't respond right away. He hadn't encountered children his age in a long time, having traveled through very dangerous places. However, the white-haired boy's enthusiasm was somewhat infectious, and he couldn't help but let out a soft laugh.

"Mydeimos," he replied in a quiet voice, glancing around as if concerned that mercenaries might be nearby.

"Woah… Even your name is really cool!" Khaslana chuckled, gripping his tattered shield tightly against his chest. However, the smile on his face quickly vanished when he looked up and glanced over Mydei's shoulder.

Quickly, he pushed Mydei behind him and lifted his shield high. An assassin had their sights set on Mydei's back, but he fortunately noticed just in time. With a loud clank, his shield almost gave way and shattered.

The tall wheat surrounded them, and the darkness of the night hindered their movement. However, it also provided the advantage of keeping them out of the assassin's line of sight. Mydei grabbed the boy's hand and dragged him into a sprint.

Khaslana paused for a moment and tugged at Mydei's arm, directing him to another path. "This way. It will lead us to the village."

"No. It's not safe to lead them toward your family." Mydei's eyes trembled with urgency. He released Khaslana's hand, leaving the other boy perplexed. "Go. Those people are only after me."

Khaslana didn't understand what Mydei meant. He believed they were merely robbers in the night, looking to kidnap young children as hostages. "It's okay. The village can protect you. I can protect you!" he insisted, tightening his grip on his nearly broken wooden shield.

Mydei felt a wave of frustration because it would be difficult to explain his situation. Before he could say anything, the mercenaries had already caught up to them. This time, Mydei was ready. He skillfully deflected their attacks and knocked out a few of them with a single strike.

He ensured that Khaslana was securely positioned behind him as the fight raged on. Despite the seriousness of the situation, the boy did not hesitate to cheer for him. Although it felt a bit silly, it genuinely lifted Mydei's spirits.

However, this only lasted for a moment. When the attackers noticed that they were no match for this beast of a child, they shifted their focus to the boy standing behind their target.

Mydei quickly recognized that the attackers had shifted their focus and hurried to intercept them. However, he was too late. One of the assailants managed to reach Khaslana and thrust a blade directly at him.

Khaslana, just like the two other times, bravely raised his shield to block the attack. However, this time, the already tattered wooden shield splintered and shattered from the impact. The force of the blow pushed the white-haired boy back, sending him flying a considerable distance before he splashed into the nearby water.

Anger surged in Mydei's vision, and he no longer held back. He had been doing everything in his power to protect the boy behind him, ensuring he would not be harmed. But the attackers were fools to change their target. Mydei unleashed his fury upon them like a vicious beast. Though small in stature, the force of his strength could topple a large animal.

It didn’t take long for the fight to come to an end. The mercenaries lay motionless on the ground, their weapons shattered around them.

Mydei swiftly shifted his focus to where Khaslana had been thrown. He scanned the area, hoping to catch a glimpse of the young boy swimming back to shore safely. However, the water remained eerily still, and there was no sign of him.

The young prince rushed toward the water and dove in. He swam as far as he could, hoping to catch a glimpse of the young boy. However, the sky was now fully dark, providing no help in seeing anything beneath the surface. Panic set in as he surfaced, desperately calling out for Khaslana.

But alas, only silence greeted him back. There was no sign of the white-haired boy.

He continued his search tirelessly until the sun finally rose above the horizon.

However, he never found Khaslana again.

He returned to the shore and sank to his knees, his gaze fixed on the shattered remnants of the wooden shield beside him. He picked up the painted gem that had been affixed to the center of the toy shield and held it tightly against him.

This was the second time in his life that Mydei experienced the weight of grief.

From that moment forward, he vowed never to fail again. His mother's blood stained his father's hands, but Khaslana's blood was on his.

"Your Highness?"

Mydei was slightly startled away from his thoughts. His retainer had been trying to catch his attention for a while. "What is it?"

"It's nothing," Mydei replied, shaking his head. "What is Eurypon up to?" His voice was cold, revealing his suspicions about the king's reasons for summoning him.

"The king has ordered for you to escort the bridal candidates to the Ohkeman border. It was deemed fitting for the crown prince to lead the royal family members there," the retainer said with a strained voice, disliking that the crown prince was already being sent away so soon after his return home.

"Why can't the king himself be the one to send away his family members? I don't imagine this being difficult for him." He scoffed at the end.

"The… advisors said it would be unwise for the king himself to attend a mere bride selection ceremony." The retainer emphasized the word "advisors," hinting to Mydei that the same individuals who had once plotted against his life were still active.

"Very well." Mydei quietly breathed and turned towards the droma carriages that were being prepared near the gates of the palace.

"But your Highness!" the retainer implored, trying to reason with him. "We cannot accompany you this time. It's too dangerous."

"Believe me, being within this madman's walls is more dangerous than anywhere else in the world," Mydei retorted, turning on his heel and striding forward, ignoring the retainer's pleas.

There were a dozen collateral members of the royal family being ushered toward the prepared carriages. Noble parents cried as they begged the guards not to take their children to Ohkema. Most of the brides were beautiful omegas with enough royal blood to qualify as bridal candidates. It was no surprise that their families were weeping for them. Being married off to an Ohkeman royal likely meant they would never see their loved ones again.

And with Ohkema being a longstanding enemy of their nation, there was no guarantee of how their children would be treated there. For all these parents knew, their children could simply be enslaved.

He wondered for a brief moment if his mother once wept for him the same way back then.

When the nobles saw him, they quickly knelt before him. Although these individuals were more or less distant relatives, he could tell their expressions of respect were insincere.

They pleaded with him to reconsider negotiations with the Ohkemans, insisting that these foreigners should not be allowed to take their children away from home. He couldn't help but laugh inside his thoughts.

"I'll see what I can do," Mydei replied, his expression blank. He offered no assurances but didn't want to leave them entirely in despair.

The bridal candidates appeared extremely tense, each adorned in beautiful white silk dresses accented with golden ornaments. Given the nature of the peace agreement, it was expected that the royal families would present their most beautiful unmarried omega children. Some of these young men and women were barely of age, anxious about their futures should they be chosen as brides.

Mydei felt a deep sense of sympathy for the bridal candidates. Their worries were justifiable, and he wished there could be a more favorable resolution to the ongoing war. Although they still had a long journey ahead to reach Ohkema, he lacked confidence in his ability to find a solution. However, he needed to first meet with the Ohkeman royals to assess the situation.

Since he was in a carriage that held many children with royal Kremnoan blood, Mydei felt confident that there would be no attempts on his life, at least until they completed the long journey. For the first time in a long while, he allowed himself to relax and get some rest.

chapters.title: Chapter 2: The Nameless Hero
chapters.html:
The council of elders meeting was dragging on, filled with arguments and debates over the upcoming peace agreement between Ohkema and Castrum Kremnos. At a certain point, Phainon lost interest in the discussions and began gazing at the horizon where the World-Bearing Titan loomed.

He knew he likely didn't need to be there, as he wasn't a true member of the royal family. However, their monarch, Cerydra, had repeatedly emphasized that, despite being adopted, he belonged just as much as anyone else in attendance. Whether or not the rest of the council believes that is no longer his concern.

His focus returned to the meeting as the heads of the noble families began to raise their voices.

"I refuse to sacrifice the futures of my children by marrying them off to those barbarians!" one of the noble heads shouted angrily. Since he had the most unmarried children, the council had somehow deemed this union his responsibility.

The other nobles in attendance began to look away, avoiding eye contact with both the shouting noble and the council of elders. It seemed they had conveniently overlooked this aspect of the agreement. One of Ohkema's children was required to be married off to a Kremnoan.

It was no surprise that this reaction occurred. War and strife had engulfed the Ohkeman Kingdom and Castrum Kremnos for centuries. To most citizens of Ohkema, the people of Kremnos were seen as battle-hardened barbarians, lacking in manners and intelligence.

Kremnoans similarly viewed Ohkemans as weak and pretentious individuals from a kingdom deemed uncivilized, stuck in a bygone era, and lacking significant advancements.

Years of conflict obscured both assumptions and beliefs, resulting in a profound lack of understanding between the two peoples.

This peace agreement is an opportunity to alter the longstanding perceptions between the two kingdoms. Through this pact, forged in blood, it could finally become possible for the Ohkeman and Kremnoan peoples to gain a deeper understanding of one another and to foster lasting peace for the coming years.

That is, assuming both parties are genuinely open to such an arrangement in the first place.

More shouting and finger-pointing ensued, with everyone refusing to sully their family lineages with Kremnoan blood. They reached a standstill, and no one was willing to cooperate any longer. Tension was high, and the council of elders began to worry. A messenger had already informed them that the Kremnoan bridal candidates were on their way to Ohkema.

Just as some nobles were preparing to leave the Dawncloud, one of them raised their voice with a suggestion. "Isn't his highness Phainon a suitable candidate? He is an unmarried collateral family member, after all, and has been graced by our monarch herself."

Everyone's eyes darted towards Phainon's direction. They stared at him with opportunistic glances, some already smiling in agreement. "Why, yes! His Highness is indeed a wonderful choice for this union! Cerydra's most loyal… knight would certainly be an excellent option." The word "knight" was emphasized to disguise another derogatory term they had been using against Phainon behind his back.

Phainon stood frozen in shock, struggling to conceal the confusion that washed over his face. "So that's how it is," he murmured to himself, lowering his gaze. He found himself unable to refute their claims.

He was well aware of how the nobles and the council of elders viewed him. As a common boy from the fallen Aedes Elysiae, he felt out of place among everyone in this gathering. Only a few people in Ohkema regarded him with genuine friendliness, and one of them was their monarch, Cerydra. No one understood why this orphaned boy had been adopted into royalty while most nobles were intent on preserving their lineages for centuries.

His existence as a collateral member of the royal family challenged their traditions, and it seemed to undermine the sanctity of their noble bloodlines.

When he first arrived in Ohkema as a young teen, he felt the weight of envy from those around him, their gazes following him in every corner of the kingdom. At one point, he even contemplated leaving the kingdom to somehow return to Aedes Elysiae.

He knew even as a child that going back would mean death. The black tide that swept through his hometown claimed every life. The plague was so devastating that many kingdoms agreed the only way to prevent its further spread was to incinerate the town entirely. He survived only because, when the first symptoms emerged, he had been hurried away to seek assistance from neighboring kingdoms.

The young boy watched as flames consumed his town, taking with them all the people who had stayed behind. His family, his neighbors, the younger children who looked up to him, his best friend—each one was gone.

Most people viewed Cerydra's decision as tyrannical and evil. However, she preferred to be seen as a tyrant if it meant keeping the rest of Amphoreus safe from danger.

She brought Phainon back to Ohkema with her, feeling a sense of sympathy for him. At this point, Phainon had ceased speaking to anyone. The boy was overwhelmed with shock and stress, which was entirely understandable.

Initially, he was to be given a small place in the Mamoreal market to live independently. However, the oracles of Okhema delivered a prophecy to Cerydra concerning the young boy. This prophecy stated that he was destined to bear a significant responsibility that would bring about change in the kingdom in the coming years.

To ensure that the boy remained within her reach and was kept safe, she needed him to be someone who lived inside the palace. However, it was challenging to justify allowing a commoner boy to suddenly take up residence within those walls.

One of her advisors suggested that she officially adopt the young boy to raise his political stature while keeping him close. To conceal the boy's identity and his role in the prophecy, they crafted a narrative in which she felt a profound sense of guilt for him and decided to adopt him. This would eliminate any suspicions about why he was residing in the palace and would also enhance her public image when the people heard the touching story.

The adoption was a success, and the people of Ohkema praised the imperator. However, it was no surprise that those of true royal lineage held contempt for this commoner boy who, by chance, had found himself in such fortunate circumstances. Somehow, they seemed to overlook the tragedy that brought him to this situation in the first place.

During the official ceremony that conferred the young boy's title, he was named Phainon of Aedes Elysiae, becoming a royal member of the Ohkeman kingdom. One might assume he would feel joy for this new opportunity in life; however, the young boy, having lost everything, including his true name, still longed for his home.

Years passed, and the boy navigated his new life quite successfully. He never lost his inner brightness, even though it took a considerable amount of time to readjust. Although there were still setbacks and drama within the noble circles, his wit and adaptability enabled him to avoid most of it. He received a proper education and maintained a positive reputation among the Ohkeman people. It was rather quite challenging for the noble circles to tarnish his name.

When he came of age, his secondary gender became a subject of interest. Most anticipated that he would be a Beta due to his lack of significant lineage. However, some believed he might manifest as an Alpha because of his striking features and notable accomplishments.

He was a late bloomer, leading most to believe that he had indeed remained a Beta, as was common. However, one day, a powerful aura surged through the palace walls, overwhelming everyone, even the most dominant Alphas. He was swiftly moved to a separate tower within the palace and locked inside, with little to no chance of escape.

Phainon had manifested as an Enigma, a trait that most people believed was merely a legend. The number of confirmed Enigmas in history could be counted on one hand. His pheromones were so potent that even the imperator was taken aback by their ability to incapacitate everyone within the palace walls.

The idea of offering an Omega to assist him during his rut was quickly dismissed. It was determined that it would be safer for everyone if he endured it alone while securely locked in the tower. For someone who had just manifested, the situation was deemed far too dangerous. Even Omegas, who typically found strong Alpha pheromones appealing, felt overwhelmed and intimidated by the ones Phainon emitted. It was as if Phainon himself was issuing a warning for everyone to keep their distance from him.

His rut lasted nearly a month, prolonged by the absence of assistance. His loyal retainers and friends grew increasingly concerned for him and urged the imperator to at least provide him with some medicinal tonics to ensure his well-being.

However, even for his own Beta retainers, approaching the tower proved to be a challenge. The farthest distance any of the Beta retainers could reach nearly knocked them unconscious, forcing them to retreat.

Finally, the aura surrounding the tower had dissipated after a full month. The retainers wished to rush in immediately, but the guards needed to hold them back to ensure that it was truly safe now.

Phainon was discovered asleep inside the tower. They had honestly anticipated that the interior would be completely destroyed and that there would be signs of his attempts to escape. However, the inside was entirely clean, except for some items that had been knocked over when he was initially rushed in. It was a cold winter, yet the nearby blankets remained untouched.

The retainers and his close comrades feared the worst when they saw him lying motionless on the bed. They hurried to his side and checked his pulse. Fortunately, he was merely asleep, and his body temperature felt slightly high, which was understandable since he had just emerged from his rut.

It was quite a mystery to them, as this was not a common sight during an Alpha's rut. They quickly moved him into the infirmary to check his overall health, considering he had been locked up without food and water for a month. Healers from the Grove were contacted to ensure his well-being.

An old classmate, Hyacinthia, took charge of checking his health, and the results were quite surprising. He was remarkably healthy and exhibited no issues despite the circumstances he had endured. It was almost as if Phainon had merely been asleep for all that time. However, he had lost a significant amount of weight and needed to be provided nourishment as soon as possible.

While the tests were ongoing, Phainon gradually emerged from his coma-like state. His voice was somewhat hoarse as he asked with a tone of curiosity, "What's going on? Am I back in the Grove?"

Hyacine let out a sigh of relief upon seeing that he had woken up on his own. "What do you remember?"

Phainon sat up with the help of his retainers. He felt uncomfortable due to his stiff muscles and wore a look of confusion. "I think I got a really bad fever, and I fainted."

She proceeded to give him a brief summary of the events from the past month. As Phainon listened, he was taken aback by the information. He had learned about Enigmas in school, but the knowledge was so limited that he struggled to recall much about them.

After the checkup concluded, Phainon was summoned by the council of elders. This sudden manifestation of his trait had somehow changed the council's perception of him significantly. A greater sense of respect was now afforded to him, especially since all Enigmas in the past had been individuals of notable achievements.

However, Cerydra ordered that the manifestation of this trait remain a secret, even from the noble factions. Phainon was to be presented to the public as having only manifested as an Alpha, suggesting to the council that his trait could serve as a strategic advantage in the future—a hidden card, so to speak. The council had no objections to this plan, and it was noteworthy that manifesting as a dominant Alpha was already an impressive achievement for someone born without royal blood.

Despite the improved treatment, old jealousies persisted, and the majority of the nobles and elders continued to view him as an outsider. They merely acknowledged his existence but never truly welcomed him.

The current meeting exemplified this treatment perfectly.

All eyes were fixed on Phainon, eager to gauge his reaction. The weight of their stares bore down on him, silently conveying that he had no right to refuse. Who better to offer to the Kremnoans than this lowborn "royal"? He lacked significant power in the kingdom. He wasn’t a lord of any territory, and he had no family to concern themselves with his future.

Phainon understood all of this, yet he still felt a bitter pang in his heart. Despite having steeled himself for years, he still couldn't fully hide his emotions.

Hysilens, the knight commander of Ohkema and Cerydra's right-hand woman, suddenly spoke up in the charged atmosphere. The nobles braced themselves, ready to bite their tongues and mutter curses under their breaths. They were well aware that the imperator consistently favored Phainon, treating him as if he were truly her own son. As Hysilens commanded everyone's attention, they braced for the worst.

However, what Hysilens said next shocked them: "Her Majesty agrees with the nobles' sentiment. This would be a great opportunity for Phainon to prove his standing."

Everyone was stunned, with Phainon feeling the weight of their disbelief. He struggled to find his voice as he glanced at Hysilens and then looked up toward the chamber where Cerydra remained obscured from sight.

The nobles erupted in praise for the imperator, pleased that she recognized the brilliance of the suggestion. They highlighted Phainon's potential as an exceptional representative who could lead the way for significant change in Amphoreus. They now spoke as if their earlier reasoning for choosing Phainon had not been driven by ill intent.

Hysilens fixed her gaze on Phainon again, as if waiting for his response.

Phainon swallowed nervously, a small smile attempting to conceal his disappointment. "It would be my honor, your Majesty," he said, bowing his head toward the imperator's concealed throne.

The nobles and elders erupted once more in applause and praise. Some of them openly expressed their relief that their children would now be safe, while others quietly snickered in Phainon's direction.

It turns out his favor wouldn’t last forever. A sad smile lingered on his face as they were being dismissed from the hall. He realized he should have expected this eventually. He owed his life to this kingdom, and perhaps this was its way of collecting the dues he owed.

"Phainon." A familiar voice called out from behind him. They were now quite a distance from the main palace, and all the nobles had departed to share good news with their families.

He turned around and found Aglaea with a somber expression. It was said that the golden weaver had shown no emotion since losing her sight, but Phainon had come to know her well enough to notice the subtle differences.

"Hey, Aglaea…" He forced a smile, but it was difficult, and his voice wavered slightly. "I know you’re probably worried about me, but there’s no need. I’ve dedicated my life to serving Ohkema, after all. If this is an order from the imperator, I would be honored to accept it."

"You don't have to act so responsible around me," Aglaea said, her tone almost gently berating. "Just know that you don't have to be forced into this. At the very least, you'll have the opportunity to meet the bridal candidates. If things don't work out, it's not Ohkema who needs a successful peace treaty."

"Regardless, this is a great opportunity that may never happen again. It has the potential to grant Amphoreus lasting peace," he said, a genuine smile spreading across his face this time. "If it means I can usher in that harmony, then I don't think I will truly mind."

Aglaea knew him well, as she was one of the few people who truly valued his presence since he arrived as a young boy. She was also aware of his dreams for the future, which included traveling the world and possibly returning to Aedes Elysiae to rebuild what was once there.

But even with her influence, Aglaea understood that there was not much she could do. Still, she wanted Phainon to know he didn’t have to shoulder this responsibility alone.

Phainon spent the night lost in thought, pondering how this new chapter of his life would unfold. Settling down and starting a family didn’t seem like a bad prospect, but he found himself yearning for the opportunity to make that choice for himself.

He chuckled softly, "I guess it's time for me to let go." He reached for the necklace around his neck, concealed beneath his shirt. It was a silver chain he had purchased for a few coins at the market when he first arrived in Ohkema, and at the end of it hung a golden signet ring.

The memory flooded back to him of that fateful day when he encountered a young boy, roughly his age, who was covered in tattoos and quietly weeping in the wheat fields beyond his hometown.

For some reason, he sensed in that moment that this boy was his destined one. He had no tangible proof, yet the fleeting memory of him would resurface every few days.

Back when he was knocked unconscious by the thief's attacks, all he could remember was being thrown into the water. He had no idea how much time had passed, but when he finally regained consciousness, he found himself pushed upstream into a pile of leaves, completely covered in mud and twigs. By that time, it was already noon, and he hurried back to town, covered in a few scratches and clutching a swollen arm.

His mother cried for nearly an hour when they finally saw him return to the village, especially given the condition he was in. Meanwhile, his father scolded him endlessly and vowed to ground him for the remainder of the summer.

When he inquired about the boy he had encountered the previous night, they claimed they had never seen him. However, some fishermen reported earlier that morning that several unconscious bodies had been found near the shore. At least with that news, he felt somewhat relieved, believing that Mydeimos had likely made it out okay and was probably back with his own family now.

Ignoring his father's shouts, he raced out to the wheat field where he had met Mydeimos, hoping that perhaps Mydeimos had left him a note or a clue about where he had gone. As he picked up the broken fragments of his shield, he stumbled upon something shining, partially buried in the ground from having been stepped on. It was a golden signet ring, and he instantly recognized the seal it bore: the Strife Titan.

"How fitting!" he chuckled to himself, recalling how fierce and strong the boy had been in battle.

Even now, as Phainon stood on the balcony of his room in the Mamoreal Palace, gazing at the night sky, he still smiled at the thought of his destined one. However, a wave of sadness washed over him. "It turns out I won't be able to properly return this to you now…" He clutched the ring tightly to his chest.

Chapter End Notes

chapters.title: Chapter 3: The Engagement
chapters.html:
"Your Highness, we will be arriving at the Ohkeman gates shortly," one of the attendants in the carriage informed Mydeimos.

The tension that had gradually dissipated over the past few days of travel had returned, stronger than ever. The bridal candidates listened intently to the attendant, their bodies stiff with apprehension as they remained still in their seats.

Mydeimos nodded and glanced out the window, observing the grand marble bridges leading to the kingdom's gates. Despite being well-traveled, he had always avoided Ohkema and its allied kingdoms. He was aware that many realms regarded the Kremnoans with considerable foreboding.

Knowing this, Mydeimos struggled to find any viable solutions to their current problem. It would be challenging to suddenly request the dissolution of the marriage agreement without presenting a better alternative. All the contracts had already been signed and sealed by the advisors of both kingdoms. Upon reviewing them, he concluded that the arrangement was, on the whole, a favorable deal for everyone involved.

In the contracts, both kingdoms had established trade routes. Castrum Kremnos was expected to join Ohkema as an ally in wartime efforts. Additionally, they were required to send special forces to assist Ohkeman soldiers in addressing issues in nearby towns plagued by problems such as rebels and mercenaries.

Kremnoan scholars were now allowed to collaborate with scholars from both Ohkema and the Grove. This collaboration would enable both kingdoms to exchange and enhance their skills and innovations. While Castrum Kremnos was renowned for its impressive industrial machinery and infrastructure, Ohkema was rich in agricultural resources and natural wealth. Additionally, their strategic location facilitated trade with nearly all the major kingdoms in Amphoreus, contributing to their status as one of the most culturally diverse kingdoms.

This was an opportunity that would likely not come again if he failed in the renegotiations. Despite spending the last few days strategizing for a better resolution, he remained at a loss. Of course, it was easy to simply sign papers and forgo peace. However, given the history between the two kingdoms, it was natural to seek something with a more significant bond.

At one point, Mydeimos even considered taking the marriage upon himself. However, as an Alpha and the crown prince, he recognized that there was no possibility of an Ohkeman Beta or Omega being sent to Castrum Kremnos under Ohkema's leadership in the peace agreement.

Ohkema held the upper hand in the alliance due to the gradual decline of Castrum Kremnos over the years. The ongoing madness of his father, coupled with relentless warfare, had resulted in disastrous decisions and significant losses, leaving them in dire need of Ohkema's assistance. Not even the pride of a Kremnoan could deceive him into thinking otherwise.

There was no more time for him to ponder, and all he could do was offer comforting words to the bridal candidates. He wasn't sure how he would manage it, but he promised them that they would not suffer at the hands of the Ohkeman kingdom.

The bridal candidates could only manage weak smiles at their crown prince, expressing their gratitude for his care during the journey and for personally escorting them. He should have been back home, celebrating his return after a long exile from his home. Instead, he found himself here, facilitating the peace agreement instead of their mad king.

The dromas came to a halt, signaling their arrival. The carriage doors swung open, and Mydeimos was the first to step out. He assisted each of the bridal candidates as they exited their carriages and guided them through the gates of Ohkema.

Mydeimos instructed one of the advisors accompanying him that he wished to remain a mere observer and not attract any attention. The advisor acknowledged this request and assumed responsibility for leading the ceremony instead. At this point, no one outside of Castrum Kremnos had ever seen their crown prince. It was almost a myth that the kingdom even had a prince, as the only stories people ever heard from traveling bards were about how Eurypon had banished his son as a form of "trial."

The gates were crowded with people, with countless Ohkemans eager to witness this historic moment. A large area in the plaza was designated in the center for the exchange, leaving most of the residents tightly packed along the sides. Mydeimos observed that the architecture of Ohkema was quite different from that of his home. It was clean—no, fresh—like it had a sense of the sun's rays beautifully cradling every corner of the place.

Without much delay, the ceremony began as both advisors from each kingdom exchanged their greetings along with the scrolls they carried. This formal exchange of scrolls signified the allied contracts between the two kingdoms. All that remained was a stamp of blood from the two royal members who were to be wed.

The Ohkeman people who watched were astonished by the royal party's arrival. Most had never seen a Kremnoan before and only held prejudiced notions about them. They were surprised to encounter so many slender and beautiful men and women adorned in elegant robes that mirrored Ohkeman fashion.

Of course, it was difficult for the onlookers to ignore Mydeimos' presence as well. Not only did he stand out starkly, but he also embodied the most exaggerated version of what the Ohkemans had imagined Kremnoans to be. He was tall and imposing, with fiery red tattoos adorning his body. His armor, though incomplete, accentuated his physique in a remarkable way. He was undeniably handsome, exuding the unmistakable aura of a dominant Alpha. Many Ohkeman ladies were already squealing and fawning over him.

Needless to say, their presence in the middle of the plaza was a sight for sore eyes because instead of apprehension, the Ohkemans looked more excited. This atmosphere certainly eased the nerves of the bridal candidates, as they could sense the light and welcoming energy surrounding them.

It was now time to announce the arrival of the Ohkeman royal, who would be choosing his bride. Cheers erupted from the crowd as they enthusiastically called out for the man making his entrance in the center of the plaza.

Phainon had been dreading this moment since that morning, doing his best to appear presentable and formal, even attempting to style his hair back. However, his efforts backfired, and instead of looking polished, he ended up a disheveled mess, prompting the need for Aglaea to step in and intervene.

After a few stern words from Aglaea, he was finally allowed to leave and head to the plaza for the ceremony. He hadn't expected the townspeople to cheer for him so enthusiastically, and it made him feel incredibly shy. He did his best to smile at the crowds and walk steadily. Unbeknownst to everyone watching, his heart was ready to pound out of his chest.

When the bridal candidates caught their first glimpse of the man they might marry, their worries vanished almost immediately. They had expected to be wed to some old, crusty man who had been divorced three times, but instead, they were met with a handsome man sporting a refreshing smile.

Even Mydei was taken aback, but for a different reason. This man seemed oddly familiar, yet there was no way he could have met him, as he belonged to the Ohkeman royal family. His face was the kind that one wouldn't easily forget, so Mydei dismissed it as having seen him in passing at some point in the past.

After disregarding his thoughts, Mydei looked back up at the man, who was now staring intently at him. The man's big blue eyes widened, reflecting an almost shocked expression. Despite Mydei's attempts to look away and ignore the gaze, Phainon kept his eyes fixed on the Kremnoan prince.

This went on for far too long until the Ohkeman advisor cleared his throat and asked Phainon the question everyone was waiting for. "Your Highness? Have you chosen your bride?"

Without looking away, Phainon nodded and strode forward. He was confident and steady, not losing sight of the person who he desired the most. The crowds even burst into more cheering and squealing, excited to see a love story bloom in front of their eyes. The beloved tragic prince, cherished by all, was finally on the brink of his happily ever after.

But the cheers faded almost immediately, replaced by shock.

Phainon had ended up walking past all the bridal candidates in the elegant white robes and went straight for the man who stood behind them. He gently held Mydeimos' left hand and kneeled to him without hesitation.

"I—Uhm. Hi—No, wait. No! Sorry." Phainon stumbled over his words in a panic, leaving everyone in stunned silence.

"Please marry me!" he suddenly exclaimed, his voice ringing out loudly across the now silenced plaza.

Even Mydei was at a loss for words, taken aback by the unexpected turn of events, and could only watch Phainon with a look of confusion.

For what felt like an eternity, silence enveloped the crowd. Then, laughter erupted from one of the royal seats situated above the fountains, shattering the stillness. Cifera couldn't contain her amusement at the hilariously awkward moment unfolding before her and broke the silence with her boisterous laughter. Aglaea swiftly smacked her lightly on the back of the head and cleared her throat loudly, attempting to restore some decorum.

What happened next left the Kremnoan party even more bewildered, as the crowd that had once been shocked was now erupting in loud cheers once more. Nearby, some young ladies were almost praising the gods for this incredible scene.

Mydei was now blushing ever so slightly while trying to remove his hand from Phainon's grasp, but the hand that held him gently was firm.

"Oh—uhm!" The Kremnoan advisor attempted to calm the crowd and attract Phainon's attention. He needed to clarify the misunderstanding that the crown prince was not one of the candidates for this marriage.

Before he could speak, Mydei suddenly recalled his earlier dilemma about how to ensure the Kremnoan party's safe return home. He raised his hand to signal his advisor to hold off on interrupting.

Mydei cleared his throat and closed his eyes, trying to suppress any signs of his slight fluster. "Very well."

Phainon's expression transformed from that of a dejected puppy to the happiest man in the world with just those words. He rose from his knees and grasped both of Mydei's hands, beaming with the largest grin he could muster. In that moment, Mydei recalled why this man felt so familiar to him.

Khaslana: the name etched in his memory. This silly Ohkeman bore an incredible resemblance to him.

The advisor was taken aback by the prince's words. This wasn't supposed to happen! After all, this was the mighty crown prince of Castrum Kremnos, so there was no way this marriage could work out. However, Mydei shot the advisor a stern glance, warning him not to intervene.

Even the bridal candidates appeared anxious, glancing over at the prince. However, the Kremnoans' trust in their crown prince was unwavering; they believed he had a plan for this situation.

The scrolls lay open, ready for both men to sign the agreements together. Mydei removed the armor from his hand and prepared to slice his palm, intending for the blood to drip down. However, Phainon gently took the dagger from him, carefully held Mydei's hand, and turned it over, drawing blood from the side near his pinky instead. This man, whom Mydei couldn't help but think was very strange, explained that drawing blood from the side near his pinky would heal better and be less painful than harming his palm directly.

Mydei would have scoffed at this gesture in any other situation, given his incredible healing speed as a warrior. Instead, the gesture genuinely touched him, even though he still found the man somewhat peculiar.

Amidst the joyful celebrations in the crowd, some nobles deemed Phainon's actions to be quite unbecoming. The man he had chosen was clearly an Alpha, suggesting that this marriage was already destined for failure. Was this Phainon's way of rebelling against them, ensuring that his marriage would ultimately come to an end?

But others had different concerns. Hysilens noticed the unusual body language of the Kremnoan advisor and the bridal candidates when the match was announced. She called over one of the knights and instructed him, "Find out who that man is."

"Yes, Commander!" the knight replied, bowing before swiftly exiting.

It was now too late for anyone to intervene, as Phainon appeared to be on cloud nine, remaining close to and holding on to his bride. The public was also receiving the match incredibly well.

Before the Kremnoan party prepared for their return to Castrum Kremnos, Mydei had the opportunity to speak with them. He instructed them not to inform the king that he had taken the place of the bridal candidates. How they planned to explain and cover for him was left for the advisor to figure out.

Mydei was now being led into Ohkema's palace with the few belongings he had. He thought to himself that these next few days were going to be challenging. However, as long as he could extend the time it would take to figure out the renegotiations, he would gladly accept the situation.

Although it wasn’t entirely unexpected, he didn’t anticipate being sent directly to Phainon’s quarters. He had asked the escorts a few questions, and they were eager to provide answers. This is how he learned that Phainon was an adopted collateral member of the royal family and likely well-loved by the public, based on their comments about him.

Phainon's quarters were situated within the main palace grounds but in a distant annex, separate from the main building. While it wasn't the largest mansion on the property, it still appeared magnificent and had a somewhat homey feel. There was a training yard behind the manor, featuring well-polished stacks of weapons. Mydei noted that this was a better choice than gardens or similar options.

The guards and maids who had escorted him bowed their heads and returned to their duties, leaving Mydei to awkwardly start lingering in front of the manor. He was uncertain about how to interact with this supposed fiancé—though it felt wrong to call him that, as he knew this marriage was not going to happen. The moment the Ohkeman officials discover his true identity, never mind the detail that he is an Alpha, he will have a lot to answer for; thus, his time is now limited.

The doors of the manor's main building suddenly swung open, and this large man of surprising strength rushed towards him.

"Mydeimos!!!" Phainon was almost ready to bridal carry the man into his arms but was quickly stopped by Mydei and was not allowed to come any closer than he already was.

"Your Highness Phainon, I am uncertain about what you are planning with this union. However, I think it would be better for me to clarify things right now."

Hearing this, the broad smile on Phainon's face vanished, replaced by a look of confusion and betrayal. "… What do you mean?"

"You surely are aware that we are both dominant Alphas. I don't need to confirm that, as your presence alone is exemplary. Therefore, it should come as no surprise that this marriage is unlikely to succeed." Mydei spoke clearly, ensuring no one was nearby to overhear their conversation. Upon noticing a suspicious golden beetle on the front of the manor's gated hedges, he suggested that they continue their conversation indoors.

Phainon nodded and led Mydeimos inside the house.

When Mydei noticed that Phainon's expression had turned sullen, he felt a pang of guilt for his directness. "I apologize for being so forward," he said. "You see, I wasn't actually one of the bridal candidates. They were under immense pressure, and their families were quite concerned since no one truly knows how they will adapt to life away from home."

He continued to explain, "But it would be best for you to have a partner who would be able to build a family with you, after all."

Phainon looked up, a new smile forming on his face. "So… does that mean you don't have a preference for Omegas?"

The question perplexed Mydei, and he hesitated before responding, "No. I don't have a preference like that—"

Before he was given the chance to finish his sentence, Phainon beamed at him and was almost ready to lift Mydei in his arms. "I'm actually an Enigma. So if it's children you want, I can give them to you! As many as you want!!!" He confidently exclaimed while holding Mydei close to him.

"HKS!" Mydei cussed after a brief moment of shock, his face flushed completely red with embarrassment.

chapters.title: Chapter 4: The First Night
chapters.html:
When Phainon was called up to stand in the plaza, his hands were sweating, his walk felt awkward, and he was unsure about the expressions he was making. When it finally hit him that he was about to choose from a number of people in front of the Ohkeman public, he suddenly felt uncomfortable. How could everyone be comfortable with a situation that resembled auctioning off goods rather than actual people?

He understood that this was a historic moment, and he wouldn't allow himself to be distracted by starting a debate about the situation. He just needed to choose someone, and from that point on, his life would change. Despite pretending to be innocent and acting as if he were pleased to be in front of the elders and nobles, he felt sad.

The necklace with the signet ring that he had worn for more than half his life was now tucked away in his home, likely never to be seen again. If he were to wear it now, he believed he wouldn't be able to cope. He would only end up thinking about Mydeimos, wondering what the man might look like now.

Perhaps Mydeimos was now as tall as he was, likely well-built like a warrior. He probably had the most beautiful face he had ever seen in Ohkema or even in Amphoreus. It's already been so long that he couldn't remember every detail of him.

Looking up from his deep thoughts, he felt his eyes flutter. "Yeah, maybe he looks just like that," he whispered to himself as he gazed at the man who resembled exactly what he had imagined from across the plaza.

With a head of hair that resembled bright flames, just as he remembered from his memories. His muscles were well-toned, and the contours of his body were reminiscent of a magnificent sculpture. His gaze was serious yet also gentle and dignified, just like a prince, a king even.

When their eyes met, Phainon’s mouth fell slightly agape, and his eyes widened. Was this real? Or was he finally losing his sense of reality? Had the overthinking he had been doing since last night, coupled with the lack of sleep, finally taken its toll on him?

Yet he could clearly hear the cheering around him and see the man in the distance, yet his gaze remained fixed on no one else. He can't be mistaken, right?

Mydeimos.

Mydeimos… Was this the way destiny was still managing to bring them together again?

When the advisor beside him asked if he had found his bride, he didn’t respond. His body seemed to act on its own, moving him forward. Their eyes remained locked on one another, and even when Mydeimos attempted to look away, their gazes would find each other again.

Phainon ended up walking past all the brides who were lined up in wait, and he went straight for him. He awkwardly took Mydei's hand with his clammy, slightly trembling fingers.

Out of nowhere, he dropped to one knee and began to stutter his words. His face flushed with embarrassment, and he had never felt so awkward in his life, fumbling through this first meeting after such a long time. He realized he wouldn't be able to form a coherent sentence right now. So he closed his eyes tightly and announced at the top of his lungs,

"Please marry me!"

The entire plaza fell silent, and everyone was taken aback by the unexpected turn of events. The man before Phainon was undeniably handsome, a striking figure. However, no one believed he was actually part of the selection of brides, especially since he was dressed so differently from the others.

But all that silence didn't matter to the man on his knees. All he could hear in that moment was the pounding of his heart, as if it were about to burst from his chest.

The next thing Phainon knew, he heard the man in front of him say, "Very well."

After hearing that, Phainon almost lunged at him, ready to carry him off. However, with the little control he had left, he simply smiled and held him close. This wasn't a dream, was it? Mydeimos was truly here. He didn't even need to ask, as he was certain of it. The moment their eyes met, Phainon felt that familiar sensation in his chest, just like the first time he had seen him when they were younger.

Everything else faded into a blur. Phainon was so overwhelmed with excitement that he nearly complained when Mydei had to step away for a moment to say goodbye to his people and gather his belongings.

But the advisor stepped forward and informed him that they would escort Mydei to his manor right afterward.

His eyes widened, and without hesitation, he began to run as fast as he could. He suddenly remembered the chaotic state in which he had left his home. Clothes were strewn everywhere, piled across the floor as he had frantically tried to decide what to wear earlier that day. Aglaea was even ready to burn some of his clothing, which he had to wrestle away from her grasp.

Even Mydei was surprised that he willingly let go of him, but he sighed in relief as he still needed to speak with his people after all.

Phainon was panting as he reached his estate and began picking up the items scattered across the floor, tossing them into a bundle inside his wardrobe. He swept as quickly as he could, trying to arrange everything that seemed out of place. Although he was technically royalty, he had never employed maids or butlers to manage the estate. He felt that having such help would be excessive, believing that simply living in such a lavish home was enough for him.

He ended up living completely alone and handled most tasks himself. Learning to cook and clean was a disaster at first, but he adapted quite well. Living alone also made it easier for him when his rut arrived. He could lock up the manor and spend that time alone, as he always did.

His pheromones were no joke. Even when many men and women attempted to seduce him in the past, he would unconsciously release intimidating pheromones, ensuring that most people would not approach him with that intent. Up until his arranged marriage, he had always planned to travel outside Ohkema one day to find his destined one again.

But now that destined one was here—inside Ohkema—and he was his bride, nonetheless!

As he recalled that Mydei was already on his way, he began cleaning up even more hurriedly. What was he supposed to do? Should he start the oven and prepare something for their first dinner together? Perhaps he should turn on the baths? Ohkemans were quite fond of their large public bathhouses, and the nobles took it a step further by having expansive private baths in their homes, some as large as pools. Phainon had one as well, but he rarely used it because he preferred the ones in the Mamoreal Palace to avoid the hassle of cleaning up.

He hurried to the bath, turned on the water, and ensured it would remain hot for later. He pressed a button that opened the shutters in the ceiling, revealing a stunning sunroom bath with an impressive view of the mountain ranges beyond Ohkema. And since it was nearing evening, Phainon believed it would be the most romantic view ever under the night sky.

Before he started blushing from his thoughts, he dashed into the kitchen, grabbed the mixed roast he had marinated the day before, and placed it in the oven to cook. He could prepare other dishes later once Mydei arrived, allowing him to showcase his impressive cooking skills. Surely, Mydei would appreciate a man who could cook well, right?

He made sure to prepare the bedroom by quickly changing the sheets, fluffing the pillows, and adding the duvet that he typically kept in the closet. Although everything was going smoothly, he felt a wave of nervousness. He was arranging his home as if for a newly married couple, conveniently overlooking the fact that they were still just fiancés at this stage. But his mind was racing, and he felt an urgent need for everything to be perfect before Mydei arrived.

When he heard shuffling outside his door, he rushed to open it with a bang. He quickly approached Mydei, already crouching slightly to lift him off his feet. "Mydeimos!!!" He beamed with the brightest of smiles, fully excited that he was finally here.

But then he was stopped. Phainon's heart was racing again, and he was confused. He struggled to grasp what Mydei was saying. Why was Mydei behaving this way? Acting as if… he didn't remember Phainon?

His heart sank, and tears threatened to spill from his eyes. "…What do you mean?"

Mydei began to explain, but Phainon was so overwhelmed by the sound of his own racing heart that all he could grasp was that they were both Alphas and that Mydei wanted him to have the opportunity to build a family. The conversation was becoming increasingly uncomfortable outside, so they decided to go inside first.

Mydei was beginning to feel guilty about how the once-excited pup now appeared as if he had been kicked. He attempted to explain again. Since he was not part of the bridal candidates to begin with, he wanted to come clean with Phainon directly, hoping that perhaps this man could assist him with his plan for renegotiations.

However, Phainon unexpectedly asked a rather inappropriate question: "So… does that mean you don't have a preference for Omegas?"

"No. I don't have a preference like that—"

Phainon's energy surged within him, revitalizing him as if he had been reborn. With a confident and prideful voice, he declared, "I'm actually an Enigma. So if it's children you want, I can give them to you! As many as you want!!!" He meant every word. If Mydei desired 13 kids, he would gladly comply and provide them all! He was confident in his endurance and would willingly try every single day. Observing Mydei's physique, he also felt assured about his partner's capabilities.

While proclaiming this with all his might, he wrapped his arms around Mydei and effortlessly lifted him into the air. Although he was only slightly taller than Mydei, he hoisted him up as if he weighed nothing.

The next thing he knew, he was nearly knocked unconscious by a swift slap from Mydei's palm, which was intended to separate them immediately. Mydei's face was glowing red from embarrassment, and he couldn't believe what he had just heard. "HKS!!!"

Phainon, now with a nosebleed, fell onto his back, a dizzy and goofy expression on his face.

Mydei helped him up onto the couch and apologized profusely for what had happened. He usually had confidence in his self-control over his strength, but that declaration had shocked him so much that he completely miscalculated. But Phainon was simply chuckling with a napkin to his face, confusing Mydei even more.

How could he smile and giggle like a child after being slapped square in the face? Mydei found it completely incomprehensible.

He's as strong as Phainon remembered. Back then, he almost passed out when Mydei tried to stab him during their younger days. At this moment, he realized that Mydei genuinely did not recognize him. The reason for this was unclear to Phainon, and it seemed that something may have happened to him in the past. He was hesitant to inadvertently mention anything that could be traumatic. Perhaps it would be best to gradually help Mydei remember before ultimately disclosing his true identity.

Mydei sighed. He understood that Phainon had a quirky side, but he couldn’t help but wonder if this man truly chose him because he liked him. As a dominant Alpha, Mydei had only ever attracted the interest of Omegas and smaller Betas. The fact that Phainon was an Enigma only added to the confusion. Phainon had the opportunity to select from a host of beautiful and slender bridal candidates earlier, so it was puzzling that he seemed drawn to Mydei instead. This man definitely had unusual tastes.

It was kind of cute. Mydei caught himself thinking that and quickly cleared his throat.

He leaned closer to examine Phainon's face. It still bore a slight redness from Mydei's handprint, but fortunately, the bleeding had stopped. Phainon smiled cheerfully as Mydei inspected him, continuing to inch closer.

Mydei was no fool, and he noticed Phainon trying to close the distance, so he stood up and removed the bloodied napkin. Phainon pouted as the gentle caress of Mydei's hand left his cheek.

"What is that smell?" Mydei's eyes squinted in confusion, looking around the room.

Phainon initially felt a surge of panic, wondering if perhaps his pheromones had leaked out. He had never been the best at controlling his pheromones, and he didn't want to make Mydei feel uncomfortable with them. However, he soon realized exactly what Mydei was referring to.

His mixed roast was burning!

He jumped up from his seat and hurried to the kitchen. Smoke was already billowing out of the oven, and just as Phainon was about to open it, Mydei intervened.

Mydei quickly grabbed the metal skewer and turned off the fire first. "Don't open it yet, or else you'll ruin your whole kitchen," he warned. He then opened the window above the oven to help the smoke escape more easily. "Just let it sit for a while until the smoke clears on its own."

Phainon felt a wave of embarrassment wash over him. Not only had he ruined their dinner plans, but he also felt flustered in front of the very calm Mydei. He looked as if he might burst into tears, but Mydei gently held his arm and guided him to sit at the kitchen counter. "It's fine," he reassured him.

Mydei picked up the apron hanging on the wall, put it on, and began to look through Phainon's kitchen for other ingredients he could use to cook. "I'll make us dinner to make up for… slapping you."

Instead of shedding tears of embarrassment, Phainon felt tears of joy welling up as he watched the beautiful sight of Mydei shuffling around his kitchen, preparing to cook something for them.
