Despite Phainon's protests that he was being truthful and had his honor at stake, Mydei ignored him with a soft smile and finished preparing the meal he made for them. It was a simple porridge using whatever was left in the kitchen.

"Do you want to come to the Mamoreal Market with me? You can pick out anything you want there, since there's nothing left in the kitchen." Phainon's voice trailed off quietly at the end, embarrassed by how unprepared he felt with his fiancé. He wasn't exactly thrilled with suddenly being forced to be politically engaged, so his mind was not really focused on being the most hospitable host.

"Sure. However…" Mydei paused, contemplating how to express his thoughts. "Should I dress more appropriately? I don't think the locals would feel very safe with me wearing Kremnoan armor like this." He spoke plainly, considering how to make the outing more comfortable for Phainon.

"No!" Phainon replied with conviction. "You look just fine, and it shouldn't make you feel self-conscious. I mean, just looking at how amazing your body is would make everyone appreciate it immediately! No, wait—maybe it is a good idea to hide it. Who knows how many will try to woo you? But we're already engaged, so they should have some shame when approaching you. But… argh!!!" At this point, Phainon was clearly battling with himself, and Mydei simply listened to him with an amused smile on his face.

Chapter End Notes

I’m currently stuck at the airport due to cancelled/delayed flights because of the massive typhoon in the area. Please send thoughts and prayers.

Also I hope this random man next to me who keeps glancing at my laptop while I’m writing this (with my biggest pokerface) is enjoying the phaidei smut.

Does anyone have suggestions on how Phainon’s pheromones would smell like? I was thinking of wheat fields, but idk if that smells very good tbh.

chapters.title: Chapter 7: Pheromones
chapters.html:
"Are you always like this with your lovers?" Mydei asked, his tone direct and filled with genuine curiosity.

Phainon couldn't believe his ears and nearly dropped the basket of food he held against his chest. "M-Mydei? Are you upset with me? What did I do wrong?" He quickly began to apologize, puzzled over what could have prompted Mydei to ask such a question.

Their day at the Mamoreal Market had gone smoothly, even with a few minor hiccups along the way. Phainon felt energized all morning, determined to be the best tour guide possible and ensure that Mydei sees the coolest parts of himself. He wanted to impress his fiancé and help him feel comfortable as they explored Ohkema together.

It was technically Mydei's second day in Ohkema, and the residents were likely still discussing him. This presented a good opportunity for Phainon to ensure that everyone held a positive and welcoming view of Mydei.

Phainon made sure to hold all the heavy items himself to show his strength. He knew Kremnoans put strength and power above all else, so he needed to show Mydei that he was a capable husband. His daily sword training was finally proving beneficial.

Whenever they walked along the large paths where dromas would pass, Phainon would always make sure Mydei was safely on the outer side of the road. If he sees that something would catch Mydei's eyes, he would immediately suggest that they take a look or buy it. He even bought Mydei a small bouquet of flowers that could be pinned to his fiancé's coat.

Surprisingly, Mydei accepted all of Phainon's whims, much to the shock of the onlookers. They had expected the Kremnoan man to be firmer and to refuse such tender treatment from Phainon. However, Phainon's genuine excitement made it difficult for Mydei to deny his advances.

Mydei was also particularly intrigued by the diverse cuisines found in the markets. Given that Ohkema served as the largest trading hub in Amphoreus, it was easy to encounter otherwise rare items, including a variety of herbs, fruits, and spices. Considering how well Mydei adapted to cooking in Phainon's bare kitchen, it would be amazing to see how he would fare with access to these unique ingredients.

Phainon happily set out to shop for whatever Mydei found fascinating. It was nice to observe Mydei's reactions to the various street foods available. While some people might find intense flavors strange and tend to dislike them at first taste, Mydei was different. He appreciated the food for what it offered and provided thoughtful reviews and critiques as he ate. The food stall owners were clearly captivated by him and would even offer him additional samples to taste free of charge.

This already made Phainon feel successful in his efforts to integrate Mydei with the Ohkemans. They found Mydei to be an unexpected gentleman and surprisingly popular with the elderly and children. His presence among the locals was clearly becoming accepted.

Yet Phainon couldn't help but think that his fiancé was getting far too popular. Although there was initial fear among the market locals when they saw Mydei in his armor, they quickly became enchanted by his charm. Phainon found this to be both a blessing and a curse. Perhaps he should urge the palace to expedite their marriage plans!

Even the small children trying their best to follow the two men were clearly curious about the Kremnoan man. Phainon would be the first to catch them in their hiding spot, telling them that it was rude to stalk people like that and that they might get reported if someone else had seen them first.

The kids whined and clung to Phainon, hanging off his arms and insisting they just wanted to see his fiancé. Phainon obliged, introducing them to Mydei. At first, Mydei appeared unapproachable, but his gentle smile toward the children was so bright it softened the atmosphere for everyone looking.

Mydei received various gifts and trinkets from the children, such as flowers and small wooden jewelry. This continued for the rest of the afternoon until Phainon had to usher all the gathered children to head home, as it was getting late. He wasn't used to being the voice of reason for these playful kids, but he needed to give Mydei some breathing space since they had been walking around for hours now.

Phainon was very attentive to Mydei, checking if he needed a break or if there was anything else he wanted to do. Mydei proved to be an easygoing companion throughout their time together, going along with whatever Phainon wanted to show him.

When their shopping had finally wrapped up and the afternoon sky began to darken, they decided to head back to Phainon's estate. As they walked, Phainon felt a sense of triumph, pleased that their day had gone well and that Mydei appeared to have enjoyed it too.

But soon, Phainon's expression fell when he heard Mydei's question.

"Are you always like this with your lovers?"

When Mydei noticed Phainon's unexpected panicked reaction, he quickly clarified, "I'm just asking if you always treat your lovers like this without expecting anything in return." His question arose from the fact that, throughout their time together, Phainon had never really asked him any questions—such as who he was or why he was part of the Kremnoan party as an alpha. It struck Mydei as odd that Phainon accepted him so completely, without any reservations.

Phainon never provided him with any rules or expectations typically associated with a political marriage. Usually, couples involved in such arrangements discuss their concerns with one another to ensure the contract functions smoothly.

Some political marriages, like theirs, typically involve couples discussing various aspects such as the number of children they want, the arrangement of their living space, their expected responsibilities, and how often they will spend time together. However, Phainon's treatment of Mydei suggested a dynamic more akin to that of a couple who decided to marry for love.

Mydei sensed that Phainon genuinely viewed him with love, leaving him feeling vulnerable to such emotions. It was puzzling to him that Phainon could harbor such feelings for him, and even more troubling was how much he enjoyed this level of attention and care from the other man.

While Mydei was lost in his jumbled thoughts, Phainon set down the basket he was carrying and reached out to take Mydei's hand. "I'm not sure what expectations to have of you. All I want is for you to stay by my side and experience each wonderful day with me." He spoke with that same handsome smile that made Mydei's heart flutter ever so slightly. "It is also my first time being in a relationship, so I hope I'm doing things right. If you ever do feel uncomfortable or if you think I'm doing something wrong, please tell me as soon as possible!"

Mydei couldn't believe what he was hearing. How was it possible that this man, who was the epitome of the perfect partner, was experiencing a relationship for the first time? No, the real question was: how had no one approached Phainon and asked him out?

Phainon was incredibly handsome, and he spoke with both intellect and grace. Though he could be a bit ridiculous at times, his quirkiness was far more charming and endearing than annoying. He possessed a physique that could rival many seasoned warriors on the battlefield. Even more puzzling was the fact that Phainon held a noble title. How had none of the aristocratic families made an effort to woo him with their children?

"I find it hard to believe you have never had lovers in the past," Mydei said, making an effort to avoid sounding accusatory.

"Ah, well… I'm not exactly noble by blood, but it is also because my trait has made it difficult for anyone with romantic intentions to approach me." Phainon felt a bit embarrassed discussing his secondary gender. Enigmas were almost mythical due to their rarity, so he lacked anyone to turn to for guidance on questions regarding his trait.

"How does it differ from alphas?" Mydei asked, curious if this would explain why Phainon never responded to his pheromones.

"I'm actually very sensitive to pheromones. Most of them, especially those from individuals with romantic intentions, become overwhelming and smell terrible to me. It doesn't matter whether the pheromones are from an alpha or an omega. As I grew up, I discovered that I often release a defensive scent when I feel uncomfortable with someone's advances. This has made it quite challenging to interact with others. Although I have learned to control my pheromones, I still unknowingly emit warning scents."

Mydei found this information hard to believe. He was a stranger in Phainon's life until yesterday, yet he had not detected any warning pheromones from him. Mydei was familiar with defensive pheromones, having used them himself in challenging situations.

"I have never sensed such pheromones from you, though," Mydei remarked, his tone curious.

"Really?" Phainon smiled brightly. "That's good to hear! I was worried that my pheromones were making you uncomfortable. My friends and retainers mentioned they couldn't detect any pheromones from me, except for the defensive ones. So perhaps I don't really have the normal ones that most have."

"What do you mean?" Mydei asked, growing more confused. He stepped closer to Phainon, wanting to catch a better whiff of his scent. "You smell like a sunlit forest, with hints of a cool flame, and it’s quite calming. It smells really comforting."

The scent was complex, and Mydei could only identify a few of its notes. However, it was undeniable that the scent was both inviting and perfectly suited to Phainon's personality. It reminded him of summer and spring, of the refreshing breeze that sweeps through a quiet forest. It even evoked memories of the wind rustling through a vast wheat field, a scene Mydei fondly recalled from his childhood.

Without realizing it, Phainon's face flushed a deep red—not only from Mydei's closer proximity but also from the compliment about his scent. He had always believed he lacked any positive scent, yet here was his fiancé, expressing just the opposite.

It was typically Phainon who made unexpected advances and flirtatious remarks toward Mydei. However, when he found himself on the receiving end of such attention, he was overwhelmed with shock and happiness, leaving him momentarily speechless.

To Mydei, he was simply being honest and straightforward, but this had a surprisingly effective impact on Phainon, leaving the other man momentarily stunned. Mydei looked up to see Phainon’s shy expression and wondered why he was trying to turn his face away. "Phainon?"

"That's not fair, Mydei!" Phainon complained, attempting to steady his nerves. It was surprising how Mydei hadn’t said anything particularly outrageous, yet here he was, a shy mess.

Mydei began to chuckle as he understood the situation. How could this man, who was so open about expressing his own feelings, suddenly be acting so sheepish?

"No one has ever told me something like that, so I was just surprised. I always thought something was wrong with me, which is why I tried my best to keep my pheromones under control." Phainon had been using scent blockers for as long as he could remember, ever since his first rut.

People regarded his dominant pheromones as too overwhelmingly strong, creating tension among the nobles who prided themselves on their alpha lineages. The idea that this fake noble could incapacitate even the kingdom's most skilled warriors solely through his pheromones sparked considerable outrage.

To ease the tension from getting worse, Phainon agreed to take daily supplements that functioned like scent blockers. Although these supplements couldn't completely eliminate his scent, they significantly reduced its overwhelming effect. However, no medication could control his pheromones once he entered his rut. As a result, Phainon was given his own estate to live alone, a decision made for the general safety of others.

This arrangement did not bother him, as he preferred not to have retainers and maids constantly attending to him. He found it sufficient to summon them only for important matters and events, and for the most part, he enjoyed the solitary life he was afforded.

This was the first time he had heard anyone describe his pheromones as anything other than terrifying. Could this be a result of them being a destined pair? While this notion was primarily associated with alphas and omegas, Phainon firmly believed that Mydei was meant for him.

Mydei recognized that Phainon truly possessed remarkable pheromones. It was unusual for an alpha to find comfort in the scent of another alpha, as they typically gravitated towards omegas.

Perhaps alphas had simply avoided him, which could explain why no one had ever experienced how pleasant his scent was, Mydei contemplated. It's also incredibly cute that he was shy about receiving praise of some kind.

Phainon couldn't handle the situation any longer and quickly ushered them both to return home. He was afraid that his pheromones would leak out further while they were in public, something he had been warned about in the past to avoid.

As they arrived back at the estate, Phainon happily began arranging their spoils in the kitchen. He talked about what they should be doing tomorrow, wondering if Mydei had any preferences. Perhaps a trip to the public baths? Or a tour atop the dromas?

He looked so happy while giving suggestions that Mydei found it difficult to interrupt him. It was time for Mydei to be honest with Phainon about his situation. The fact that Phainon was not a snobbish noble who only married for title made this mission more complicated for Mydei. He did not want to hurt him, but he needed to clarify things before it was too late.

A knock on the front door startled the two. They glanced out the window and noticed that it was already evening, leaving them to wonder who could possibly arrive at this hour.

Mydei offered to answer the door, but Phainon insisted on doing it himself. Ultimately, the two of them rose to answer the door together. Something felt off, and Mydei could sense it.

When Phainon opened the door, knights attempted to rush inside to seize the man behind him. Phainon reacted quickly, blocking their entry into his home while ensuring that Mydei remained safe. "What is the meaning of this?"

"Your Highness, please step aside. We are here on orders from Her Majesty," one of the knights stated, holding up a scroll that detailed the instructions for apprehending his fiancé.

"If Her Majesty wishes to speak with us, we will do so in the morning." Phainon remained steadfast, releasing pheromones that served as a warning for the knights to keep their distance.

Mydei already understood the situation. The imperator had probably discovered his true identity. He was not merely a noble son from Castrum Kremnos; he was far more notorious than that. However, he hadn’t expected this revelation to happen so soon. He wished he had been granted more time… time to speak with Phainon and clarify everything.

"Phainon." A voice emerged from behind the knights, familiar and trusted by Phainon. Yet this time, the tone was urgent and carried a clear intent.

Aglaea stepped forward as the knights moved away from the suffocating pheromones. She was a dominant alpha herself and had already grown accustomed to Phainon's scent, enough to approach with a confident stride.

"Aglaea, what is going on?" he asked, remaining on guard, knowing she was not here to take his side—not this time.

"The man behind you is not who you think he is. He must be taken into custody immediately for the safety of Ohkema until we are completely certain he does not have plans against us," she explained.

"Like I said, we will go to the palace ourselves once it is morning." Phainon remained resolute, even as Mydei attempted to restrain him, saying that he was willing to accompany them. It was the least Mydei could do, considering he had come here under false pretenses, deceiving Phainon.

But Phainon was refusing to back down, resulting in a standstill where neither party could move forward. Aglaea let out a sigh and started to clarify the situation. "Are you aware of who the man behind you is and the reason for his arrest?"

"He is Mydeimos, a Kremnoan noble and my fiancé," Phainon stated confidently. Before Aglaea could counter his claim, he continued, "If there's more to discuss, I will let Mydei speak for himself. Otherwise, I will see you all tomorrow."

Before tensions escalated further, Aglaea accepted the situation and ordered the knights to retreat for the night. Despite vocal complaints regarding her decision, she instead commanded that the perimeter be well-guarded until tomorrow, when they would be escorted to the palace.

Phainon closed the door, locking it securely, and turned to face Mydei, who averted his gaze in shame. Despite this, Phainon took Mydei's hands and pressed a tender kiss upon them. "Are you alright?"

Mydei was astonished by what he heard. Despite the circumstances, Phainon continued to look at him with eyes brimming with trust and admiration. After everything that had transpired, this was the first question he asked Mydei.

"When you are ready to talk, I will listen," Phainon said with a reassuring smile. Mydei felt his heart sink at the thought of what he needed to share next.

Chapter End Notes

Thank you so much for all the thoughts and prayers. I have safely arrived home!

All the suggestions for Phainon’s pheromones were also really good that I couldn’t choose one and just meshed them all together until something made sense. I’m not the best at describing scents, but I hope the picture it paints is enough.

For those wondering about the signet ring, don’t worry! I haven’t forgotten about it, and it will be used later on. Phainon can’t exactly focus on anything except his beautiful wife right now.

chapters.title: Chapter 8: Please Stay
chapters.html:
Phainon understood that Mydei had much on his mind. He didn't want to rush him into providing an explanation. Instead, he suggested that Mydei take a warm bath and wait for him in the bedroom, where their conversation would be more private. Given that there would be guards patrolling Phainon's estate, it was best for them to talk in that secluded space.

Mydei obliged, grateful that Phainon remained considerate of him despite the earlier scene. He knew it would be challenging to explain everything to Phainon. After all, he was a Kremnoan who had been at war with them for decades. It would be thoughtless for him to believe that Phainon would still trust him.

As he rested and took time to gather his thoughts, Phainon returned to the kitchen to prepare a light meal for both of them. Phainon also needed a moment to clear his mind and brace himself for what lay ahead.

He sounded confident and straightforward with Aglaea earlier, as if he already understood the situation. In reality, the words he spoke were all he knew. Mydei was a noble from Castrum Kremnos, and he was his fiancé. Whatever else Mydei might be hiding couldn't be that serious, right? The worst-case scenario would be that Mydei wasn't of noble birth at all, but Phainon had no problem with that. Perhaps it was more of a concern for the rest of Ohkema.

The peace agreement relied on the marriage of two nobles from opposing kingdoms, meaning that if Mydei were not truly of noble birth, the entire contract would be nullified. But how could that possibly be the case? Mydei was stunning and exuded an undeniable aura of royalty. If Mydei claimed to be the king, Phainon would have no doubt in believing him.

Though that presents a problem on its own, Phainon can't exactly marry the king, can he? He was merely a noble by title, and deep down, Phainon knew he could never compare to Mydei if that were the case.

Perhaps Mydei was secretly a spy sent to Ohkema, which would explain the urgency that prompted Aglaea to arrive unannounced in the middle of the night. But could that truly be possible? Mydei wouldn't do such deception, and he knew it in his heart.

Phainon sighed, attempting to refocus on the porridge he was preparing. He knew a lengthy conversation with Mydei awaited him once he finished, so he shouldn't waste time worrying. The only way to truly understand the situation was to speak with his fiancé.

Meanwhile, Mydei was fighting with his own internal struggles as he contemplated how to explain everything to Phainon. No matter how he tried to frame his thoughts, the outcome remained the same. It was going to hurt Phainon, and Mydei couldn't bear the thought of seeing the man look betrayed. But it would be even more unfair to him if he did not give Phainon the full, honest truth.

He believed only a few minutes had passed, but it had already been an hour since they last spoke. It stunned him a bit when he heard Phainon's steps approaching the bedroom. Phainon knocked gently on the door before entering. He wheeled in a small cart that carried their dinner and a few drinks.

Mydei realized he needed that drink, so without hesitation, he poured himself a full glass of wine and downed it in one gulp. Phainon attempted to intervene but was too taken aback by Mydei's actions.

That wouldn't be enough to get Mydei drunk, but it did provide him with a bit of courage to speak. Phainon guided them both to sit on the couch south of the bed, as if he were gently steering a tipsy lover. Mydei couldn't help but feel a sense of shame for having indulged in relaxation over the past two days, allowing himself to be pampered like this.

"Phainon." Mydei began, his voice serious and laden with regret. However, before he could continue, Phainon quickly downed his own glassful of wine. "HKS. You need to be sober and listen to me." Mydei attempted to wrestle the cup away from Phainon, but instead, Phainon was already pouring himself another drink.

There was a struggle as both of them tried to take the cup away from each other, with Phainon remaining uncharacteristically quiet throughout. Was this man already drunk? Mydei couldn't help but sigh under his breath. In the end, the wine spilled on both of them, and the initial shock left them speechless, soaked from their torsos down.

After a brief silence, the two began to laugh in unison at their ridiculous state. This was supposed to be a serious moment and conversation, yet here they were, playing with a bottle of wine and spilling it everywhere. Fortunately, it didn’t get on the couch or carpet, so Phainon simply took off his soaked outer coat and used a towel from the tray to pat them dry.

"I'm sorry… I might have to take you back to the baths later because of this." Phainon's expression quickly shifted to one of sadness and guilt, once again dampening the mood around them.

"It's alright. Let's eat this porridge before it gets cold." Mydei grabbed the towel and playfully wiped the frown off Phainon's face. Phainon chuckled lightly and brought the tray closer so they could enjoy their meal.

The expectations for the meal were low, given Phainon's last mishap in the kitchen. However, Mydei was pleasantly surprised to discover that the porridge was tasty. While it was plain, its flavor was delicious and perfect for a cozy night. He had been half convinced that Phainon was a poor cook, but it was nice to be proven wrong this time.

Phainon appeared very shy again when Mydei complimented his cooking, downplaying it as something simple since it was just porridge. However, Mydei left no room for Phainon to be shy about his cooking, as he eagerly finished the entire plate without leaving a trace this time.

They sat for a few moments in awkward silence while Phainon refilled their cups. This time, they didn’t gulp it down all at once, but they were definitely consuming the wine more quickly than they should have.

"Mydei?" Phainon broke the silence first, setting down his glass on the table.

Mydei looked up at him. "Hmm?"

"Before you explain what's happening, can I ask you something first? Actually, can you promise me something instead before we go any further? Phainon stuttered slightly as he spoke, worried that his request might come across as irrational.

"It depends on what you want me to promise. But if it's something I'm able to do, then I will." Mydei nodded, his tone sincere. It was the least he could do after all.

Phainon pondered for a moment, trying to decide what he wanted to confirm with Mydei first. What was he supposed to say? He didn’t even know what Mydei was going to say yet. Still, he couldn't shake the anxiousness stirring in his heart. The outcome of their marriage could heavily depend on what was about to unfold next.

"Can you promise me that, no matter what, you will still stay with me?" Phainon realized he sounded selfish. He understood he was placing a heavy burden on Mydei by making such a request, making him no better than the Ohkeman nobles who had trapped him in this marriage in the first place.

Despite Phainon's genuine love for Mydei, he actually did recognize that their union was primarily a marriage of convenience. This reality meant that Mydei was essentially forced to participate in it. Even if Mydei had the chance to decline the proposal, the notion of choice was merely an illusion. Ultimately, whoever Phainon selected that day would be bound to him, regardless of their personal feelings.

But Phainon believed deep in his heart that they were fated for each other, and he knew that Mydei felt the same. Even if they had barely met, the way their pheromones complement each other would make anyone looking believe they had shared a deep connection for years.

If it had been anyone else, Phainon would not have reacted as he did when he first laid eyes on Mydei that day. In that moment, he lost all sense of reason and ended up looking quite foolish. However, he had no regrets after successfully persuading Mydei to agree. If he had been more silly, he would have carried Mydei in his arms and paraded him around Ohkema. But of course, he knew he would have gotten scolded by not only Mydei but also by the elders if he did. So he chose to imagine their wedding day instead, where he could freely carry Mydei in his arms without fear of reprimand.

But after the events that unfolded earlier that evening, Phainon began to feel anxious. It wasn't that he doubted the genuineness of their feelings for each other, but rather that the world might not permit them to be together.

He couldn't shake the feeling that Mydei might leave again. He recognized it was unfair to think that the younger Mydeimos from all those years ago had left him intentionally, but what can a man who has been abandoned by everyone he had ever loved truly believe?

Please. He just needed to hear him promise to stay.

He wanted Mydei to respond firmly and immediately with a promise that he would stay, but why was Mydei silent now? Why was he refusing to look Phainon in the eye?

Phainon could feel a ringing in his ears. Maybe it was the strong alcohol he had just consumed, or perhaps it was due to the fatigue from their long strolls throughout the day. No. It was because he already knew the answer to the question.

"Phainon, please listen to me first." Mydei tried to reason with him, but it was too late, as tears were already streaming down Phainon's face. This time, it was Mydei who held Phainon's hands as the other man attempted to turn away and cover his face.

"I am the crown prince of Castrum Kremnos," Mydei sighed, beginning his explanation. He could sense Phainon freeze at those words, and Mydei braced himself for the worst.

"I'm sure you've heard tales about the Kremnoan royal family and the tradition that heirs must first defeat the reigning monarchs to claim the throne. And of course that includes the stories about how the sole crown prince of the kingdom was exiled in order to prove their strength. I've returned to reclaim what's rightfully mine. But the current king has gone mad, refusing to relinquish his throne even if it means murdering all of his direct heirs."

He could tell Phainon was listening intently, gripping tighter at the hands that held him. So he continued, "Since there are still laws that disallow thoughtless murder, particularly for heirs who have not yet come of age, the quickest way to eliminate me was to exile me without any training or support. I've spent my life being pursued by mercenaries and assassins, honing my skills and learning to fight on my own, and this is where I stand now."

He began to explain how King Eurypon had killed everyone who opposed him, including his own wife and Mydei's mother. The mad king was so blinded by his power that the kingdom was now in shambles and on the brink of collapse. When Mydei had arrived that day, he couldn't believe that his father had willingly accepted a peace treaty. There had to be a catch, and Mydei couldn't help but worry for the unfortunate Kremnoan nobles who were about to be offered up as sacrifices.

There was no longer any room for Castrum Kremnos to make mistakes that could lead to their ultimate demise, so he needed to take action. He had to determine whether this exchange was legitimate or if Eurypon intended to use underhanded tactics against the Ohkemans. If there was a way for him to turn the tide and ensure Eurypon's downfall, he would do whatever it took. However, he did not expect this to come at the cost of deceiving Phainon in this manner.

For the brief time they spent together, Mydei could no longer deny his feelings for the man. However, he understood that his responsibilities had to take precedence.

He just wished they could have had more time together.

"I can help you," Phainon said, surprising Mydei, who had anticipated Phainon's rejection and an immediate call for knights to come and arrest him. "The peace agreement was always on shaky ground, even with the council of elders and the Imperator. It felt like a deal too good to be true, so Her Majesty was already wary of potential complications."

Phainon took Mydei's right hand and placed it over his heart, as if pledging his loyalty. "If your desire is to reclaim your birthright and restore glory to your kingdom, then I will do everything within my power to assist you."

"Why…" Mydei struggled to find the right words, looking up at Phainon in confusion. "Why do you trust me so easily? I am a stranger in this kingdom and a liar who has deceived you."

"Because you are my fated pair." Phainon chuckled softly, lifting the hand he held to his lips to kiss it.

Mydei couldn't respond to that. He knew it was true, but there was still guilt left in his heart. How could fate be so cruel to them?

"We shall meet with Her Majesty tomorrow, and I will be there with you the entire time to explain the situation. There may be some requirements, such as offering your thoughts to be read by the golden threads, but as long as you answer truthfully, everything will be alright." Phainon felt nervous about tomorrow, but his heart was a little lighter after discovering the truth.

Depending on the length of their conversation at the Dawncloud tomorrow, Mydei might leave Ohkema sooner than expected. Tonight might very well be their final opportunity to be together. This realization pierced Phainon's heart, leaving him feeling helpless to change what was to come. But he knew this was important to Mydei, and he couldn't simply dismiss it for his own desires.

And yet a part of him still wished to be a little selfish.

"Mydei… At least for the time before you leave, can I still treat you like my fiancé? Can we please pretend this is real, just for a moment longer?"

Despite the smile on Phainon's face, the tears were ready to spill. Even if he understood that their marriage was a lie and that it would never come true, he could still cherish these memories of Mydei, where he could pretend that even for a short time they were destined for each other.

Chapter End Notes

chapters.html:
Perhaps it was the alcohol taking effect, or maybe it was when Mydei noticed the change in Phainon's expression. One thing was certain: Mydei could no longer be patient. If this man was not going to act, then he would.

He reached out for Phainon, grabbing him by the collar of his inner shirt and pulling him closer. Before Phainon could react, he pressed their lips together.

Phainon was initially too shocked to react, his eyes wide as he processed what was happening. But soon, he reached out for Mydei, placing a gentle hand on the back of his head and reciprocating the kiss.

The kiss began with awkward and tentative pecks on each other's lips. Neither Mydei nor Phainon had ever kissed anyone before, so they both felt a bit shy. However, as their instincts took over, Mydei playfully opened his mouth and licked at Phainon's lips.

This action made Phainon shiver, and Mydei could feel the man's pheromones enveloping him. The sensation was intense and almost greedy, as if Phainon's scent was wrapping around Mydei. For most alphas, such behavior would be deemed unacceptable and incredibly disrespectful towards other alphas, but Mydei found himself enjoying the feeling.

The kiss deepened, albeit slowly. Phainon allowed Mydei's tongue to enter, struggling to control his breath while keeping their lips together. Mydei's tongue brushed against his teeth, creating a ticklish and sensitive sensation. Phainon had never experienced kissing like this before. It was strange, yet his body felt ignited with heat. Soon, he moved his own tongue to meet Mydei's, and the kiss grew more passionate.

Phainon could also sense Mydei's pheromones pushing back against him, striving to prevent his full submission. The excitement of this challenge thrilled him, prompting Phainon to consciously release more of his pheromones this time.

At some point, neither of them knew where to place their hands, but Phainon seized the moment to reach around Mydei's back. His hands glided smoothly over Mydei's bare skin, tracing the contours of his muscles. Mydei's breathing became more erratic, but he was determined not to back down as he began to run his fingers through Phainon's hair.

Mydei's gentle touches to his hair left Phainon feeling particularly sensitive, causing him to exhale softly. Phainon's hand continued to glide over Mydei's back as he began to trace his fingers down Mydei's spine.

When Phainon reached a specific point on Mydei's back, he felt Mydei flinch in his arms and heard him let out a soft moan. Both men were taken aback by the unexpected sound, and Mydei hesitated, contemplating pulling away to explain. However, this reaction stirred something within Phainon, prompting him to draw Mydei's body even closer, gently gliding his fingers along Mydei's spine once more.

Their faces remained close to each other, lips left wanting more. Phainon took this chance to stare at Mydei's reactions as he continued to explore Mydei's back.

Mydei's face and upper torso flushed bright red with embarrassment as more unfamiliar sounds escaped his lips. He was unsure of what was happening, but the spot where Phainon was caressing felt so pleasurable that he couldn't help but react to it.

Phainon was clearly enjoying the reactions he elicited from Mydei, but Mydei was beginning to reach his limit. He tightened his grip on Phainon's hair and pulled him back.

"HKS!" Mydei exclaimed in frustration, though his tone conveyed more embarrassment than genuine anger. Their lips glistened from the passionate kisses they had shared, and Mydei could see that Phainon was blushing deeply as well.

Surprisingly, Phainon reached for Mydei again, pulling him into a tight hug. He ceased his attempts to caress Mydei's back but held onto him firmly, and Mydei could feel Phainon's body shaking slightly.

To say that Phainon was overwhelmed was an understatement. Earlier, he had fully expected Mydei to decline his wish. No, Phainon would have preferred it if Mydei had just outright rejected him then and there. It would have helped him ease into reality more smoothly. But what was happening now? Why had Mydei kissed him? Was it okay for him to hold onto this moment and let hope continue to fester inside him?

He began to quietly sob while holding onto Mydei, fearing that the other might try to pull away again. There was no way he would let his pathetic crying be seen again, so he rested his chin on Mydei's shoulder, trying to shield his tear-streaked face from view. With the hope Mydei had given him, he wanted to cling to this moment a little while longer.

Mydei hugged Phainon back, despite their awkward position on the couch. Had he pulled Phainon's hair too hard? A wave of guilt washed over him, prompting him to gently caress Phainon's hair again while his other hand offered comforting pats on his back.

Now that the heat of the moment had subsided, Mydei found himself struggling to respond to Phainon's earlier question. Was it truly acceptable for them to maintain this pretense of being fiancés? When they face the Imperator tomorrow, would anyone genuinely believe they had any sort of relationship that resembled that?

The saturation of their pheromones had calmed down, but if anyone were to see their current state, one might assume they had spent a very intense night together.

Mydei knew it was his fault for initiating the kiss earlier, but what other choice did he have? He was also far too lost in the moment to deny that he wanted to stay with Phainon too. There was no way he could ever turn away from the other so coldly.

Both of them desired one another. In an ideal world, they would be destined partners united by fate, a romantic tale to be recounted for generations. Yet their reality was unforgiving.

Mydei remained a crown prince of a foreign nation, burdened with the responsibility of restoring peace to his homeland. He would have to abide by the laws of their land, and it was uncertain how long it would take to undo the destruction done by his father.

He could not afford to lose sight of his duty now, even if it meant leaving behind his destined love.

Given the political dynamics between the two kingdoms and their treaty, it was clear that Mydei lacked authority over Ohkema. Even the idea of asking Phainon to accompany him was clearly out of the question. Furthermore, Mydei was reluctant to expose Phainon to the dangers he would encounter upon returning to Castrum Kremnos.

How could Mydei possibly ask this young noble, whose eyes sparkled with so much light, to join him in a war for which he held no certainty of victory?

He knew he should respond to Phainon and ask that their relationship come to an end tonight. For the first time in his life, Mydei is acknowledging his own cowardice, as he refuses to conclude things here. Even if he returned to Castrum Kremnos, he still wanted to keep Phainon's heart.

Should he face the possibility that they would never see each other again, he would still cling to the belief that he has a fiancé waiting for him in a distant land.

Mydei soon noticed that Phainon's weight on his body felt a bit heavier. He gently tapped Phainon's back, only to realize that the other man had fallen asleep after crying by himself.

He wasn't even annoyed but rather surprised. Instead, he let out a soft laugh at the absurdity of the situation. Although Phainon was taller and heavier than him, he was still a Kremnoan prince for a reason. He easily lifted Phainon and carried him to the bed, being careful not to wake him.

"Good night, Phainon." He tucked him into bed, gently caressing his cheeks that were still slightly damp from tears.

Mydei climbed onto the other side of the bed and tried his best to fall asleep. However, he knew he wouldn't be sleeping any time soon, as he was troubled by thoughts of how he would face the Imperator tomorrow and somehow secure their support.

He debated getting up to work elsewhere so as not to wake Phainon, but given how Phainon had reacted to his disappearance that morning, he decided against it. But also the sight of Phainon's sleeping face was simply too comforting to leave. Perhaps getting a good night's sleep would be more beneficial for him after all.

It didn't take long for Mydei to fall asleep as well. As the night deepened, the quiet sounds of the world outside faded, and the heated pheromones from earlier had already softened. Whatever challenges awaited them in the morning, he was certain Phainon would be there with him.

The following morning was tense, but both were prepared for it. As soon as the sun broke over the horizon, the anticipated knock on the door echoed through the manor. The knights had arrived to escort them to the Dawncloud. Prior to this, they had managed to grab a quick meal, and Phainon had briefed Mydei on what to expect when they faced the Imperator.

Despite the knights' obvious attempts to separate them, Phainon was determined to walk side by side with Mydei. He was still a member of the royal family, and he could not be physically detained by the knights without explicit orders.

However, this defiance was short-lived, as Phainon was ultimately compelled to stand off to the side while Mydei faced the Imperator's throne alone. But just knowing that Phainon was still there with him was enough to calm Mydei's nerves.

On their way here, they mostly remained silent, but Mydei used that time to strategize what he intended to say. There was truly no way around it, and only the truth of the situation would work to his favor. So when the question finally arose, he felt prepared.

"Mydeimos, crown prince of Castrum Kremnos." Cerydra's voice echoed from behind the curtained throne, elevated several steps above the rest of the audience. "What brings you here to Ohkema?"

Before Mydei could respond, a golden glint shot toward him at high speeds. Had Phainon not warned him in advance, Mydei would have instinctively dodged or even retaliated. However, he was not here as an enemy but as an ally seeking aid.

The golden threads coiled tightly around Mydei's arms, restraining him in place. His extremely calm demeanor astonished many of the onlookers, who exchanged whispers among themselves. Mydei maintained his expression, allowing the threads to assert their control over him without resistance.

Even Aglaea, who manipulated these threads, had to recognize how composed Mydei remained in this situation. Not a trace of fear or guilt could be sensed through the threads.

As Mydei began to speak, the audience fell silent, some even holding their breaths. After all, the words he was about to utter would be considered treasonous anywhere else. However, the fact that the threads showed no signs of shaking made his claims all the more shocking.

"I'm here to seek Ohkema's aid in preventing my father from completely destroying my homeland. His madness has resulted in too much unjust bloodshed, and it is costing us everything." Mydei spoke with conviction, his gaze fixed on the curtained throne as if he were looking directly into the Imperator's eyes.

He continued to explain the situation in the Kremnoan kingdom and how the common people were suffering as a result. He also pointed out that, although their nations had never been allies, the amount of bloodshed had not reached such levels until a couple of decades ago, when Eurypon began to show signs of madness.

Mydei recounted how he was banished as a child, how many direct lineage royal family members were killed in mysterious circumstances, and how Queen Gorgo, his mother, was also slaughtered unjustly. He spoke about the council of advisors who are slowly poisoning the royal court and that there was no more saving his father.

There was truly only one way for Mydei to claim the throne, and it was the path Eurypon most dreaded. Only through his death could Mydei restore peace to Castrum Kremnos.

The reality he faced was grim and burdened him with responsibilities that could further devastate an already crumbling nation. What made it all the more regretful was the fact that Mydei never had the desire to become king or uphold the traditions of Castrum Kremnos. However, he knew more than anyone that the responsibility of safeguarding this nation rested solely on his shoulders.

Through the years, as he faced daily challenges that threatened his life and trained both his body and mind for the long war ahead, no one else was more suited to take on this role than him. Even Eurypon was no fool to believe that his son was not a force to be reckoned with, which was why he probably thought it would prolong the inevitable by sending his son away so he could plan their next cause for banishment.

But Mydei was no longer the helpless child who had yearned for his mother's care and craved his father's approval. The determination in his eyes was reminiscent of those destined to become gods among men in history.

The elders and nobles who listened to Mydei were taken aback. They had arrived expecting to execute a spy who intended to ambush Ohkema, but instead, they confronted a stark reality about the nation they believed they were allied with. Yet, the golden threads never lie.

"But the peace agreement between Ohkema and Castrum Kremnos will remain. I fully intend to uphold it after I succeed in my plans. If you find my explanation insufficient, I am prepared to provide more." Mydei finally concluded his speech and awaited their judgment.

A few whispers could be heard around the court, but no matter the opinion of others, it was the Imperator who held the authority.

Aglaea and Hysilens could be seen ascending the steps to confer privately with the Imperator, with the former confirming that the threads show no signs of deceit from the Kremnoan prince.

"Very well, young prince." Cerydra's voice resonated from behind the curtain, carrying an air of approval. "Your eloquence speaks volumes, and I have no reason to doubt the threads that bind you."

While Mydei spoke earlier, one of the oracles, Trinnon, was behind the curtain with Cerydra, already drafting a new contract. However, there was one section they could not finalize.

"But tell me, Mydeimos, what will happen should you fail to slay your father and liberate your nation?"

The question resonated throughout the court, silencing all whispers in an instant. Even Phainon struggled to comprehend the question. How could Mydei possibly fail?

"Should I fail, I will rise again from the Sea of Souls and face the mad king once more. Until the Lance of Fury falls and the flames of Castrum Kremnos are extinguished, I will keep on returning."

Chapter End Notes
