chapters.title: Chapter 10: Goodbye
chapters.html:
Chapter Notes

I was sick for most of last week, so I only got to finishing this chapter today. But I made sure to make it a bit longer than usual!

The audience with the Imperator passed more quickly than expected. Mydei received official support, but the contract will only take effect once he successfully claims the throne of Castrum Kremnos.

In less than a day, Mydei was expected to depart from Ohkema. There was no point in delaying the inevitable, and the Imperator was insistent on finalizing the peace agreement as quickly as possible. Since no bride would remain in Ohkema, the treaty was deemed void. However, if Mydei succeeded in his mission, Cerydra was prepared to overlook this issue.

This also posed a greater challenge for Mydei, given that the responsibility for lasting peace between the two nations now rested on his shoulders.

But Mydei had been prepared for a long time. He would not have even stepped foot in Castrum Kremnos again if he were not. Yet this time, something else occupied Mydei's thoughts.

There was still a sense of guilt in his heart for refusing to end things with Phainon. He realized that even if they never discussed it again, his departure from Ohkema meant they would return to being strangers.

Phainon remained silent throughout the walk back to his estate. They were once again accompanied by knights, but this time it felt more lenient, as Mydei had been granted temporary asylum by the Imperator.

The silence troubled Mydei, and he found himself at a loss for words to break it. Should he pat Phainon on the back and express his gratitude for the support? Or perhaps offer some consolation since they were soon to part ways?

Why was he even still acting so awkward, as if they hadn’t willingly exchanged kisses the night before?

The thought caused a faint blush to rise on Mydei's cheeks, prompting him to quickly dismiss the embarrassing memories of the previous night.

When the knights finally took their leave and the two men were alone again, they stood a few feet apart, awkwardly fidgeting, unsure of what to do or say to each other. Both men tried to speak simultaneously, quickly apologizing to allow the other to go first.

The awkwardness didn't linger for long, as they quickly laughed it off. Mydei broke the silence first, saying, "Thank you, Phainon… for everything."

Phainon inched closer, and he flashed a big smile at Mydei. "This calls for a celebration! Let's head back to the market, and I'll treat you to the best restaurant there. At the very least, you'll get to experience authentic local Ohkeman food that isn't burnt to a crisp like mine."

"Hmm, I don't know. I think the slightly burnt aftertaste has been my favorite so far," Mydei joked. Phainon looked like he was about to complain, but Mydei stepped even closer and reached out to hold Phainon's hand.

This was a rare moment when Mydei took the initiative to make contact, and Phainon felt overwhelmed with emotion. Both of them were aware that this would be their final day together, and they wanted to create a lasting memory.

They wasted no time, heading out again and racing toward the Mamoreal Market for a delicious lunch together. Although this particular restaurant usually required reservations, Phainon rarely used his status to skip such formalities. Given Phainon's popularity and the locals' newfound love for Mydei, they were swiftly escorted to the finest table on a private terrace.

The whole meal would have been on the house had Phainon not insisted on paying, feeling awful already for skipping through the waitlist.

Mydei had never experienced such luxury in a meal, especially one with multiple courses. Each dish arrived fresh and warm, offering a variety of flavors that Phainon typically wouldn’t choose for himself. However, he knew how much Mydei enjoyed trying new things, making it worthwhile to see the delight on Mydei's face. The wine was exceptional as well, boasting a sweet flavor that he was certain Mydei would appreciate.

The restaurant servers and chefs were thrilled to see two very hearty eaters, especially one who offered remarkable praise for the cooking. Despite Mydei and Phainon already feeling quite full, the staff insisted on packing some complimentary desserts to take home.

The waiter cheerfully explained to Mydei that the complimentary dessert was a selection box of chocolate treats, which he highly recommended enjoying at night before they went to bed. Mydei thought it was unusual to eat such treats before bedtime, but he expressed his gratitude to the servers anyway.

After lunch, they decided to take a pleasant walk around the other areas of central Ohkema that they hadn’t been able to explore yesterday. Phainon served as an excellent guide, enthusiastically sharing information about everything they passed and even offering some interesting little facts along the way. Mydei wasn’t much of a talker and usually disliked listening to idle chatter, but perhaps he had a change of heart, as he found Phainon’s musings surprisingly enjoyable.

Mydei was never one to take the time to enjoy the scenery, but this time he absorbed everything around him. The views of Ohkema were stunning, especially with Phainon's smiling face at the center of it all.

"Oh! I want to show you my favorite spot in Ohkema," Phainon said happily as their walk brought them back to the Mamoreal Market. He led Mydei through a series of staircases and somewhat precarious cloth bridges until they reached a seemingly private rooftop view, perfect for spending an afternoon in peace. While they were hidden from view from the crowds, the sounds of the busy streets below were comforting.

"When I first arrived in Ohkema, I wasn't very… cooperative with the nobles. The caretakers would often try to drag me into these classes about poise and manners or something, so I would end up trying to hide. They kept finding me, so I had to come up with better hiding spots," Phainon explained, gazing at the bright horizon, the golden sunlight perfectly illuminating his features. "Eventually, I discovered this place, and nobody has ever managed to find it."

Mydei wanted to say that he would now know where to find Phainon in the future, but he held his tongue. There was no point in fostering such false hopes. The last thing he wanted was to make Phainon believe that he could wait for him, and that would be too unfair.

So all he could do was listen and gaze at the beautiful memory he was carving in his mind.

It was starting to get late as the sun dipped closer to the horizon. How could time move so quickly today? It felt like they had just arrived a moment ago.

Music floated up from below, drawing the attention of the two, who leaned over to see what was happening. A street band was playing at the corner, urging the surrounding crowd to pause for a moment and enjoy the songs.

At some point, some of the onlookers began taking their partners and inviting them to dance to the slow music. Many others quickly followed suit, and soon the crowd was in pairs or groups, swaying to the rhythm. Even little kids gathered together, swaying along with the enchanting music.

Mydei couldn't help but reflect on how different Ohkema was from his home. The relaxed and laid-back lifestyle of the Ohkeman people felt foreign to him, yet he found himself appreciating it more and more. Something like this would never happen in Castrum Kremnos.

He hadn’t noticed that the man beside him had stood up until he saw Phainon extending his hand toward him. Mydei took the hand that helped him rise from his seat and was quickly drawn closer to Phainon’s body. It felt only right for them to share a moment of dance.

Mydei felt awkward with the slow, swaying movements, but Phainon held his waist and hand securely, guiding him as he adjusted to the rhythm. However, Phainon was also not particularly skilled at dancing and occasionally missed the beat, which resulted in amused chuckles from Mydei, who noticed his missteps.

The sun was setting, and the stars over Ohkema were now visible above them. The serene darkness and beautiful music created a picturesque scene, and both men almost thought it was a shame that the performance was ending.

Even as the music came to a close and the crowd below began to disperse, the two men remained swaying closely together on their secluded little rooftop. Mydei found himself resting his cheek against Phainon's shoulder, unconsciously taking in Phainon's scent.

In turn, Phainon leaned closer, resting his face over Mydei's hair. They both closed their eyes, finding comfort in each other's warmth.

It was unclear who moved first, but they turned to look at each other before sharing a gentle kiss. In that moment, there were no tears and no negative thoughts—just the desire to close the distance between them, savoring the intimacy of this moment.

Phainon's gentle hand caressed Mydei's cheek after they pulled apart. "Let's go home."

The walk back was quiet yet comforting, and they held hands the entire time, leaning closer to one another.

When they arrived back at the manor, Phainon shyly suggested that Mydei go ahead to the baths while he prepared their dinner. He still felt too embarrassed to bathe with Mydei again after what had happened last time. However, he was taken aback when Mydei tightened his grip on Phainon's hand, refusing to let go.

"Are we not going in together?" Mydei asked, his eyes averted, a faint blush coloring his cheeks.

Whatever weak resistance Phainon was trying to muster crumbled instantly at that moment. He scooped Mydei into his arms and hurriedly carried them both into the bath. Their clothes were discarded in a flash, and Phainon held Mydei close, determined not to let him slip away this time.

Mydei felt a wave of embarrassment at how effortlessly Phainon lifted him. How could this man be so strong when he looked like he had never seen a day of battle in his life?

As they descended into the water, Mydei settled over Phainon's lap as they faced each other. Without exchanging any words, the two eagerly resumed their passionate kisses, pressing their bodies against each other. There was only one thought occupying their minds: it was their last night together as fiancés, as lovers.

It didn't take long for Mydei to feel something stiff pressing against his stomach, prompting his hand to slide down to meet the expected intruder. Phainon flinched slightly at the touch, breaking their kiss as he attempted to gently remove Mydei's hand.

"What's the matter?" Mydei asked playfully, his hand teasingly caressing Phainon up and down. Phainon's face flushed bright red as he stammered an apology, but Mydei silenced him with another deep kiss.

The warm flesh that Mydei teased was as incredible as what he remembered, making it embarrassingly difficult for him to fully grasp it around his hand. He, too, was sporting an excited intruder, but Phainon's flustered expression was simply too amusing to focus on anything else.

He could feel the veins running along the shaft as his thumb glided over it, causing Phainon to shudder at the delicate touches. Mydei continued the kiss, gently pulling at Phainon's lower lip until he was able to slide his tongue into Phainon's mouth once more.

Mydei sensed the intensifying pheromones that Phainon emitted, feeling his control slip away with each teasing touch. However, Phainon was remarkably skilled at restraining himself, leaving Mydei to escalate the situation on his own.

His hand tightened slightly at the base of Phainon's shaft, moving slowly upward until his thumb brushed against the tip. He felt the body beneath him shudder, and suddenly, a hand moved to Mydei's back.

The action itself didn't initially bother Mydei until he felt Phainon's warm hand press against a specific spot in the center of his back. His eyes widened as he pulled away from the kiss, releasing a startled moan.

"You!" Mydei exclaimed, quickly responding by intensifying the movement of his hand. Phainon gasped, moaning Mydei's name as he instinctively curled over, attempting to create some distance between them. However, Mydei maintained his straddled position, effectively pinning Phainon against the wall of the pool.

It was only when Mydei felt Phainon's entire body shake in pleasure that he experienced a sense of triumph, but that smug expression faded quickly as Phainon's hand found its way to his own erection.

Phainon's hand was relentless and forceful, expertly guiding Mydei toward climax. Yet, just as Mydei approached the peak of pleasure, Phainon would always pause, sensing the moment he was about to reach his limit. Mydei gripped tightly on Phainon's shoulder, groaning in frustration.

Mydei looked up at Phainon, trying to interpret the other man's expression, which was difficult to read. How is this man able to hold back so much? The level of control Phainon exhibited was quite unusual for many alphas, but Mydei realized this is probably what set him apart from the rest.

But this was good for them, Mydei thought. They shouldn't get too carried away and do things that they would end up regretting. This much is enough.

Before he could wallow in guilt once more, he reached out to cup Phainon's cheeks and pulled him into another intense kiss. Phainon finally ceased his teasing, allowing Mydei to release into his hand, quickly drawing him closer until there was no space left between their bodies.

This was enough.

The two continued being glued to each other throughout the night. Although they didn't go any further than they did, they were both in silent understanding that this was their limit.

Neither of them escalated the heat of the moment. Instead, they took the opportunity to breathe in each other's scent as deeply as possible. How long would it be before they forgot the way the other smelled? A few months? Perhaps a few years?

There was no point in making promises about the future that they couldn't be sure of. For Mydei, promising to Phainon that he would one day return to Ohkema felt too cruel. The moment he ascends to the throne, he will face a long period of rebuilding for his nation. There is no chance for their king to pursue someone he could not bring back to Castrum Kremnos.

He understood all too well that if he made such a promise, Phainon would be willing to wait for him, no matter how long it took. Even if it meant waiting until their own deaths. Phainon deserved a better life than that. He still had the opportunity to marry and start the big family he desired, which Mydei could never guarantee.

For Phainon, he wanted to go with Mydei and fight alongside him. If Mydei were to ask that of him right now, he would pack up everything and leave without a moment's notice.

But he knew Mydei would never permit that. This was not Phainon's battle, and taking an Ohkeman royal family member to war like that would only create a rift between their nations. The repercussions of such an action would be endless. Still, Phainon didn't care, and he wished Mydei would ask for him.

And yet none of these worries surfaced between the two throughout the night. They quietly remained wrapped in each other’s arms in the darkness. And how they wished the next day would never come.

But fairytales always had their endings.

The sun began to rise over the horizon, casting gentle beams of light through the bedroom window. The change of seasons was approaching, as a chilly breeze wafted through the gap in the window.

Phainon was the first to pull away from their embrace, offering a gentle smile to Mydei, who now avoided making eye contact with him.

Their movements were slow and deliberately sluggish in an attempt to prolong this quiet early morning together. Mydei never had many things with him to pack in the first place, so the preparations went by quicker than they liked.

Mydei would leave behind many trinkets, spices, food, and gifts he had gotten in his short stay here. Given his next destination, it seemed these items would be of greater use to Phainon. However, Phainon managed to sneak in one item he had purchased for Mydei, knowing the other wouldn’t mind keeping it. It was a beautiful hair tie, which he carefully placed into Mydei's braid. The tie was small and discreet enough that Mydei didn't object to keeping it.

When the sun fully rose above the horizon, they set out toward the gates of Ohkema. It was still early enough that no locals were present to witness their departure. Only the knights who stood guard, as they always did, were there.

This was their final opportunity to exchange words, yet neither of them could bear to say goodbye.

An awkward silence passed between them as they stood at the steps leading outside the gates. But Phainon finally had the courage to say something.

"Before you go, I wanted to return something to you."

"Return something?" Mydei asked, unable to remember giving Phainon anything of his.

"I was meant to use this when I officially proposed to you, but…" Phainon cleared his throat to mask his emotions. "I guess now is the best time to return this to you."

He reached into his pocket and pulled out a golden signet ring. It appeared to be well cared for and had a thin golden chain attached for safekeeping.

Mydei's eyes widened as he took the ring into his palm. A surge of emotions washed over him as he remembered the last time he had seen this ring. It was the final item he possessed that belonged to his mother, and the day it was lost marked one of the most difficult moments of his life.

He gazed in shock between the ring and Phainon, his voice trapped in his throat. "How…"

The sun shone brightly behind Phainon, creating a halo around his head as he smiled warmly at Mydei, tears threatening to spill from his eyes. Meanwhile, Mydei was trembling, oblivious to the tears streaming down his own face. "Khaslana?"

Phainon’s eyes widened, and he let out a chuckle, tears also spilling down his face as he desperately tried to wipe them away in an effort to maintain his composure. "You still remember me?"

Mydei reached out for Phainon, pulling him into a tight embrace. "Why didn't you tell me? Why now?" His voice was laced with frustration, and he could feel his composure slipping away. "I thought you were…" He couldn't finish his sentence and just hugged Phainon tighter than before.

"You didn't seem to recognize me at the bridal selection ceremony, but I knew you right away, Mydeimos. Not a single day passed where I would ever forget your face." Phainon smiled, placing a gentle kiss on Mydei's forehead.

Mydei felt a surge of guilt and frustration, wanting to cuss out Phainon about what had happened back then. Where had he vanished to? He had searched for him for hours! Khaslana was gone, and he blamed himself for it all.

But he was right here, and Mydei still couldn't believe it was real. Were the titans merely toying with them? How could their fates intertwine like this, only to have them continuously pulled apart?

Their time was running out, and Mydei needed to leave before the residents noticed what was happening. It was incredibly painful to pull away from Phainon, especially after that revelation.

"May the lance of fury always bring you victory." Phainon took the signet ring and carefully placed the chain around Mydei's neck. "Goodbye, Mydeimos."

Mydei closed his eyes, forcing the pain in his heart to settle. "Goodbye, Phainon."

chapters.title: Chapter 11: A Winter Cold
chapters.html:
It has been a few months since Mydei left Ohkema. In the first month, a large number of residents began to question why the two fiancés had not been seen in public. When Phainon appeared at a private gathering for nobles, he arrived alone, which sparked even more public speculation.

Initially, it was assumed that a quarrel had occurred and now there was going to be a new bride soon, but this was quickly dismissed by the residents of the Mamoreal Market, who affirmed that the two men were undoubtedly in love with each other days prior.

As more weeks passed, the public noticed Phainon's declining health during his appearances at official royal functions. He looked a little thinner, and his complexion appeared somewhat sickly. This sparked outrage among the residents, who demanded answers from the palace about Mydei's whereabouts as well as the well-being of Phainon.

It seems the palace did not anticipate the public's positive perception of Mydei, believing that the public would soon forget about Phainon's engagement. However, Phainon was no longer seen around the markets, where he had previously interacted with the locals weekly. This absence led the public to spread rumors that the palace had sent Mydei back to Castrum Kremnos against Phainon's will.

"Why would the palace do something like that? It doesn't make any sense! Isn't their marriage meant to support the peace treaty?" One resident began to gossip loudly in the busy streets. More people began to chime in on the conversation.

"Of course it makes sense! The palace must have realized that Mydei was an alpha! Why would they ever allow two alphas to wed when they cannot even produce heirs?" Another resident responded, shaking their head and clicking their tongue, reflecting on how unfair this situation was for Phainon.

"Then they shouldn't have allowed Lord Phainon to choose his bride like that in the first place. The poor man looks utterly heartbroken!" More frustrated murmurs followed.

"Lord Phainon has never looked so distraught before. How could they do such a thing?"

"It's the 4900s, and they still discriminate based on secondary genders!"

"I suppose discussing heirs is quite important for the nobles."

"But it shouldn't matter for Lord Phainon, as he isn't even in line for the throne. Wasn't he an adopted collateral member of the royal family? Why should heirs matter for him?"

"We still don't know what happened to Lord Mydeimos. Was he taken away in secret? The palace needs to provide answers!"

The unrest among the people was becoming increasingly difficult for the nobles to overlook, and they needed to intervene soon to prevent a potential riot.

It was impossible to pretend to be unaware of the people's pleas, as rumors had spread widely even among aristocratic families. Even the official press has been circulating various rumors and news regarding the relationship between Phainon and Mydei.

Aglaea, who oversees public relations, has been grappling with this challenging situation, hearing most of the outcries through her numerous golden nymphs spread across the kingdom. While she understands the concerns being raised, she is uncertain about how to explain the circumstances without revealing too much about the new peace contract, which must remain confidential.

It didn't help that Phainon had isolated himself in his estate for months, only making appearances at official events. This behavior has only fueled further controversy surrounding the palace.

Even as the seasons shifted and winter settled in, the heat of public discontent toward the palace continued to grow intense. Perhaps it was time for Aglaea to pay Phainon a visit. They had attempted to visit Phainon several times in the past few months, but each time they were turned away without any explanation.

Aglaea understands better than anyone in the palace how infatuated Phainon was with Mydeimos. Although she may not fully grasp the reasons behind their deep affections, her nymphs have informed her that the two have been remarkably close during their public appearances.

Although it might be challenging to persuade Phainon to present a smile for the public and help dispel the rumors, Aglaea knew she had to at least attempt to check on him.

Hyacine and Castorice requested to accompany Aglaea because they too were both extremely concerned about Phainon's physical condition. His last public appearance, which was a week ago, had raised alarms.

Upon arriving at the estate, the ladies observed how neglected the gardens had become, with old autumn leaves left scattered and not cleaned up at all. Snow was soon expected to fall, making it much more difficult to manage the garden. They could only imagine the condition of the inside of the manor.

They first knocked lightly, trying not to startle Phainon with loud banging on the door. However, when they received no response, they began calling out his name.

"Something is wrong," Castorice said, feeling the cold handle of the door. "Please pardon the intrusion, Lord Phainon." She gestured for the others to step back as she raised her weapon and carefully pried the door open.

As they entered, they felt an intense chill in the room, even colder than the winter winds outside. This suggested that Phainon had not been lighting the fires to warm his home.

"Lord Phainon?" They called out to him again, their voices raised in agitation, but were met with the same unsettling silence.

"Is he not home?" Hyacine inquired, but Castorice shook her head, asserting that she sensed Phainon's presence within the house.

The house was not disorganized, but it had an unsettlingly abandoned feel. Dust accumulated on the tables, and there was a distinct absence of warmth during the frigid winter.

"Search for him at once," Aglaea urged, her voice filled with alarm. They sensed that something was amiss and understood the urgency of locating Phainon without delay.

Hyacine and Aglaea searched the downstairs while Castorice ascended the stairs to check the bedrooms. After a few moments, Castorice's voice echoed from the top of the staircase.

"Aglaea! Hyacine! Please come to the master bedroom at once!"

The two raced upstairs as quickly as possible, and Hyacine was already unfastening her medical briefcase, which she had brought with her just in case.

As they entered the room, they saw Phainon lying in bed, appearing to be asleep with nothing out of the ordinary. However, upon checking, they discovered that his temperature was alarmingly high and almost too hot to touch.

"Cassy, could you please bring me some water and a clean towel?" Hyacine asked as she quickly removed the blankets covering Phainon. She retrieved some cooling gel from her bag and applied it to his forehead while unbuttoning a few buttons on his shirt. "Please excuse me, Lord Phainon."

The next few minutes were chaotic as the three of them tried their best to lower Phainon's temperature. Hyacine remembered it being reminiscent of when Phainon experienced his first rut. However, the symptoms were notably different, and they did not sense Phainon's imposing pheromones this time.

"What's happening to him, Hyacine? Is he about to enter his rut again?" Aglaea asked, keeping a towel firmly pressed over Phainon's chest.

"No. This isn't a rut. It's something else..." She began to rack her brain for anything that might explain his condition, but she needed Phainon to wake up in order to get a clearer picture of what he was experiencing.

When Phainon's temperature began dropping, they felt him stir in his bed until he finally opened his eyes.

"Lord Phainon! Can you hear us?"

Phainon felt a slight dizziness as he lay there, but his vision quickly cleared, revealing three very worried faces surrounding him. "Hmm? What's going on?"

"Phainon, we found you curled up in bed with an extremely high fever, and you were unresponsive to everything." Castorice explained to him, sighing in relief that he was finally awake.

"But I shouldn't be entering my rut for a while." He attempted to rise, but all three women gently pushed him back down, insisting that he remain still.

"This isn't a rut, but you do seem to be unwell. How are you feeling, Phainon? Please tell me any symptoms you’re experiencing at the moment." Hyacine pulled out a small notebook and began to write.

"I feel really cold," Phainon explained, clutching his chest, which was covered by a cold towel. "But my chest has been feeling this weird sensation lately, like it's on fire while the rest of my body is freezing. I haven't been able to control my pheromones very well, so I've been avoiding going outside as much as possible."

Hyacine continued to jot down notes while listening to Phainon's explanation.

"My appetite hasn't been particularly good lately. Occasionally I feel… confused? Like I could be walking around my house and suddenly forget what I'm doing. My chest starts to hurt so much that I end up heading back to bed."

Phainon did his best to explain his situation, but he soon noticed a somewhat sullen expression on Hyacine's face.

"What is it?" Aglaea asked when they realized Hyacine had fallen silent.

"I need to confirm some things first and consult Professor Anaxa about your condition. For now, would it be alright for you to move to the medical clinic in the palace?" Hyacine inquired, hoping that Phainon would agree.

"I'd prefer to stay here. My pheromones have been quite unstable lately, and I would rather not cause any additional trouble," Phainon explained. "I apologize for worrying all of you."

"If you ever feel something is wrong again, I have a nymph outside your manor. You can call for me from there, alright?" Aglaea assured him. "We're relieved that we found you and that you're safe."

"Thank you." Phainon looked embarrassed, but he was clearly too sickly to even pretend he was in any condition to mask how he felt.

As the evening grew late, the ladies decided to retire for the day. Hyacine felt a twinge of reluctance to leave Phainon in his weakened state, but he assured them he was feeling much better now. He also promised he would take the medicine Hyacine had provided and would contact Aglaea as soon as possible if anything happened again.

For now, that was sufficient for them, and Phainon found himself alone once again in his manor. Hyacine had promised to return the next morning with a diagnosis, and Phainon felt a slight sense of relief, knowing that he was likely just suffering from a winter illness.

His appetite remained poor, but he assured them he would eat the porridge that Castorice had prepared earlier. He dragged himself into the kitchen and began eating in silence. The food was intentionally bland to make it easier for Phainon to swallow.

As he ate and felt the warmth of the food, he clutched his chest, grimacing at the burning sensation within while the rest of his body remained frigidly cold.

However, he chose to push those thoughts aside.

Phainon already had an inkling of what was happening to him, and he recognized that it was all his fault. However, he was reluctant to acknowledge this shortcoming, as he hadn’t anticipated things would backfire to this extent.

He hoped his fears were unfounded when Hyacine arrived the next morning. Yes, everything was fine. He just needed some medicine for a winter cold, right?

With the little strength he had left, he hurriedly cleaned the kitchen before heading straight back to bed. His steps felt heavy, and the burning sensation in his chest was making him dizzy.

"I just need to hang on…" Phainon reassured himself as he slowly ascended the stairs.

He couldn't remember how long it took him to reach his bedroom again, nor did he recall how quickly he fell asleep after hitting the bed. When he finally came to, he found himself sprawled haphazardly across the mattress, with one leg dangling over the edge.

He could have sworn he had just closed his eyes moments ago, yet the morning sun was already rising on the horizon. His body felt so heavy, and it seemed as if he hadn't slept at all throughout the night.

Perhaps it would be acceptable for him to sleep a little longer. At least this way, he could pretend that the searing pain in his chest wasn't worsening.

At the very least, he had no difficulty falling asleep, which was both a blessing and a curse, as the pain was so intense that it would simply knock him out.

The door to his estate suddenly swung open, and two individuals hurried inside. After Castorice had broken the lock yesterday, nothing could prevent these two from charging straight for the master bedroom.

Despite the heavy footsteps echoing through the quiet house, Phainon stayed asleep, curled up in numerous layers of blankets once again.

"Lord Phainon!" Hyacine burst into the bedroom, quickly assessing his current condition once more. The fever was still high, but it had improved slightly compared to yesterday's state.

The two visitors swiftly adjusted Phainon's position on the bed, ensuring he was more comfortable. They began checking his vitals and administered a few shots to help reduce his fever.

After feeling a sharp prick in his arm from the shots, Phainon gradually woke up, still groggy. He looked up to see Hyacine and an unexpected face. "Professor Anaxa!" he exclaimed in surprise, nearly knocking himself out in his frantic attempt to sit up.

Hyacine gently but firmly pushed him back down onto the bed, her smile masking a hint of annoyance. "Lord Phainon, I must insist that you refrain from moving around so much. It would be best for you to avoid sitting up for now."

"Sorry…" He apologized while looking down at his arm.

"Phainon of Aedes Elysiae," Anaxa began, his voice curt. He sat down next to the bedside table while Hyacine stood on the other side of the bed.

Phainon appeared to brace himself for a scolding, keeping his gaze lowered to avoid eye contact with the two doctors who had come all this way to his home personally.

"Good. It seems you're already aware of what you've done." Anaxa sighed while studying the obviously guilty expression on his student's face. "Now tell me why you decided to do this to yourself."

"I…" Phainon couldn't finish his sentence, unable to give an answer that would make sense.

"Your condition is quite rare, and it could really only be achieved by dominants of respective traits," Anaxa continued, jotting down notes in his notebook. "Honestly, I expected better from my own student than to willingly do something like this."

Phainon still didn't look up and just looked down in embarrassment.

"Phainon." Anaxa called his name again, waiting for the man to look up at him. When Phainon finally gained the courage to look up at his old teacher, Anaxa gave him a stern gaze. "Are you aware you could die by doing this? Your pheromones will be extremely erratic, and your physical condition will continue to deteriorate."

"Professor…" Hyacine tried to intervene for a moment. She sat down on the bed next to Phainon and gently patted his shoulder.

"Why would you do a one-sided imprint?" Anaxa asked again. "Does Mydeimos even know you did this?"

"No." Phainon finally responded, "He shouldn't know."

"We need to send out a messenger at once and ask for Mydeimos to return immediately. Otherwise, you could seriously get hurt, Lord Phainon…" Hyacine attempted to convey this in a gentler tone.

"No! Please don't," Phainon exclaimed, glancing up with a look of concern. "He’s in a very difficult situation right now and can’t risk jeopardizing his position by returning here."

"Is this why you did this?" Anaxa set down his notepad to meet Phainon's gaze. "So you could feel what Mydei is going through, no matter how far away he is?"

Phainon could not deny the question and fell silent once more.

"Phainon, you could die the longer Mydeimos stays away. You need to be around him and his pheromones to counter the side effects of your one-sided imprint. Did you even think this through? What if Mydei does not come back to Ohkema even after reclaiming the throne of Castrum Kremnos?"

"He will. I know he will come back."

Anaxa sighed, refraining from arguing further with a clearly sick patient. He was doing his best to make some sense of Phainon's situation, but he knew it would be a challenge given how stubborn Phainon was.

"For now, you will need to take a few medications daily. There are some tonics to drink each morning, as well as powders to mix with your food. While these will not completely eliminate the side effects of the imprint, they should help reduce dizziness and may improve your appetite."

"Thank you," Phainon said in a soft voice.

Anaxa could almost laugh at how absurd the situation was, but he suppressed the urge and stood up. "Hyacine will check on your condition every three days. If your health continues to deteriorate, we will send a messenger to Castrum Kremnos, whether you want us to or not."

chapters.title: Chapter 12: The Gate
chapters.html:
Both Anaxa and Hyacine expected Phainon to last no longer than a month, but they seriously underestimated the man's stubbornness. Despite clearly witnessing his declining health, Phainon continued to keep himself active, pretending that everything was fine.

As winter grew colder and snow began to accumulate outside, the anger and rumors surrounding Phainon and his missing fiancé were temporarily subdued. Most people stayed indoors, allowing Phainon to avoid encounters with those outside his estate.

Aglaea and Castorice received an update about Phainon's condition from Hyacine. They were clearly outraged by Phainon's behavior, but they understood that arguing with a seriously ill man would be futile.

They also tried to reason with Phainon by suggesting that he send an envoy to bring Mydeimos back from Castrum Kremnos. Phainon held immense respect for his friends, but he simply could not agree with this idea. Mydei was engaged in a civil war at his home, and Phainon felt that he could not jeopardize all the hard work Mydei had put into the situation by pulling him away.

Phainon made every effort to reassure them that he was doing well, insisting that the medicine Anaxa and Hyacine had provided was effectively keeping him healthy.

But nobody believed him at all. He might appear to have energy, but they could see he was growing paler and weaker by the minute. His eyes were slightly sunken from the stress and pain he was experiencing, causing him to wake up multiple times during the night.

They recognized that reasoning with him was never going to work, yet it was incredibly painful for his friends to witness his gradual decline, knowing they might eventually have to disregard his wishes.

It was impossible to keep his condition a secret from the Imperator, as everyone was openly discussing Phainon. She had also agreed to delay disturbing the crown prince of Castrum Kremnos until it became absolutely necessary.

Aglaea considered this decision to be very cruel, hoping that the Imperator would have overridden Phainon's decision for his own well-being. However, everyone understood that Cerydra was opportunistic and seldom prioritized matters that did not serve to advance her reign.

For now, Aglaea enlisted Cifera's assistance to monitor Phainon in secret and to be prepared to leave as soon as possible should Phainon's condition deteriorate further. She hoped that before that happened, Mydeimos would manage to return on his own.

They had serious doubts about whether Mydei would return at all. He was on the path to becoming king of his country, and he would face numerous challenges before he could even consider returning to Ohkema.

Why would he even think of returning to Ohkema? It was a question no one dared to voice, all for Phainon's sake.

Imprinting is a delicate process that cannot occur accidentally or be forced. It is something that partners share to keep their hearts connected, effectively opening up all their emotions to one another and ensuring their devotion without room for doubt.

Imprinted couples share an intimate connection, allowing them to sense each other’s emotions, regardless of the distance between them. It may seem like a desirable trait for all couples, but in reality, very few partners end up imprinting, no matter how long their relationship has lasted.

Imprinting essentially binds you to one person for the entirety of your life. It is far more unforgiving than the marking that alphas can place on omegas, as it ensures that there will be no one else for them throughout their lifetime. Feelings could change, and these feelings between partners can turn into resentment, and yet this connection will never be severed.

Even if one partner cheats, ending the relationship would result in a lifetime of anguish, as their imprint prevents them from connecting with anyone else. Additionally, if one partner dies, the surviving half would be unable to form a romantic bond with anyone else.

Although the act of imprinting could be viewed as the most romantic practice in the world, it is simply unrealistic for most people. And so, it is rarely discussed between couples.

The process requires total affection and devotion from both partners for the bond to form. However, the expectation of mutual commitment often results in disagreements and breakups when one partner is not as devoted as the other.

One-sided imprinting is an exceptionally rare phenomenon, as it can only be achieved by individuals with hyperdominant traits. While it remains essential for both parties to harbor deep affections for one another, there are rare instances where these individuals can imprint themselves without exerting pressure on the other person to reciprocate.

More often than not, instances of this phenomenon occur between forbidden lovers who, despite their deep affection for one another, understand that they will never be able to be together.

In most cases, the individual without the imprint remains entirely unaware of what the other has experienced and would go through life oblivious to the fact that this person is suffering in silence. The mortality rate associated with one-sided imprints like this approaches one hundred percent, and the situation can only be remedied if the other half chooses to imprint themselves, thus completing the connection.

And it was because of these facts that Phainon's close friends could not completely get angry at him. The pain of the imprint itself was already enough, and all they could do was support him for as long as they could.

Things had been quiet for a long time, and even Phainon had started to adjust his lifestyle slightly to accommodate his illness. He still trained for a few minutes each day in his training ground behind his estate to maintain his fitness. It was remarkable to see that he could still keep a sharp mind, even as his energy was being sapped by the side effects of the imprint.

But without warning, Phainon suddenly collapsed.

He dropped his sword and knelt on the ground, clutching his chest and panting heavily.

Cipher quickly emerged from the shadows and rushed to him, struggling to support him. "Phainon!"

"Something happened to him…. He's… He's hurt!" Phainon started to panic, clutching his chest as pain gripped his heart. The imprint made it known to Phainon that something terrible had happened to Mydei.

This was information that none of them anticipated. No one had considered the possibility that Mydei could be in danger during the battle. Their attention was solely on Phainon, and they overlooked the risks that lay ahead.

Cipher did her best to help Phainon to his feet and hurried him inside the manor. Once they reached the living room, she ensured he was lying down on the sofa before she quickly went out to inform Aglaea.

Leaving to fetch Mydeimos was completely out of the question now that something had happened to him.

Aglaea was still in a meeting with the elders regarding winter supplies for the Ohkeman residents, and she could not entertain guests at that moment. However, when Cipher suddenly appeared before them, Aglaea noticed the panicked expression on her face—a look Cipher rarely showed.

Despite the elders' clear outrage at Cipher's sudden intrusion during their meeting, Aglaea swiftly dismissed the proceedings, citing an emergency that required her immediate attention.

As soon as the elders had departed and there was no one who could hear them, Cipher urgently explained to Aglaea that Phainon had collapsed and something had happened to Mydei. Although she attempted to maintain her composure, both women understood that the situation was dire.

"Call for Anaxa and Hyacine immediately. I will catch up with you as soon as I can. This needs to be brought to the Imperator without delay," Aglaea instructed before both women dispersed.

Cipher was the fastest person in Ohkema, and perhaps even in the entirety of Amphoreus. She was also extremely agile, her steps as light as a feather so that no one would notice if she passed by them. This skill allowed her to enter places easily without a permit or anyone noticing.

She quickly located Anaxa and Hyacine, who were in the midst of a lecture for young students in the medical wing of the Mamoreal Palace. Anaxa was the first to sense her arrival, and he instinctively understood that something terrible had occurred.

The class was dismissed at once, and the three hurried to gather supplies before racing back to Phainon's estate. By the time they arrived, both doctors were breathless. The thick snow and cold weather did not help them get there as fast as they would like.

But as they neared the manor, Cipher started to have a sinking feeling in her stomach. Why was the main door wide open? She could have sworn that she closed that door firmly before leaving.

She rushed ahead of the others to get inside the house, searching around the living room for Phainon, but the man was not where she had left him. Hurriedly, she checked all the rooms in a frenzy, calling out for Phainon but only receiving silence in return.

"Lord Phainon?" Hyacine started calling out for him as well when they realized what happened.

"He went outside. There are some footprints leading off towards the side gate," Anaxa announced, trying to capture the attention of the two who were still searching the manor for Phainon. Due to the heavy snowfall over the past few days, the paths had become easily obscured, making them difficult to notice.

While this whole frenzy was happening, Aglaea was having a hard time speaking with the Imperator about sending out assisting troops to help Mydei's encampment. It was crucial that they dispatched assistance as quickly as possible to guarantee not only the success of Mydei's campaign but also the safety of Phainon, whose life now depended entirely on Mydei.

But Cerydra was not cooperating this time, asserting that the affairs of Castrum Kremnos were not a matter in which Ohkeman troops could involve themselves, especially since the current king remained Eurypon and not Mydei.

Of course, Aglaea understood this better than most: the political dynamics between nations are fickle and sensitive. A single misstep could turn Ohkema into an enemy, with dire consequences to follow.

Before she could reason with the Imperator or offer any suggestions, she was promptly dismissed and unable to secure the assistance they required. She shouldn't have expected much in the first place, knowing how ruthless Cerydra truly was.

Not long after, she heard hurried footsteps approaching her. Despite Cipher's reputation for being fleet-footed, Aglaea's senses were always one step ahead. "Cifera, what happened? Is Phainon alright?"

"He's missing," Cipher said, doing her best to maintain a calm demeanor. "We tried to follow his trail into the palace, but somehow he managed to slip away."

"Didn't you say he collapsed not too long ago? How has he suddenly disappeared?" Aglaea was now beginning to show signs of agitation, which was unusual for her, as she typically remained the most composed and clear-headed among them.

"Agy! Ciphy!" A small voice called out to them from behind a pillar nearby.

"Tribbie?" They turned toward the voice and saw the oracle, who was signaling for them to be quiet while motioning for them to follow her. The two took a moment to steady themselves before silently following Tribbie.

Soon, they reached a secluded area in the Garden of Life, the home of the three oracles. This space was quiet and removed from the main pathways where most people would walk, ensuring that it was unlikely anyone would disturb the oracles.

Everyone was already huddled together inside the quiet home, including Phainon, who appeared to be just one strong breeze away from collapsing again.

Aglaea resisted the urge to berate him, relieved to see that he had made it safely to the others. In addition to the three oracles, Anaxa, Hyacine, and Castorice were already present, engaged in deep conversation that nearly bordered on an argument.

"Agy," Tribbie said as she approached her with a relaxed smile. "With your permission, we will open a Century Gate to Castrum Kremnos."

Aglaea was taken aback to hear this. The Century Gate was notoriously difficult for the oracles to conjure, often leaving one of them out of commission for an extended period. What surprised her even more was that they were asking Aglaea for permission. While she was a royal family member with succession rights to the throne, she still lacked the authority to grant such a request.

However, Aglaea realized that this was not a formal request. Instead, it served as a pretext for the triplet oracles to extend their assistance to Phainon. They understood that the Imperator would never permit Ohkema to offer official assistance to Castrum Kremnos. Nevertheless, they were determined to take action if it meant helping their friend.

"How many can pass through?" Aglaea asked, signaling her agreement with the plan.

"Triane says we can only transport three, or else we might get caught," Tribbie explained. Transporting even one person through the gate was enough to exhaust one of them, and to ensure that none of them would be decommissioned in the process, they could only pass one person each.

"Thank you, teacher…" Phainon finally spoke up, keeping his head held low to show how apologetic he was.

While everyone scrambled to figure out what to do and locate him, Phainon immediately sought out Tribios, the oracles, believing they might be his only chance to help Mydei.

"I will go with him." Castorice raised her hand first. "I'm well-trained in battle and do not have any official duties that would raise suspicion in my absence."

No one doubted Castorice's abilities, and they all agreed to let her be one of the companions.

"Hyacine, you can go. I will cover for your absence and handle any concerns that arise. If Mydeimos has indeed sustained an injury, your healing expertise will be invaluable." Anaxa spoke up next, understanding that Hyacine was hesitating to volunteer due to her responsibilities.

"Thank you, Professor Anaxa!" Hyacine beamed with a big smile.

"Okay, listen up!" Triane called out to grab everyone's attention. "We will keep the gate open for you to pass back through. It will remain open for only three days. By sunset on the third day, you must return, no exceptions. Only the original three who used the gate will be able to use it to come back through. Is everything clear?"

"Yes!" Phainon, Castorice, and Hyacine nodded their heads in agreement.

"Be careful, everyone. Especially you, Snowy!" Tribbie said this while giving a reassuring pat to Phainon's arm. "Make sure you all return without exception! Or else we will get very mad!"

Phainon placed his hand over his heart as he promised, "Thank you so much, everyone. I promise we will all return safely." The pain in his chest was still present, and there was an anxiousness creeping up on him every second. But he tried his best to conceal all of that.

Trinnon's soft voice echoed from the other side of the room as a glowing portal appeared beside her. "The gate is ready."

Chapter End Notes

chapters.title: Chapter 13: An Ongoing Battle
chapters.html:
Chapter Notes

Apologies for the delayed updates. It has been a very hectic few days for me, and I haven’t even done the new HSR main quest yet.

Castrum Kremnos has always been distant from the barbaric lands that many foreign nations imagined them to be. Despite their tendency to instigate wars and conflict, they were, in fact, a highly advanced fortress nation in terms of technology.

The sight of the palace and its surrounding infrastructure from afar caused the three unexpected visitors to stop and take in the awe-inspiring view.

However, it was evident that a war was ongoing in these lands. Dark smoke billowed from various points in the distance, crumbling ruins could be seen nearby, and they could hear the unmistakable sounds of conflict.

Contrary to what most people believed, this well-loved and protected lord from Cerydra's collateral line has fought in a good number of battles. To ensure his loyalty and strength for retaining his position in the palace, he was trained from the moment he was brought into Ohkema as a child.

Phainon had experienced wars, witnessed death, and healed from his own injuries. He was likely just as well-trained as Mydei, although he started a little later as a teen. Yet, this information had always remained a secret, as the common folk in Ohkema were unaware of his true background.

He was as skilled as the generals leading the frontlines of the Ohkeman armies, yet he remained a nameless soldier. Even those who fought alongside him were oblivious to the young noble concealed behind his mask and armor.

And so it was also a surprise to his two companions right now at how well he was holding his ground as they started fighting through armies of Kremnoan soldiers to enter the gates.

Phainon led the charge, deftly cutting down enemies with his expertly trained movements.

"Lord Phainon, where did you learn such remarkable fighting skills?" Hyacine asked, her expression animated with awe at how well Phainon was moving despite his health condition. She concentrated on providing support to her companions from the rear as they pressed forward in the charge.

"I've fought in a fair number of battles," Phainon said, letting out a small laugh to keep the mood light, as if it weren't a significant matter. However, it was clear that his two companions felt differently. At first, he considered keeping the truth hidden, but given how much his friends had supported him thus far, he felt more inclined to share a bit more with them.

"Her Majesty had me trained as a soldier to assist in some of the conflicts that Ohkema has been involved in in the past," Phainon explained. "It's a bit… unheard of for royal family members in Ohkema to participate directly in conflicts, but that's alright. I was happy to help."

The expressions of confusion and astonishment on Hyacine and Castorice's faces were unmistakable, showing that Phainon was clearly attempting to minimize the significance of his sudden confession about how he had been living his life under the Imperator.

But now was not the time for them to debate the implications, as they heard a commotion up ahead.

"Traitors to the crown of Kremnos will not be tolerated! All of you will be sentenced to your deaths here."

Phainon urged his friends to stay low and hide behind a large marble pillar with him. They watched as a group of armored Kremnoan soldiers raised their spears, pointing them at a smaller group of less armored men who were trying to shield what appeared to be another group of civilians.

"You call yourselves soldiers of this land while you point your weapons at your own people!" An older man among the civilians shouted at them, following up with a barrage of curses in a language they could not understand.

"Silence! By choosing to support that exiled prince, you have already shown your disrespect for the king and this land!" The soldiers moved forward, closing in on the group that had nowhere left to escape.

"A true king would fight in battle and prove himself! Only a coward would hide behind his army and resort to petty tricks to harm his own son!" One of the men shielding the civilians retorted sharply.

Phainon glanced at Castorice, nodding in her direction. She returned the nod, understanding what needed to be done. Rising first from her hiding spot, Castorice raised her arm toward the group of soldiers.

The ground beneath the soldiers shifted unexpectedly, transforming into a large, purple puddle that caused them to sink slightly into the floor, rendering them unable to move. Before they could make sense of what was happening, Phainon and Hyacine moved next.

The Kremnoan soldiers were swiftly dealt with, unable to call for reinforcements due to the quick ambush.

"Who…?" The men shielding the civilians looked up at them in surprise. "You are not from here," one of them quickly pointed out, noticing their foreign attire. Castrum Kremnos was in the midst of a civil war, and the arrival of these foreigners to rescue them was certainly unexpected.

"Greetings! We are allies of Prince Mydeimos, here to assist in his fight for the throne." Phainon bowed formally to them, ensuring that he and his companions kept their weapons sheathed before speaking.

The armored men still had very weary eyes, because they could not recall the prince ever telling them about such reinforcements arriving to assist them.

"Now don't be so ungrateful!" The old man from earlier interjected, giving the weary men a firm pat on the back. "Anyone who fights that well must be good friends with our prince!"

They could not even argue with the elderly man right now, even though his reasoning did not make any sense, because more Kremnoan soldiers could be heard in the distance, preventing them from escorting the civilians to a safe shelter.

"If you are indeed allies of our prince, we urgently need your assistance. The civilians must be escorted to safety." One of the men finally spoke up, bowing respectfully. "We are from the Kremnoan Detachment, led by the crown prince himself. I am Hephaestion, the prince's closest confidant."

Phainon smiled, and he hoped that his expression did not betray what was going on in his thoughts right now. Not only was he a little taken aback by the term "closest confidant," but he was also shaken by the fact that the man who said that was clearly an omega.

Hephaestion wasn't blatantly releasing pheromones, but Phainon's sensitivity made it clear to him.

Castorice quickly noticed Phainon's slightly tense expression and decided to speak on behalf of the group. "Hello, I'm Cassie. This is Cinny, and this is Snowy." She preferred not to reveal their true identities, so she opted to mention the nicknames that Tribios had given them.

The names were certainly unusual, but the group didn't have time for more pleasantries. They needed to begin moving and escorting the innocents away from the area.

Phainon took the lead, swiftly disarming the ambushing soldiers. He was clearly trying to show off right now. Who knew when Mydei would show up? He needed to ensure that he remained the most eligible man for Mydei, so his strength was necessary to be showcased to Mydei's people. Despite looking a little sickly, he still looked incredibly handsome and reliable, which made the civilians feel at ease.

He ensured that his actions were swift while also demonstrating mercy, making certain that no children witnessed any excessive bloodshed. Hyacine also made a protective bubble that shielded around the civilians and wounded warriors.

The civilians were certainly looking up at the group with much delight, and they were clearly impressed by their presence. When they were almost caught earlier by the soldiers, the warriors from the detachment had already been worn down quite a bit from the relentless fighting. It was embarrassing for the Kremnoans to be found lacking and to be saved by outside forces, but there was no time for pride in that moment.

They soon arrived at a securely hidden location, away from the fighting, that the detachment had prepared in advance to shelter several civilians. Naturally, the sight of foreigners caused a bit of a commotion, but the people quickly calmed down upon hearing Hephaestion speak and explain that the three were allies.

Now that they had finished the task, Phainon quickly asked the warriors about Mydei's whereabouts. They were at first a little hesitant to talk about it, since they still did not know how these foreigners even came to know their prince.

Hyacine quickly demonstrated her willingness to help by starting to heal the many wounded warriors. Castorice assisted her closely by retrieving some supplies they had brought along. The scene was very heartwarming, as many of the warriors thought they would not be able to receive healing until the war was over.

The warriors conversing with Phainon felt a surge of gratitude for the assistance they were receiving. "We cannot disclose too much information, but the prince is currently engaged in an ongoing battle with that tyrant. It has been several days since their battle began, and we are unable to intervene. Prince Mydeimos has made it clear that, regardless of the dirty tricks Eurypon may employ, he intends to handle it. Alone."

Upon hearing this, Phainon felt a heavy weight in his chest. If the battle had already been ongoing for that long, that would mean Mydei is probably still fighting right now while badly wounded. "Where is the fight?"

"You cannot intervene." The warriors warned him.

But Phainon calmly responded to them, "I just need to see. I promise I will not intervene."

The warriors were still hesitant as they looked at Phainon, aware that foreigners often held very different values. For the Kremnoans, honor in battle was as vital as their own lives, which made it difficult for them to believe his words.

Hephaestion stepped forward to propose a solution, as neither side was willing to yield. "Please leave your weapons behind. You cannot destroy our prince's honor by intervening."

Without hesitation, Phainon took his sword and gave it to Castorice for safekeeping. "I'll be back before you know it." He assured his two companions.

"Lo—" Hyacine cleared her throat, almost using his title. "Snowy, please don’t do anything reckless," she said curtly, her hands resting on her hips.

Now that everything was agreed upon, Hephaestion and a man who introduced himself as Leonnius were to escort him to a location far enough from the battle yet close enough for them to observe it.

They sensed no negative intentions from Phainon, but they did recognize his strong alpha pheromones. This awareness was why Leonnius volunteered to accompany them, as it was generally unwise to leave an alpha and omega alone together.

Phainon, however, displayed no interest in Hephaestion, despite the latter being renowned as the beauty of the Kremnoan Detachment. Most alphas would regard him with gentleness rather than indifference. In fact, it seemed as though Phainon actively disliked Hephaestion's presence. While this behavior puzzled them, they attributed it to a foreigner’s unfamiliarity with the true concept of beauty.

The opinions of other alphas also held little weight for the warriors close to the crown prince. To them, Hephaestion stood out as the obvious choice for the eventual king consort. Although he possessed a small stature and a strikingly beautiful face, he proved to be a formidable force on the battlefield, bolstering his reputation with his considerable strength and numerous achievements.

Phainon could sense the eyes staring daggers at him as they left to go see Mydei's battle, but he did not care for anything else right now. All that consumed his thoughts was the fact that Mydei was severely injured, and he needed to check on his well-being immediately.

He understood that he had no right to intervene and tarnish Mydei's reputation. However, he also held a strong belief that Mydei would emerge victorious, and he wished he could be there to support him as soon as the battle concluded.

As they approached the inner sanctums of the palace, the sounds of fighting grew louder. Phainon's heart raced with worry, yet he remained calm and focused.

They reached a platform that provided a view of a large, circular open arena. The surroundings were in ruins with destruction, and in the distance, two figures battled fiercely, exchanging heavy blows without pause.

Phainon fixed his gaze on Mydeimos, the burning sensation of his imprint flaring up once more. He was so close now, yet still too far to offer any comfort. Instead, the distance intensified his longing, sending waves of pain coursing through his body.

Mydei appeared injured, though not seriously enough to hinder his movements. He remained steady and calm as he faced the deranged king before him. Eurypon had transformed drastically into a madman. He no longer resembled his usual noble and respectable self.

His hair was a tangled mess, his clothes hung loosely on his frame, and his body was marred with wounds. Despite his uncoordinated movements, each strike still carried considerable force. Mydei had to exercise caution, as Eurypon's unpredictable actions made him a difficult opponent.

Even the two companions with Phainon were intensely focused on the fight, remaining silent as they held their breaths whenever dust from the rubble obscured their view.

They were unaware of how long they had been standing there, watching intently, but each second seemed to stretch on endlessly, and they could not pull their attention away. Each powerful strike exchanged between the two could ultimately be the deciding factor, after all.

Phainon was the most incredibly affected. Throughout this time, as he sensed Mydei drawing nearer, he could feel each painful strike exchanged in the fight. He started to feel lightheaded, but he persevered as long as he could see Mydei.

Eurypon's movements were starting to slow down, and Phainon observed the same was true for Mydei. Mydei was closely guarding his back, suggesting he had likely sustained a serious injury there.

They were oblivious to the sun setting above them and the night sky casting a dim glow. The fiery torches around the arena provided barely enough light to see through the fight, yet neither side paused to rest.

When Mydei was unexpectedly pushed back a significant distance after a powerful blow, Phainon doubled over in pain and knelt on the ground. His two companions were taken aback by this and hurried to assist him, asking him what was wrong.

Phainon clearly couldn't respond directly to the question, so he weakly laughed it off and falsely claimed he had been injured on their way to the palace earlier. He grasped his heart tightly and shut his eyes, trying to steady himself on the ground.

"Mydei, I know you can do it. I believe in you!" He prayed quietly in his mind, hoping that his feelings would somehow reach Mydei. If his words could provide even a little comfort, that would be enough.

While Mydei recovered from the blow, he felt a soothing wind enveloping him. A gentle scent, faint yet familiar, wrapped around him, bringing a sense of relief and support.

"Phainon?" He looked around the arena, but he couldn't see anyone there.

Chapter End Notes
