chapters.title: Chapter 14: Reunion
chapters.html:
Chapter Notes

Just wanted to rant a little before the chapter. You can ignore all this and carry on!!

I saw the recent drama over people accusing Phaidei artists and writers of spamming and suspicious growth, which they claim is why the ship is becoming number 1 now (on HSR) on many platforms. Some even go as far as saying that the AO3 tag is filled with AI slop just to inflate the number of fics. This is just so disrespectful to all the creators out there who pour out so much passion and love into their works, only for others to accuse them just because of the exponential growth of this fandom. And for what? Because their own ships have been "dethroned"? Has this ever been a popularity contest? I haven't written fanfiction since I started working a few years back, but this ship has singlehandedly made me come back and contribute to fandom again. I could be sleeping early after getting back from work, but I instead spend nights outlining and writing my silly little gay stories. Many of us are real people with real lives outside of fandom, and it sucks to be labeled "sus" and ingenuine just because the love of this ship has grown so much over the past few months. I hope this negativity can be redirected into their own ships instead of intruding here.

The sudden scent that filled Mydei’s senses jolted him awake from his exhaustion. He felt revitalized, and he realized that this battle was nearing its conclusion.

Eurypon remained engulfed in madness, his expression deranged, exhausted, and desperate. The king, once revered by the entire nation from his throne, had become a mere shell of his former self.

A part of Mydei still remembered his father from his childhood. He had been loving and devoted to both his wife and son, a king who embodied compassion alongside strength. Mydei struggled to recall when things began to change back then.

Perhaps it was when he began to see his father less frequently. Queen Gorgo often appeared frustrated, and his parents seemed to argue whenever they were in the same room.

It was odd, the young Mydeimos once thought. Was his father sick? He had been acting so differently back then. Even the scent of his pheromones changed and became foreign to them. It was no longer a comforting scent. It was rotten, and everyone around them could sense it.

The memory of being dragged out of his bedroom as a young child was still vivid in Mydei’s memory. He would reach out to his mother, pleading with her to help him. But even the queen herself was being restrained by multiple guards, unable to reach out for her son.

The king glared down at Mydei with a look of disgust. What had caused him to regard his own son in such a way? Where had the tender gaze of a father gone?

Even now, as they faced off for the last time, there was no trace of familiarity in his father's eyes. Mydeimos wondered if, had he been older then, he might have been able to prevent the council of advisors from slowly poisoning his father. Was there more a crown prince could have done?

Would he have been able to prevent their nation from crumbling beneath him right now?

He understood that blaming himself for the past was futile, yet it remained painful to witness the destruction of everything his family had built, all at the hands of treacherous snakes lurking within their own walls.

Killing each and every one of those advisors in the council was the first task Mydeimos undertook upon his return to Castrum Kremnos. It didn't matter whether it was accomplished through surprise duels orchestrated by the five generals of the detachment. Ambushing them in public duels was sufficient to wound their pride.

To hold high positions, they needed to possess at least some skills to contend with mercenaries. However, it was evident that many of these cowardly old fools had not ascended to power through their own strengths. Their pride, which led them to refuse to admit defeat, culminated in their swift downfalls at the hands of the Kremnoan Detachment.

Killing was still considered dishonorable, as most types of duels served primarily as a test of strength. However, such incidents became unavoidable when unfortunate accidents occurred. As the advisors were gradually killed one by one, many began to cower in fear within their homes, choosing to hide.

As the king's council continued to diminish before their eyes, the need for replacements to maintain balance was necessary. This presented an opportunity for members of the detachment, under the leadership of Ptolemy and Peucestas, to infiltrate the council. They were the smartest and most charismatic of their group and assimilated into the council without issue.

Their rapport and position needed to be established and solidified. This would facilitate Mydei’s rise to power more swiftly while ensuring that some council members remained in place.

The next priority for the detachment was to establish a safe zone for the residents. The kingdom was on the brink of chaos, and involving civilians in the fighting would render their efforts pointless. Without its people, the kingdom would cease to exist, making the protection of its citizens the most critical aspect to address.

It was no surprise that it took several months before they could even put their plans into motion. Careful planning for the aftermath was essential. Even if Mydei were to slay his father the moment he returned to Castrum Kremnos, it would not adequately prepare their nation for the impending change.

In all those grueling months of preparation, Mydei was consumed by anxiety. He couldn't pinpoint the cause, but something had been troubling him ever since his return from Ohkema.

Perdikkas, the doctor of the detachment, had thoroughly examined him and confirmed that there was nothing physically wrong. Although he did not feel ill or in pain, an unexplainable anxiousness lingered within him.

He attempted to dismiss it as mere nerves about the impending battle with his father, but that reasoning simply did not make sense.

Mydei had prepared his entire life for that day and felt more confident than ever. However, he was not worried about the impending battle. It was something else that he could not quite explain.

Every time he closed his eyes and thought long and hard about what was bothering him, images of the same man came to mind.

Was he anxious about not seeing his beloved after a very long time? Just the thought of himself unconsciously referring to Phainon like that made him feel shy.

He knew his worries were unfounded. Phainon was safe and sound in Ohkema, where he belonged. There was no reason for him to feel anxious about him.

Perhaps Mydei simply missed him. The thought made him scoff, and he would quickly wipe a smile off his face to avoid being noticed by anyone around him.

Even though Phainon was far away, Mydei found solace in the thought of their eventual reunion. It might not happen soon, but he was committed to completing the majority of his responsibilities as the new king first so he could visit Phainon again. He wasn't quite sure yet what he would do when they met again, but that was a worry for another time.

Mydei couldn’t help but sigh in relief when he suddenly sensed the soothing pheromones of Phainon enveloping him. Whether this was merely a figment of his imagination or not, it filled him with energy and provided the boost he needed to finally conclude this battle.

With his newfound confidence and energy, Mydei was able to discern the openings and weaknesses in Eurypon's movements more clearly. The mad king appeared shaky and uncertain, his expressions growing increasingly erratic. However, these delayed reactions provided Mydei with the advantage he needed.

Mydei could have easily ended this fight, but he did not want to grant Eurypon the mercy of a quick death. He felt it was necessary for his father to experience the weight of his years of pain, to lie there suffering until his final breath. While this approach was vengeful, it also offered a more dignified end.

To die in an instant would be a show of compassion, but it would also feel like a mockery for someone who had once been the king of this land. Perhaps deep down, Mydei still wished to preserve at least a shred of dignity for his father.

With the final blows that reverberated through the arena, Eurypon finally sank to his knees and gradually lowered himself to the ground. As he lay there, gazing up at his son, the dull hue of his eyes flickered with the slightest hint of light.

It was almost as if the light in his eyes had returned in those final moments. Mydei couldn’t believe it. He saw the eyes of his father from all those years ago staring up at him.

In his final moments, the poison briefly subsided. There were no words he could offer that would bring any comfort to his son. All he could do was give a weak smile and a quiet apology. His body, frail and severely injured, was unable to shed any tears, and his eyes would not close as he breathed his last.

Mydei clenched his hands into tight fists, turning his gaze away from his father.

That day marked the fall of King Eurypon at last.

Earlier, when Hephaestion and Leonnius saw Eurypon fall to the ground, they couldn’t help but cheer inwardly. Knowing that Mydei would soon be joining them, they carefully assisted Phainon to his feet and led him back to camp.

At that moment, Phainon remained conscious and longed to cheer at the top of his lungs upon witnessing Mydei’s victory. However, the stabbing pain in his chest prevented him from moving.

So much for trying to look good in front of Mydei’s people. Phainon internally cursed at himself for ending up in a state like this in front of Mydei's close confidants, no less. He thought he would be able to hold out a little longer, but his stubbornness could only get him so far.

As the three returned to the camp, Hyacine and Castorice were taken aback by his condition and swiftly moved to attend to him.

“He suddenly collapsed while we were observing the battle from a distance. He mentioned that he was injured on the way here, so it might be best to have his wounds treated again,” Leonnius explained to them.

Hyacine expressed her gratitude for their help in bringing Phainon back and quickly cleared a space for him to sit and lean back.

“Lord Phainon…” Hyacine said, her voice laced with concern as she placed a comforting hand on his shoulder. “We really need to get you to Lord Mydei as soon as possible. The medicine is starting to lose its effectiveness. Do you think we can help end the battle sooner?”

“There’s no need.” Phainon smiled weakly and looked up to gesture toward the distance. On the long bridge that led to the civilians' encampment, a striking figure donning gold and red-clothed armor was walking towards them.

Everyone else noticed as loud cheers erupted around the encampment. The new king had arrived!

There was a mix of emotions amidst the loud cheering. Some parents cried tears of joy while clutching their young children. Warriors, even those still injured, struggled to rise and salute the new king. Children dashed out of the encampment to be the first to welcome Mydei.

The generals of the detachment were first to greet Mydei by his side. Hephaestion stood particularly very close to Mydei while they spoke. No one could hear what they were talking about, but Mydei would soon let out a tender laugh while looking at Hephaestion.

It was undeniable that the sight of the two together was stunning. They were a match that made perfect sense: a strikingly handsome and well-built alpha paired with a slender, beautiful omega.

Phainon could not help but watch this in silence, and the feeling in his chest started making him feel dizzy again.

“I wonder if Mydei has ever looked at me like that…” Phainon murmured to himself. Straining to rise, he attempted to navigate through the crowd to get closer to Mydei.

Hyacine and Castorice were doing their best to restrain him, insisting that he needed to stay put while they called for Mydei. However, they could see the desperation in Phainon’s eyes, which made it difficult for them to hold him back.

Mydei remained frustratingly out of reach. Phainon could already sense his pheromones, but the closer proximity only made it more challenging for him to stay on his feet as the pain flared up.

The crowd surrounding Mydei was busy and full of excitement, and there was no easy way for Phainon to squeeze through in his current condition.

His vision was becoming increasingly blurry, and he was being jostled back and forth in the sea of cheerful people. Hyacine and Castorice were also quickly engulfed by the crowd, losing their grip on Phainon.

"Snowy?" Mydei repeated, confusion evident in his voice. Hephaestion began recounting how a man named Snowy had assisted them earlier with the last group of civilians needing relocation. However, Mydei struggled to remember ever meeting someone by that name or encountering two women named Cassie and Cinny.

It was not until he heard a name being yelled in the crowd. The voices were faint amidst the cheering, but it was a name that Mydei had longed to hear out loud for a very long time.

Phainon's consciousness was fading. He was finally pushed back hard enough to collapse once more. But before his head could hit the ground, strong arms wrapped around him, pulling him close.

The crowd was taken aback when their king suddenly made his way through, his face filled with worry. A hush fell over the spectators as they witnessed him lift a man off the ground in his arms and carry him away.

"Perdikkas." Mydei called for one of his generals, and he quickly exited into a tent that was reserved for him.

The other generals attempted to steer the crowd's reactions back toward celebration, clarifying that Mydei was concerned about an old friend and needed to step away for a moment.

Castorice and Hyacine witnessed the scene unfold, their breaths caught in their throats as they hurried after Mydei into the tent.

"Lord Phainon!" They rushed into the tent, calling out to him, but Phainon lay fully unconscious on the bed.

While Perdikkas was examining his condition, Mydei turned his attention to the two unfamiliar faces, asking them if they came here with Phainon. Why did Phainon look ghostly pale? Why did he look as if he had lost so much weight since he last saw him? Why are they here?

When he had held Phainon earlier, the man felt worryingly light, and his body was icy to the touch. Had Mydei not detected his faint breathing, he would have feared the worst.

"He… has been sick these past few months," Hyacine explained, her voice hesitant and vague. She felt uncomfortable discussing Phainon's condition with another man present in the room.

“Months?” Mydei felt his heart drop at that word.

He noticed Hyacine's discomfort and promptly asked Perdikkas for a moment of privacy. As the man left the tent, Castorice also chose to stand guard outside the tent, ensuring that no one would overhear their conversation. Phainon's status as a royal family member of Ohkema remained significant, and it would be detrimental to Castrum Kremnos if news about his collapse within its walls spread.

Hyacine understood that she could no longer postpone her explanation. She realized Phainon would be angry with her for revealing his condition so quickly, but there was no time for his outbursts. He was in a critical state, and he needed Mydei's support immediately.

She started by explaining the one-sided imprint. At some point during their time together, enough pheromones had been exchanged between them for Phainon to imprint without Mydei’s awareness. While this was a rare occurrence, Phainon’s unique trait made it significantly easier.

Mydei couldn't understand how he had never noticed this or why Phainon would even consider doing such a thing. He was aware that it was a dangerous and taboo act, and hearing Hyacine explain what had been happening over the past few months only added to his frustration.

Now the unease he had been feeling all along finally made sense. He had always thought he was worrying about Phainon for no reason, but he hadn’t realized that the man was gradually deteriorating.

Hyacine reassured him that, as long as Phainon continued to receive Mydei's pheromones regularly, he would be fine.

"However, we certainly don't want to impose, Lord Mydei." She bowed her head respectfully. "As the new king of Castrum Kremnos, your responsibilities here are of utmost importance. We apologize for causing all this trouble. The scholars in Ohkema are currently researching a way to reverse the one-sided imprint, so—"

"No," Mydei abruptly interrupted her. "I…"

He tried to speak, but the words eluded him. What was the plan now? He couldn’t kidnap Phainon and keep him in Castrum Kremnos. According to Hyacine's account, they had arrived here without the Imperator of Ohkema's approval. The war had just ended, and he was not willing to initiate another one at the expense of his people.

"May I have a moment of privacy with him?" he asked, and Hyacine obliged without hesitation. It was somewhat embarrassing for imprinted couples to share pheromones with someone else present, so Hyacine gladly exited the room.

Phainon lay there, a solemn expression on his face. Mydei noticed his slightly sunken eyes and the once vibrant complexion now appearing ghostly white. He had become so accustomed to envisioning Phainon's smiling face that witnessing his current state brought a painful ache to his chest.

"HKS…" Mydei whispered, a hint of frustration lacing his voice as he gently ran his fingers through Phainon's hair. "I've wanted to see you for so long."

He settled closer at the edge of the bed, holding Phainon's hand tightly against his heart. "But not like this."

chapters.title: Chapter 15: Imprint
chapters.html:
Chapter Notes

Thank you for the continued support!

Please prepare for this roller coaster of a chapter! :D

It’s been nearly two days since Phainon fell into a deep sleep. Mydei has remained at his side for most of that time, refusing to leave him. Occasionally, Hyacine and Castorice would take turns with him whenever he was absolutely needed elsewhere or when he was compelled to go rest.

Mydei has been feeling anxious the entire time since Phainon still hasn’t woken up. Over the last few days, he has been releasing as many pheromones as possible around Phainon, sometimes climbing onto the bed to lie beside him. Fortunately, Hyacine and Castorice are both betas, so they aren’t too affected by the thick scent of pheromones.

Although they could still detect it, the scent was pleasant and conveyed Mydei’s genuine worry and care for Phainon.

Initially, the two ladies were wary of Mydei and felt more than a little indifferent toward this mysterious man who had somehow captured Phainon’s heart, leading him into such a perilous situation. They were puzzled by their friend, who had previously shown no interest in romance or settling down, suddenly getting on one knee and proposing so passionately to a stranger from a different land.

Maybe destiny truly did exist?

They were grateful for Mydei's attentive care over the past two days. After successfully seizing the crown, it took only a few hours for them to be moved into the palace, where they were accommodated in spacious guest rooms with all amenities provided.

Phainon ended up resting in Mydei’s chamber, which made sense since he needed to absorb as much of Mydei’s pheromones as possible to recover. However, the other members of Mydei’s party were stunned that this foreign man was allowed to sleep in the same bed as their king.

This was an alpha man, after all! Was he some close relative they had never heard of? Yet nothing about them looked remotely alike. Was this closeness considered normal? The Kremnoan Detachment had been stressing among themselves about it for the past few days.

As the hours passed, Mydei’s efforts were not in vain. Phainon’s complexion had improved significantly compared to when he had collapsed in Mydei’s arms. His vibrancy was returning, and he no longer appeared extremely ill. However, Mydei wished that his pheromones could have also helped with how thin Phainon had become. He made a mental note to arrange a feast for Phainon once he woke up, so he could personally feed him.

The lost muscle would need to be rebuilt afterward, but only until Phainon reached his normal weight again. Mydei appeared extremely serious as he contemplated the training regimen he would implement for Phainon once he woke up.

Although Phainon appeared outwardly the same—tall, handsome, and well-built—Mydei was aware of the hidden changes in Phainon's physique beneath his clothing. Thus, he was genuinely shocked to witness the significant loss of weight over the months.

He suddenly envisioned the thought of Phainon looking up at him with sad eyes, feeling the effect of his physical body’s changes. This image prompted him to shut his eyes in slight annoyance.

“I’ll still love you no matter how you look, HKS.” Mydei sighed with his eyes closed, surprised by his own words. He hadn’t intended to voice that thought, but his imagination had gotten the better of him.

When he opened his eyes, he was taken aback to find bright blue eyes staring at him in equal astonishment.

For a moment, the two stared at each other, unable to discern whether they were truly in reality. Mydei couldn’t even process the embarrassment of his words just now, because he was more stunned at the fact that Phainon was awake now.

It wasn’t until the teary-eyed man from Mydei’s earlier imagination suddenly shot up from the bed and lunged at him with surprising speed that he jolted up from the shock.

Mydei looked at him with crestfallen eyes. He had always believed that it was cruel to promise his return to Phainon, because he truly did not know when, or if, he could return to Ohkema. In his head, he could envision Phainon finding love again and forgetting all about him, a man who couldn’t promise a future with him. But he wasn’t able to truly read Phainon’s thoughts. Before his panicked thoughts could spiral downward again, Mydei firmly placed both hands over Phainon's cheeks. "Hey. Stop doing that."

Now that they were fully imprinted with each other, every fear and worry in their hearts was laid bare to their counterpart. When Phainon began to entertain negative thoughts, Mydei could sense it as well.

Phainon sensed a soothing sensation attempting to calm him, a profound tenderness and love he couldn't quite explain. Was Mydei the source of this feeling? It felt as though Mydei was comforting him directly to his heart.

"Mydei…" Phainon gazed into Mydei's eyes, which were filled with love, even as a laugh escaped Mydei's lips.

He had tried his best to prepare himself for the worst possible outcome, thinking that this would allow him to leave with his head held high. However, now that Mydei had reciprocated his feelings and willingly imprinted with him, he found himself back to being an emotional mess.

The two had spent the last few minutes lovingly entwined in each other's arms, so by the time they finally decided to sit down for breakfast, the coffee and food had already grown cold. But of course that wasn't enough to sour the mood between them.

After finishing their meal, the two were once again glued to each other, unconsciously releasing pheromones that drew them closer. They began discussing what's to come: what their next steps would be, why Phainon should return home for the time being, and how Mydei plans to go back to Ohkema once the nation has stabilized.

Because the two were now mutually imprinted, Phainon would no longer experience the negative effects of prolonged separation. Their bond was now strong enough to endure distance, ensuring that each could still feel the comforting presence of the other.

The two felt anxious because Phainon had not woken up after two days. They wondered if they would have to carry his unconscious body through the gate, missing the opportunity to let Phainon say goodbye. They knew Phainon would be devastated if he woke up back in Ohkema, forced to confront the side effects of the one-sided imprint that would gradually consume him once more.

That explained why Phainon's pheromones were lingering in the air. Although they could feel its presence, the scent itself was still a mystery to them.

However, their celebration was cut a little short as they were more concerned about what would happen next. Their initial worry was that this meant Phainon would not be returning with them to Ohkema so that he could stay by Mydei’s side.

Mydei reassured them that Phainon needed to return with them to Ohkema and that he would figure out his own way back later. As a king now, he had greater authority and power to make decisions regarding this land. It would be challenging, but he felt determined to uphold his love for Phainon.

"Stop being so impatient." Mydei rubbed a hand over Phainon's other cheek. "I just need you to wait for me. Okay?"

"Okay." Phainon responded, leaning in to Mydei's hand.

The sunlight outside the windows had started slowly shifting, signaling that their time together was nearing its end. Despite this, neither of them felt anxious anymore. They understood each other's feelings on a profound level, and this mutual understanding provided them both with a sense of peace.

They knew there would definitely still be a few more hurdles for them to face in the upcoming future, but they no longer felt isolated in their worries and problems. Their destined pair was here in their arms right now, and they were here to stay forever in their hearts.

chapters.title: Chapter 17: Return to Ohkema
chapters.html:
There was a noticeable tension in the air when Mydei and Phainon finally emerged from the king's bedchamber after several days. Back then, Mydei would only occasionally leave when something of utmost importance arose. Otherwise, he preferred to remain inside the bedchamber for anything he could manage on his own, like paperwork.

Nobody seemed willing or brave enough to ask the more pressing question: Why was this foreign man residing in the king's bedchamber? Phainon could have easily been brought to a separate room or the palace's health ward, yet the king himself took the initiative to bring Phainon there.

Of course, the Kremnoan Detachment soon began to question the true identity of the foreigners who had arrived just a few days earlier. It was impossible for any member of the detachment not to recognize who they were, after all.

They had followed Mydeimos for several years, ever since he was a teenager, so it was impossible for no one member of the detachment not to notice these three individuals who stood out significantly.

Unless, of course, their king had encountered them when none of the detachment members could accompany him. The only thought lingering in their minds was about Mydeimos's visit to Ohkema a few months prior.

However, it still did not make any sense to them. The way their king treated and protected this foreign man almost suggested that he was their lover. But this thought did not linger long in the minds of the detachment members.

Because how could that be possible? Mydeimos had only spent a maximum of a week in Ohkema. The man in question was clearly a dominant alpha, yet he seemed no match for the detachment's own Hephaestion, who was also the closest friend of Mydeimos. While this alpha was undeniably handsome and strong, his health raised concerns among the Kremnoans.

The only person they could turn to was Hephaestion to inquire about their king's situation. However, the sickly man in the king's bedchamber emitted unstable pheromones, preventing anyone from approaching. It was strange. Among them were many alphas, yet this foreign man's pheromones were extraordinarily potent and overwhelming. It felt suffocating to anyone who dared to approach with dubious intentions. How could this be?

Mydeimos never voiced his apprehension either, but his actions clearly indicated that he did not want anyone near the bedchamber either. And so the only thing they could do was wait it out until the man named Phainon, who was initially introduced to them as Snowy, would wake up.

In just a few days, Castrum Kremnos underwent significant changes. The entire royal court system was overhauled, and an investigation into the poison used by the advisors was initiated. Soon, many aristocrats fled the nation in haste but were quickly apprehended. Authorities raided an underground lab beneath the castle, leading to the capture of several more criminals for questioning.

A few cowards had even taken their own lives rather than own up to the horrors they had committed against the royal family over the past decades. It was soon discovered that many other members of the royal family were also under the influence of the poison and were approaching the same levels of insanity as Eurypon.

Perdikkas and Ptolemy, along with a group of scholars, initiated their research on the poison in an urgent effort to develop a cure and rescue as many individuals as possible.

While all this was happening, Mydeimos was inundated with documents and paperwork to finalize the changes in their kingdom. Nevertheless, he remained steadfastly by Phainon's side throughout this period. He understood that it was inappropriate for a king to prioritize anything other than his own kingdom, yet he would not deny that he was far more concerned about the man he loved, who had been unconscious for almost three days.

When they finally stepped out of the bedchamber, the detachment members were more tense than ever. How could they not be? Their king was enveloped in unfamiliar pheromones. Although the scent was not apprehensive, the message conveyed by this pheromone shower display was unmistakable.

It also did not help their worries when they could sense their own king's pheromones all over Phainon's body. They knew Mydeimos to be one that never released pheromones haphazardly, and he had incredible control even among deliberate advances on him.

Was this man truly the king's lover?

Despite the obvious dislike that detachment members showed by glaring at the white-haired man, the generals closest to Mydei were mostly unfazed and even approached them with smiles and relief.

Mydeimos might not appear to be the type who readily shares personal details, but he had actually already informed his friends months earlier about his unfinished business back in Ohkema. Without needing to ask, they understood that this signified Mydei had finally found love.

This news was a cause for months of celebration! Their king, who had always been indifferent to love, had finally discovered its sweet embrace!

They were quite annoying for weeks as they tried to pry more information out of Mydei about the maiden who had finally captured his heart back in Ohkema. However, he responded to their inquiries with increasingly curt answers.

It took them placing bets and arguing over an imaginary person before Mydei finally decided to step in. Leonnius and Ptolemy were already at each other's throats, debating what the "perfect omega" companion for Mydei would look like. Meanwhile, Peucesta and Perdikkas were arguing about whether he would prefer a strong-willed personality or a damsel in distress.

When Hephaestion suggested that Mydei's type was more likely to be an alpha, the others laughed at him. However, when they noticed Mydei's somber and shy expression in response to the comment, their jaws dropped in disbelief.

Was this the reason their king never showed interest in the beautiful omega men and women sent to seduce him into his demise? It also explains why he never acknowledged Hephaestion's beauty, except for the occasional platonic remarks he offered to everyone.

This revelation only intensified everyone's curiosity as they pressed for more details about the mysterious alpha from Ohkema. However, their luck began to wane when Mydei finally grew tired of their relentless questioning. Despite their protests, they had no choice but to redirect their focus back to their tasks. Yet, in their eagerness, they inadvertently made Mydei promise to share more details if they succeeded in their missions.

Over the past few months of completing mission after mission, Mydei has offered only a few hints regarding his mysterious lover. He is a man, slightly taller than Mydei, with deep ocean-blue eyes and snowy white hair.

Never mind the notion of them attempting to pry into the man's personality and background, at least they had some semblance of an image of what he looked like. While they each had varying interpretations of his appearance, it was only Hephaestion who quickly recognized all those traits the moment he laid eyes on Phainon.

Hephaestion was the only one who readily welcomed Phainon and his friends into their group, even allowing him to go and see Mydei's fight against Eurypon. He wanted to keep the surprise under wraps for now, especially since tensions were still running high, but he was eagerly anticipating collecting his winnings from the bets.

"It's an honor to finally meet you, my lord!" Ptolemy grinned slyly at Mydei while shaking Phainon's hand.

"Apologies for my earlier rudeness, my lord." Leonnius stepped closer and began to pat Phainon on the shoulder.

"It must have been difficult for you these past few days. Don’t worry! We’ll be here to help you as much as we can, brother-in-law!" Peucesta spoke up, catching Phainon's attention while the others were distracted.

"That's enough." Mydei warned them all to back off.

They all stepped back simultaneously, returning to their previous positions at attention, wearing pouts and murmuring quiet protests.

"They'll be returning to Ohkema today." Mydei explained as he continued walking while Phainon trailed close by behind him.

The five generals initially nodded in understanding, but their expressions quickly shifted to shock. "Huh???" It was no surprise they were taken aback. This man, who had appeared out of nowhere and coincidentally arrived just in time for their victory, was now planning to leave so abruptly? Wasn't he meant to be their king's consort? Where could he possibly be going?

Hyacine and Castorice arrived, quickly wrapping their arms around Phainon in a tight group hug. They had been worried sick over the past few days, dreading the thought of forcing Phainon to return without ever having the chance to speak with Mydei.

But the third day had arrived, and evening was approaching. Although Phainon had just woken up, they needed to pass through the Tribios gate once more. This time, however, they departed with good news and light hearts.

Explanations for the rest of the Kremnoan Detachment would need to wait as the king, the generals, and the three foreigners set off for an unknown location. Fortunately, the gate was specially designed so that only the three who had previously entered could see it and pass through.

Phainon felt a wave of sadness at the thought of leaving so soon. They had just mutually imprinted and professed their love for each other, yet now he was preparing to depart. If it weren't for Mydei's anger over his suggestion to stay, he would have been waving goodbye to Castorice and Hyacine without a second thought.

But he recognized that it would be selfish of him to stay, especially with so much at stake if they failed to return together. It would already be remarkable if those back in Ohkema were able to successfully conceal the fact that all three of them had been missing for the past few days.

Trying to protest against Mydei was also out of the question since the Kremnoan king was so good at reassuring Phainon with his pheromones and the effect of the imprint.

When they finally arrived at the gate, Phainon gripped Mydei with anxiety. However, the calming wave released by Mydei through the imprint was enough to reassure him. To give the two some space, the rest of the party moved ahead and exchanged words of thanks with one another.

"Maybe I should schedule another time to come back here," Phainon suggested quietly. "I don't know if we can manage it another time, but perhaps in a week? Two weeks? One month? Please?" His suggestions kept extending further into the future as he noticed Mydei's disapproving gaze.

"This time, I will be the one to come to you, okay?" Mydei said gently. "What you really need to focus on is yourself. I expect you to eat three meals a day and train hard to get back into shape. Otherwise, how will you keep up with me?"

Phainon blushed a little at the last remark, which earned him a light smack on the arm from Mydei.

The sun was now just above the horizon, casting a bright light on the gate that was visible to the three of them. Phainon found it challenging to be affectionate toward Mydei in front of others. What if Mydei didn’t appreciate public displays of affection? It would be quite inconsiderate for him to suddenly ask for a goodbye kiss from their king in such a setting.

All he could do was awkwardly bow to Mydei before turning on his heel and walking toward the gate. He didn’t want to glance back and risk being unable to pass through, so he figured it was best to keep moving.

But he felt a firm hand grip his arm and pull him back. A sudden peck on his lips was all it took for Phainon's face to flush red. He was then gently pushed forward until he passed through the gate.

Chapter End Notes

Slightly shorter chapter because I ended up getting sick from the trip. But I’m getting a little better now!

As mentioned before, I’ll be holding some polls and stuff on twitter soon. Made a new one so that it’s fully dedicated to Phaidei! so for those who want to participate, it’ll be at @ackivili

chapters.title: Chapter 18: Royal Announcement
chapters.html:
Before Phainon was pushed through the gate, Castorice and Hyacine had already gone ahead. Phainon felt so distraught that he didn't even get the chance to pull Mydei into another kiss himself. However, he had no opportunity to voice this complaint after passing through the gate, as he suddenly found himself facing multiple Ohkeman soldiers, along with Castorice and Hyacine.

The chamber where Tribios resided was now crowded with over a dozen Ohkeman soldiers, who appeared to be expecting the three of them to arrive. Phainon scanned the area but was unable to locate his other companions, including the triplets.

"Welcome back to Ohkema, your highness. We are here to escort you to Her Majesty, the Imperator," announced one of the higher-ranking soldiers as he approached. "Miss Hyacinthia and Miss Castorice will be taken to a separate chamber for the time being."

Phainon instinctively moved in front of the two ladies and shielded them from the approaching soldiers.

Hyacine reached out to Phainon's arm, speaking softly to reassure him. "It's alright, Lord Phainon. I'm sure it will be fine." Castorice echoed her sentiment, also assuring Phainon that they would be okay.

As Phainon stepped back, concern etched on his face, his two friends were led out of the chamber first. He cast a glare at the soldiers who signaled for him to follow. While he had no doubt that Hyacine and Castorice could handle themselves, he couldn't shake the guilt that he was the reason this situation was unfolding.

He should have realized that the Imperator would eventually discover their absence. They had been gone for three entire days, after all. While Hyacine and Castorice might have managed to evade Her Majesty's notice, Phainon was a heavily influential individual, even though he lived alone in his own estate.

"Please do not worry, your highness. We assure you that your companions are unharmed. The Imperator simply wishes to speak with you alone," the soldier beside him said to inform him.

Phainon was unsure if he could trust this information. However, he has no reason to disbelieve them either. It was his fault they were in this situation, but he hopes that the good news he brings of Mydei's ascension as king will be enough to appease Cerydra's anger.

The walk to the throne room was brief, as it was already close to the residence of the Tribios. Phainon entered the room alone, while the knights who had escorted him remained to guard the entrance.

Phainon strode forward with confidence, despite the intense anxiety that gripped him. Just as he began to feel nauseous, a sudden wave of calm and reassurance washed over him. He couldn't help but smile, knowing that even from this distance, Mydei could still comfort him in this way.

"I hope that smile means you have good news, Phainon." Cerydra's voice echoed from above the throne chamber, resonating down the steps. With only them present in the room, the curtain that usually concealed the Imperator was drawn aside, revealing the figure seated on the throne.

Phainon quickly bowed and knelt on one knee to show his respects, but Cerydra waved him off, indicating that such gestures were unnecessary. "Spare me the pleasantries. Are you here to deliver news of Castrum Kremnos or not?"

"Mydeimos has successfully claimed the throne, your Majesty. Castrum Kremnos is being rebuilt as we speak," Phainon said as he rose from his position.

"What of Eurypon?"

"He has been slain, as are the rules of their throne succession."

"Good. That was quicker than I expected. Still, I can't help but wonder if your presence there influenced the outcome." Cerydra's voice resonated with curiosity.

"Certainly not, your Majesty. The honor belongs solely to Mydeimos, and accepting any external assistance would render their battle a mockery."

"Interesting." She leaned back in her chair and crossed her legs. "If that is the case, then pray tell why you chose to disobey protocol and take a little trip to Castrum Kremnos?"

Phainon looked up, hoping the sincerity in his voice would come through. "It's entirely my fault, your Majesty. The Tribios, Hyacine, and Castorice—none of them are to blame. I selfishly wanted to visit Mydeimos."

"Why should I believe you?" Her words sliced through the air like a knife at Phainon's throat. One misstep could cost him everything.

"Because I selfishly performed a one-sided imprint on Mydeimos last year," Phainon admitted, his gaze dropping in shame.

He could hear a sigh from the throne chamber above, and he closed his eyes, bracing himself for the punishment he expected for going against the Imperator. Instead, he felt a sudden flick on his forehead.

In shock, he opened his eyes to see that it was Cerydra herself who had flicked him.

"Truth be told, Phainon, I am not upset that you went behind my back to travel to Castrum Kremnos, nor am I upset that you attempted a one-sided imprint on Mydeimos," Cerydra said, her voice tinged with a feigned sigh as she paced in front of him. "Why did you never approach me?"

Phainon was taken aback by the last question. What could he possibly say in response? How could he dare approach the Imperator? His actions were certainly not befitting of a noble with a questionable background. What could he possibly bring to the Imperator's attention?

"Have you forgotten who it was that brought you to Ohkema all those years ago?"

"Of course not, your Majesty! You rescued me from the black tide and gave me the chance to live here." Phainon eagerly responded.

"Exactly, Phainon. I was the one who brought you here, clothed you, granted you a title, and trained you into the person you are today. Yet, why do I never hear a word from you?"

The question took Phainon by surprise. It took him a moment to truly grasp and understand what Cerydra was talking about. Phainon was a collateral member of the royal family, and by title, he is directly positioned under Cerydra's lineage, albeit not receiving succession rights by law. He was also someone who worked closely with Cerydra and followed her directives for most of his life.

Despite this close working relationship, he never took the time to speak with Cerydra outside of reports and official meetings. He had always maintained a boundary, believing it was necessary due to their respective positions, but he was surprised to realize that this boundary did not exist for the Imperator.

But it was not entirely unheard of. How could Phainon, an outsider, act like family? Even now, as he pondered this, he wondered if he was misunderstanding the situation. Was he interpreting this incorrectly?

"Anaxagoras and Aglaea informed me about your condition that led to your illness over the past few months. Why didn't I hear about this sooner?" She crossed her arms, her brows furrowed as she awaited his response. "You were so ill that all of Ohkema was in an uproar over your broken heart after losing your fiancé. Aglaea was working tirelessly to find a way to appease the masses."

"Please forgive me, your Majesty. My lack of awareness led me to make terrible decisions." He apologized, but he realized that this was not what Cerydra wanted to hear. "I did not wish to burden you with my stupidity and cowardice."

Cerydra looked up at him with narrowed eyes and an unimpressed expression, anticipating that Phainon would provide a more satisfactory answer than that.

"Had you informed me of the events from months ago, I would have modified our plans for aid to Castrum Kremnos." Cerydra huffed quietly, her annoyance evident at the unfolding situation. "Do I appear unworthy of offering you counsel?"

"Of course not, Your Majesty!" Phainon replied without hesitation, though confusion began to creep in. This behavior was unlike the Imperator, yet it also felt distinctly like her.

After further discussion, during which Phainon had to pledge to improve his "reporting" to the Imperator, he was finally permitted to leave and join his friends.

It felt a bit strange for him to suddenly speak more informally to Cerydra, yet he sensed that their relationship was becoming closer, reminiscent of a younger brother receiving a scolding. He never anticipated such a reaction from Cerydra, yet it seems logical in hindsight. After all, most of Phainon's life in Ohkema has been quite uneventful.

Whenever he was summoned to obey commands, he completed them successfully and without complaint. When required to study in the Grove, he also finished his studies, completing them with flying colors.

Phainon's actions in Ohkema were neither unusual nor driven by his own desires. He was there to express gratitude and to stay out of the spotlight as a noble with impure blood. It was only recently that he discovered something, someone he wanted for himself and wished to protect, which finally broke him out of his monotonous thinking.

He realized that he had never spoken with Cerydra during those grueling months of his illness. Not a single word of complaint or anguish to ask for help. This was not something any noble, regardless of their position in the palace, could allow themselves to do.

"You are under my wing now. No one in this nation shall ever question your history." Those were the words that echoed in his mind when he first arrived in Ohkema, and he would remember those words for the rest of his life.

Perhaps it was at that moment that Cerydra truly considered him part of her family. She was a ruthless, often cruel tyrant who held power and influence throughout Amphoreus, but for the briefest moment, Phainon could see her as family too.

Phainon was escorted to the hall where all his friends were gathered and kept while he spoke with the Imperator. When the doors opened, the people inside got up immediately and rushed to him with worried faces.

Aglaea was the first to reach out to him, pulling everyone into a group hug. Even Anaxa and Cipher, who typically shunned close contact with others, joined in briefly for the reunion.

They asked about what happened with Cerydra, wondering if any of them were going to be in trouble for going against her orders. But Phainon reassured them that everything was fine.

Given that Mydei successfully claimed the throne in Castrum Kremnos, Cerydra indicated she was willing to overlook their insubordination and pretend it was all part of the plan. They felt a wave of relief wash over them upon hearing this news, allowing them to finally relax once more.

"Hmph. I figured at least one of us would end up beheaded soon. That woman never lets treasonous actions slide so easily." Cipher remarked while casually stretching on the table she leaned against.

"Cifera," Aglaea warned, gesturing toward the door where knights might be listening from outside.

"What? It's true, though. I bet it's because Phainon is her favorite child, so she's letting us all off easy."

"Snowy, you look much healthier now." Trianne said, trying to ease the tension. He reached over to pat him on the shoulder while Phainon was sitting down. "Can you tell us about your trip?"

For the remainder of the evening, the group took time to catch up on the events of the past few days. They were even surprisingly treated to a small welcome feast in the hall where they were being kept.

The night continued until their stomachs were full and every story had been shared. When they were ready to leave, Phainon expressed his gratitude to them once more. Without their support over the past few months, he wouldn’t have been able to reunite with Mydei, nor would he have survived the initial months when the effects of the imprint were taking a toll on him.

Given that he appeared healthier and happier now, everyone felt reassured about allowing him to return home alone without concern. The walk there felt quite solemn, as it was very late into the night. However, nothing could diminish the smile that was fixed on his face.

His estate needed some tidying up here and there, but everything was generally in order and left as he remembered it. Still, he couldn't shake the feeling that something was amiss. It didn't seem to make sense given his position, but it felt as though someone had been following him during his walk home.

He would rather not make a fuss about it, especially since he was exhausted and wanted nothing more than to rest. He reasoned that Aglaea had likely instructed Cipher to follow him home. So, he simply pretended not to notice anything unusual.

The rest of the night passed without incident as Phainon finally enjoyed the long-awaited bath he had missed. He went straight to bed and did not stir until the sun rose high enough in the sky to wake him.

Phainon was in such high spirits that he decided to go for a morning jog and even visit the Mamoreal market to buy some food. It had been months since he had last been there, and even longer since he had the opportunity to buy and cook a proper meal at home. He recalled his promise to Mydei about getting back into shape before their next meeting, so he needed to act quickly. He didn't know how soon Mydei might arrive, so he didn't have an opportunity to slack off.

His clothes felt noticeably loose on him, which heightened his eagerness to exercise and train throughout the day. It was remarkable how differently he felt now compared to just a few days ago. The energy that had drained from him surged back like a powerful wave.

Even his stamina and overall mood had improved drastically, and he could even say that he felt stronger than how he originally was. The vibe he exuded was certainly noticed by all the citizens he passed.

The people who had been searching for him and gossiping about his absence over the past few months were, quite frankly, shocked. The beloved noble had returned! Where had he been? His complexion looked so much healthier! He was smiling again! What had happened?

In no time at all, the local papers were filled with news about Phainon's return to the public eye. Those who had a chance to speak with him briefly in the market shared how the young lord appeared to be a new man. The streets were once again alive with excitement, and everyone had countless questions to ask. However, there was one question that many were eager to pose but couldn’t.

Has Phainon finally gotten over his failed engagement?

Although it was never truly confirmed by Phainon, the timeline in which he experienced a beautiful romance, only to be abruptly separated from the love of his life, was so evident that everyone just assumed it was true. They watched as the beloved noble, cherished by the public, deteriorated and fell ill with grief.

Some even feared that they might soon receive tragic news of his passing, given how dire his condition had become. However, he was now reappearing with a surprising sense of happiness and vitality.

Perhaps after all those months of heartache, Phainon had finally let it go. Or maybe he had found a new lover?

The gossiping all across Ohkema was reaching new heights. Who could possibly capture the heart of the young lord again after months of sadness?

"I heard a young doctor from the Grove has been seen frequently coming in and out of Lord Phainon's residence. She was also spotted with him before, back when they studied together," one of the aunties at the market chimed in.

"Oh my! No wonder he looked like he was healing well from illness."

"No, no. I heard that Lady Castorice was also seen recently visiting Lord Phainon's estate while carrying some baskets of fruits and vegetables. Can you imagine that? Like a wife bringing home groceries, no?"

"That's true. She is also of noble blood, right? She's a high priestess from Aidonia, after all."

"No, that doesn't make any sense! What if it's someone entirely new? Lord Phainon has never shown interest in them before, so why now? The only time we've seen him truly infatuated was when he proposed to one of those Kremnoans." The aunty suddenly gasped, "What if a new bride has finally been sent from Castrum Kremnos?"

The gasps and arguments echoed throughout the market. Every stall owner, every child, and every traveling merchant were all discussing the new love that had captured Phainon's heart.

It was not until a crier arrived at the entrance of the Mamoreal palace and called for everyone's attention that the buzzing conversations halted. The crier took out a scroll marked with an official seal from Castrum Kremnos, with a golden signet ring dangling from the rope that secured the scroll.

Hysilens and Aglaea stood atop the steps, waiting to receive the message from Castrum Kremnos. They suspected it was likely an official announcement regarding Mydeimos' ascension to the throne, so they did not appear surprised by the arrival.

But nothing could have prepared the nation of Ohkema for the announcement that was about to unfold.

"Hear ye! Hear ye! Hear ye! By royal proclamation and with joy resounding through all of Amphoreus, let it be known to all good citizens of this noble land that a most illustrious proposal of union hath been declared to his royal highness, Lord Phainon of Ohkema!"

Aglaea's mouth was agape upon hearing the announcement. "Is this a marriage proposal?"

Chapter End Notes

God pls take all my period cramps and give it to Lygus.

I hope Cerydra isn’t too OOC here. This story was planned waaaay before the new patch so I actually have no idea how she is actually like, and I also haven’t had the time to play the new main story yet. I did manage to pull for Cerydra tho! My Phainon is too greedy with supports.

chapters.title: Chapter 19: Unexpected Visitor
chapters.html:
Chapter Notes

TW: drugging (nothing graphic)

Within an hour after the announcement that echoed across Ohkema, the once bustling streets filled with gossip became even more chaotic as people reacted in shock. How could there suddenly be a marriage proposal presented to Lord Phainon out of nowhere? And this time, there is no option for him to choose as well? This seems especially sudden, considering Phainon had just recovered from his illness.

What will happen to Phainon's new love, the one who helped him heal during his illness? Is he now on the verge of being torn away from the happiness he has found all over again?

This was the topic of conversation for the Ohkeman people throughout the week following the announcement. During this time, Phainon remained confined to his estate, asked by the palace to avoid the need to explain the situation and exacerbate the public outcry.

"How audacious of Castrum Kremnos to present such a proposal! Aren't they supposed to offer brides first, as they have in the past? This seems very disrespectful, don't you think?" The aunties in the Mamoreal markets were all abuzz with the news now.

"Exactly! There is no way the Imperator will not take offense to such an insolent display."

"What of Lord Phainon? Has anyone seen the young lad again this week?"

"I believe the palace is hiding him once more," the merchant passing by said. "The man has endured enough, yet he continues to get swept up in these love affairs. I feel sorry for the boy."

"It’s moments like this that really highlight the struggles that we common folk would never understand. Just think about having to be passed around for the sake of politics."

"Why can't Lord Mydeimos just come back?" A small voice spoke up. The large group of elders turned to see a group of children gazing up at them with sorrowful expressions. These were the same kids who had played with Mydei and Phainon at the markets last year.

"We still don’t know what happened or why he was taken away. Who knows? Maybe Lord Mydeimos himself proposed!" One auntie suggested cheerfully, hoping to lift the spirits of the young children.

Although they knew it was highly unlikely, they couldn't help but hope that Phainon was coping with the news better than they were.

Unbeknownst to them, Phainon was pacing in his home like a frantic bee. He was filled with panic and anxiety, stumbling around as he tried to gather items scattered all over the house. Why wouldn't he be worried? In a month's time, Mydei was set to return to Ohkema, and his house was in complete disarray!

His belief that the estate didn't look too awful the other day was merely a lie for himself to justify his neglect of cleaning for the past months. Now, Phainon was frantically rearranging everything in sight as he scrubbed away the dust and grime he had long ignored.

He was sweating and panting as he lifted various books and antique items scattered throughout the house. First, he needed to move them elsewhere to clean the living room. However, every other room was just as dirty!

Just thinking about the need to scrub every tile and glass surface in the baths was already giving him a headache. This could have all been avoided if he had simply accepted the help of the palace maid staff while he was sick. Aglaea had been insistent back then, when Phainon could barely get out of bed. However, not wanting to inconvenience anyone, especially due to his unstable pheromones, he had firmly rejected the idea.

Maybe he could ask for help now? No, Phainon thought. His stubbornness would surely be his downfall.

Forget about working out all day to regain his strength. He was now determined to clean every corner of his house by himself until he collapsed yet again!

In the evenings, he would only take a short rest and rise early, before the sky even began to lighten, to train in his courtyard. He would run a few laps around the estate, followed by strength training with his swords. He was meticulously focused on every detail, determined to impress Mydei as soon as his beloved arrived.

To his friends who visited him occasionally, they felt both worried and impressed by the daunting feats Phainon was accomplishing, all to avoid being a burden to others. Despite the numerous complaints from both Aglaea and Hyacine, Phainon was surprisingly taking good care of himself, making it appear as though he was doing just fine.

They still managed to send a gardener to assist Phainon with cleaning up the outside of the manor. As long as no one entered the house itself, Phainon felt relatively comfortable with it.

The days were passing quickly, yet Phainon felt it still wasn't enough time to prepare. Although his physique had improved significantly over the past few weeks, he still felt a bit self-conscious about showing himself to Mydei.

However, he missed his beloved so much that he was glad he would finally see Mydei again in just a few more days.

He was already thinking of plans for how he would greet Mydei upon his return. Perhaps he would ask the gardener to prepare a beautiful bouquet of flowers for him. Oh, and making a reservation at the restaurant where they first dined a year ago would also be a wonderful idea for the evening.

Phainon found himself constantly reaching for the gold signet ring he had tied back around his neck. In the past, when he held the ring in the same way, he was filled with hopelessness, uncertain if he would ever see his first love again. However, now that the ring had been returned to him, it felt like a promise. He knew he would finally have the opportunity to propose in the way he had always wanted.

Of course, there were still a few hiccups along the way, such as the Imperator's lack of enthusiasm regarding the sudden marriage proposal sent to Ohkema via a crier. There were still many things to consider, as Mydei was now a king of a foreign land indebted to Ohkema. It would cause complete chaos in the royal court if they discovered that their own nobility now appeared to be an offering to Castrum Kremnos.

Although Aglaea reassured Phainon not to worry, explaining that she was collaborating with her inner circle to find a way to bypass the law in favor of Phainon and Mydei's union, it was truly going to be a challenge. Phainon remained grateful for all the assistance he was receiving, even as he struggled with the feeling that he did not deserve any of it.

In the present time, the royal carriages of Castrum Kremnos were set to arrive in Ohkema again within a week. Phainon found himself practicing day and night on how to woo his beloved. He was so distracted that he jumped at the sudden sound of knocking on his front door.

He hadn't anticipated any visitors today, but he was accustomed to his friends dropping by to check on him from time to time. However, when he opened the door, he was met with an unfamiliar face.

"Good day, your highness." A lady dressed in the attire of the palace maids, who serve the royal court, stood before him. "Her highness, Aglaea, has sent me to deliver some nutritional supplements to you."

"That's odd," Phainon thought to himself. Typically, it was Hyacine who delivered his medicine personally, and he couldn't recall Aglaea ever mentioning anything like this before. Nevertheless, he smiled and thanked the maid as he took the small package from her.

The maid bowed to him briefly before departing. He felt a slight discomfort when she had looked at him earlier, believing it was because she was an omega attempting to leave her scent on the package.

This wasn't the first time omega men and women had tried to get close to him by using their scents to entice him. Yet, every attempt always ended the same: he was visibly disgusted by such acts. Using underhanded tactics like that might work on other alphas who didn't care about their nightly affairs, but Phainon simply found no other scents enticing at all.

The fact that this package now reeked of that woman's scent disturbed him deeply. He might need to report this to Aglaea soon, as such behavior was simply unacceptable, especially for palace staff.

He sighed and made his way to the kitchen to inspect the package. It could be that he had expressed his concerns to Aglaea the other week about not being in peak physical condition yet, so she might have decided to procure for him some supplements to assist him in his training.

The package was small and tightly wrapped in paper. The folds and adhesive made it difficult for him to open. After several attempts to unwrap it carefully, Phainon grew frustrated and decided to simply rip it open.

But this decision proved to be a grave mistake. A sudden, pungent smell wafted directly into his face as a thick, musky smoke escaped from the package, quickly enveloping the air around him. The odor was suffocating—a powerful blend of packed rotten flowers mixed with something distinctly unfamiliar. He dropped the package, desperately fanning the air around him in an attempt to find space to breathe.

What was in that package? There was no way Aglaea would send something so disgusting. Phainon coughed as he struggled to escape the kitchen. His throat felt tight from the awful odor, and he was already starting to feel disoriented.

"Something's wrong…" He coughed, grasping at his neck in an attempt to relieve the suffocating sensation, only to realize that his temperature was suddenly rising.

He needed to act quickly, as his eyes were becoming heavy and his mind felt foggy. He hurried to the door and stepped outside the manor, desperate for fresh, clean air to fill his lungs. However, the moment he exited, a different, overpowering smell assaulted him.

It was the maid from earlier again. She reached out to him, covering him with her pheromones.

A sudden rage surged through Phainon as he pushed her away, but his condition was becoming increasingly alarming. The heat he had felt in his throat earlier was now spreading through his body. An insatiable hunger overwhelmed his senses, leaving him feeling physically weak.

"Your Highness, let me assist you," the woman said with a smile, moving closer to him again and trying to intensify her pheromones. "I can help you feel better."

Phainon felt increasingly lightheaded. The strong scent of smoke from earlier now mingled with the woman's repugnant pheromones. Any other alpha might have succumbed to her advances by now, but his unique temperament kept him immune to her influence.

He resisted her touch once more, pushing himself away to create distance between them. With all his willpower, he stumbled backward, scanning the area to look for something.

It was becoming increasingly difficult for him to maintain his balance as the searing pain in his stomach threatened to make him double over. This sensation was unfamiliar to him. Had he not endured the torturous effects of the imprint for months prior, he would have already lost consciousness.

The woman was cautious, watching intently and smiling as the man before her struggled for his life. She understood that it wouldn’t be long before he was knocked out.

A golden glint in Phainon's eye finally signaled that he had found what he was looking for. One of Aglaea's nymphs was nearby!

He recalled her saying previously that if he ever needed assistance, she had a nymph waiting outside his manor. He sprinted toward the location of the nymph, but the woman attempted to block his path once again.

The maid continued to speak to him in her best sultry voice, but Phainon's mind was too foggy to comprehend her words. Summoning all his strength, he pushed through and reached the nymph. He grabbed the golden bug tightly and squeezed it, managing only a weak cry, "Agy..."

As his consciousness began to slip away, he stumbled to the ground, and the woman wrapped her arms around his hunched figure. "Don't worry, your Highness. I'll take care of everything."

Phainon's eyes were already closing by the time he heard sounds of footsteps quickly approaching them. He couldn't recall what happened next, but he at least felt safe as soon as he heard Cipher's loud voice calling out to him.

He couldn't believe this was happening to him again. How many times was he going to be weakened into a state of passing out? The first time was definitely his fault, but now he was being targeted like this.

Even as he lay on the cold, hard pavement, his thoughts were consumed by Mydei. He hoped he would regain consciousness in time to still be able to prepare for Mydei's arrival.

In his deep sleep, he could only hear faint voices around him, but they were too distant to decipher. He couldn't determine how much time had passed. However, he was vaguely aware that he had been moved to a soft bed at least.

The voices surrounding him were familiar, which eased his distress.

He felt an overwhelming sense of fatigue and lacked the desire to wake up just yet. A sharp pain throbbed in his upper arm, a lingering effect of the medication that Anaxa had administered to him earlier.

"Has the perpetrator still not been found?" Anaxa asked, arms crossed, as he looked up at Aglaea and Castorice, who were standing on the opposite side of the bed.

"No." Aglaea replied with a sigh. "Cipher tried to go after her when she escaped, but Phainon was convulsing on the ground. She needed to attend to him first and make sure he was okay. The palace guards are now on high alert with the description that Cipher provided. I also have multiple nymphs on standby waiting to hear any news."
