Mydei sensed that something was wrong. Whenever he felt the connection between himself and Phainon, he could effortlessly release a reassuring wave, which usually calmed Phainon down instantly. However, this time, he could physically feel that something was amiss.

Phainon was no longer responding to the signals from their imprint, and it almost felt as if Mydei could sense some level of pain. While the pain wasn't strong enough for him to fully acknowledge it, it was enough to leave him feeling very uncomfortable.

But the most troubling aspect was that this feeling continued to intensify, causing him to worry that something awful had happened to Phainon once more. He sighed and repeatedly urged the dromas coachman to quicken the pace of their journey.

He couldn't believe it had only been around two months since they parted, yet something was happening again. If this continues, Mydei would seriously consider kidnapping the man and bringing him along everywhere they go. He knew it was unrealistic, but this was already the second time it had occurred whenever they separated.

"Is something wrong? Why are we in a hurry?" Hephaestion knocked on the carriage's window. He switched carriages to inquire about the sudden change of plans. Mydei usually never deviated from plans unexpectedly, especially when it meant the Kremnoan party would have to forgo a night's rest and continue traveling until they reached Ohkema.

If they stuck to their plans, they would arrive the next day in the afternoon. However, given their current pace, it wouldn’t be surprising if they arrived by dawn instead.

"Something happened," Mydei responded, opening the door to let Hephaestion in to sit. "I never really learned much about imprinting, but ever since I did so with Phainon, we have been able to sense each other's moods to some extent."

"I see. I believe I heard about it briefly in school, but I can't be sure since imprinting isn't very common in Castrum Kremnos. What's going on? Is he anxious?"

Mydei shook his head, a visible frown on his face. "At first, it was just discomfort, but now it… it feels painful." He struggled to articulate his thoughts and found it difficult to express such an emotional experience as this.

Hephaestion's eyes widened in concern. "Painful? Are you alright, your majesty? Should I call for Perdikkas?"

"I'm alright. It just feels uncomfortable to me, but I have a terrible feeling that Phainon is in pain right now." Mydei sighed in frustration. "Our messenger falcon has already confirmed through Ohkema that there are no conflicts on their land and that it is safe for us to arrive. So it can't be that Phainon is involved in battle."

"Could he be ill again? He looked quite unwell when he first arrived at Castrum Kremnos."

"I doubt that. His previous illness was a result of the one-sided imprint."

"One-sided imprint?" Hephaestion gasped, covering his mouth in shock. Mydei realized he shouldn’t have mentioned it, as it would only lead to more questions and pestering from the detachment generals. "I knew you two were in love, but wow!"

Mydei cleared his throat, trying to hide his embarrassment. "At this point, I would prefer he be ill with the last cold winds of winter, as we near the start of spring. But I sense it's more serious than that. I can feel it."

The journey to Ohkema was fraught with tension, as the entire Kremnoan party remained confused about why they were in a hurry to reach the foreign kingdom ahead of schedule. However, no warrior from their kingdom would ever confess to feeling weary from the restless travel, so they pressed on without complaint.

As expected, the walls of Ohkema came into view with the break of dawn, and torches were lit by the Ohkeman knights to guide the arriving carriages through the kingdom gates.

Throughout the journey, Mydei had been growing increasingly worried and distressed, experiencing nothing but discomfort and pain from his connection with Phainon. He needed answers urgently but was met with only one familiar face, but not the one he longed to see.

"Welcome to Ohkema, Your Majesty Mydeimos of Castrum Kremnos," the woman greeted him formally as he stepped out of the carriage. Mydei recognized her as Aglaea, the woman with the golden threads. Although their first meeting had been tense, he knew that she was a close ally of Phainon.

"Something happened. Where is he?" Mydei wanted to remain courteous, but he could already feel a stinging pain in the pit of his stomach now that he was inside Ohkema. There was no more room for him to beat around the bush.

"Hysilens, please escort the Kremnoan party to their quarters and make sure they are properly settled." Aglaea gestured toward her first before turning her focus back to Mydei. "Please follow me, your majesty."

It felt strange for Mydei to be addressed by such a prestigious title after living as an exiled prince for most of his life, but he was aware of the importance of not undermining his new status among nations. He needed to leverage his position if he hoped to execute his plans successfully in the months ahead. Initially, he found it a bit uncomfortable, but now it filled him with a sense of pride for his nation, which was currently being rebuilt.

The generals standing behind Mydeimos were preparing to join him but were interrupted by Hysilens. "Dear guests, we apologize for the discourteous behavior, but we can only speak to His Majesty Mydeimos alone."

Their expressions soured, and they seemed ready to protest, but Mydeimos swiftly intervened. "Please rest well for now. I will return after my business is concluded." His tone was resolute, leaving no room for debate.

Hysilens respectfully bowed to Mydeimos before returning to her duty of escorting the remainder of the Kremnoan party. Aglaea then began to lead Mydei into the palace. However, instead of proceeding directly to Phainon's estate, they took a detour toward the palace's medical wing.

Mydei's anxiety was clearly etched on his face, yet he made an effort to remain patient as he followed Aglaea. Upon reaching the room, Mydei swiftly scanned the area for Phainon, but the man was not among those present.

"Where is he?" Mydei asked for the second time.

"Please allow us to recount what happened. It would be best if you were aware of the whole situation." Aglaea offered him a seat at the long table where Anaxa and Hyacine were already seated.

As a prince surrounded by many foes over the years, Mydei had become adept at maintaining a stoic expression and a calm demeanor. He was not one to rush into battle unprepared and typically did not allow his emotions to cloud his judgment. Even now, as he listened to the horrifying details of the events that had transpired days earlier, his expression remained almost unchanged. Yet, the growing strength and intensity of the pheromones he began to emit made it clear to everyone present that he was furious.

"My warriors can assist you in the search efforts. They are highly skilled in espionage and adept at locating potential hiding places for criminals," Mydei said as soon as Aglaea finished speaking.

"Thank you, your Majesty. Your warriors will be invaluable in our search for the perpetrator. Since the incident, Ohkema has been under lockdown, and we are quite certain that the suspect remains within the city."

"How is Phainon doing? May I go see him?" he asked without hesitation.

"I'm afraid it might be difficult to see him right now," Anaxa finally interjected from across the table. "As you may already know, Phainon possesses a very unique trait that is so rare that not many studies have been conducted to document such phenomena."

"He mentioned it in passing in the past. So it's true?"

"Yes. He is an enigma, potentially the rarest trait we know of among our secondary genders. With that in mind, I'm sure you've noticed that he has extremely strong pheromones that can sometimes come across as very aggressive toward others." Anaxa continued explaining, "Because of this, whenever his rut comes along, he manages to erect a very powerful barrier of pheromones that guards his location, making it difficult for even the most dominant of alphas to approach."

Hyacine nodded in agreement and began to speak as well. "Typically, alphas in rut can receive medication or spend their cycle with partners to alleviate it. However, Phainon has created a situation where absolutely nobody can approach him. His pheromones are already quite daunting to others on a normal day, but during his rut, they have caused even our most experienced knights to collapse when attempting to get close."

"And this is where I must express my deepest apologies, your majesty," Aglaea spoke up. "Phainon's ruts typically last at least one month, but due to the rut inducer, there have been unexpected changes, and it is possible that his rut may extend beyond that."

"Since his first rut as a young adult, he has spent it in deep sleep. However, we now believe he is fully awake and experiencing the rut without any available medication."

Mydei listened intently to all their explanations, but something still troubled him. "You mention that Phainon's pheromones are unpleasant, yet I don't recall ever detecting such a scent from him." He began to recount his previous conversation with Phainon regarding this matter, noting how he actually found the scent to be calming and welcoming.

"How unexpected," Anaxa mused, deep in thought. "Given the timeline of events, it appears you were not yet imprinted with one another at that time."

"Perhaps it is fate!" Hyacine grinned.

"Then that would make things easier! Would you like to help us conduct an experiment, your Majesty?" Anaxa suggested, but Aglaea quickly interrupted. She shot him a warning glance.

"Relax." Anaxa waved her off. "Over the past two days, I have been perfecting a drug that may help alleviate Phainon's rut. This formula is more potent and specifically designed for an enigma. However, since no one can approach him, injecting it will not be possible. Unless… his Majesty is able to do so."

"Your Majesty, please ignore him. This is not your responsibility."

"I'll do it. I just need to get close to him and inject him with it, right?" Mydei was quick to respond in agreement, and Anaxa could not help but break into a big smile and laugh loudly by himself.

"Excellent!" Anaxa exclaimed.

"There are potential dangers, Your Majesty. As I have explained, no one else possesses the ability to get close and intervene if something goes wrong." Aglaea made a concerted effort to regain control of the situation. "I cannot permit this if it puts Castrum Kremnos' monarch at risk."

"I've faced many trials throughout my life since my exile, so I am not one to shy away from such a challenge," Mydei said with pride. "Moreover, Phainon is my imprinted pair. Every moment I sit here, I can feel a pulsing discomfort in the pit of my stomach, which I can only assume is pain from him. If there is even a small chance that I can help alleviate that pain, I will do it."

"Still," Aglaea said firmly, "I will need to speak with the Imperator on this matter first. I cannot make this decision alone." It wasn't that she didn't want to help Phainon. Everyone here was clearly concerned for him. They had spent the last few days tirelessly searching for the culprit and researching medicine that could assist Phainon during his rut cycle. However, Aglaea could not overlook the fact that Mydei was not an ordinary citizen. He was a king from another country, and the risks involved were too dangerous to ignore.

"Then you can go do that while I explain to His Majesty here how to use the medicine properly, along with the preparations for emergency measures." Anaxa stood up to fetch the medication.

Aglaea still looked visibly stressed, giving a slight bow to Mydei before turning to exit the room.

Now that Aglaea had left the room, Anaxa glanced at Hyacine and signaled her with a nod. Hyacine stood up from her seat, appearing somewhat anxious. She had been holding a small box tightly in her lap the entire time.

"Your Majesty, I hope you will forgive me if I come across as disrespectful." She extended the small box toward him with trembling hands. "We wanted to ensure that you were… ahem… prepared for whatever might happen should you choose to see Lord Phainon against Aglaea's wishes."

Mydei took the box and opened it, revealing several items within. There was a glass bottle filled with a clear, viscous liquid, a rubber item that was distinctly phallic in shape, and two ointment jars intended for treating sores and wounds.

It didn't take long for Mydei to understand the purpose of the items, and a light blush began to creep onto his face. This only intensified Hyacine's embarrassment as her own cheeks flushed a bright red as she struggled to maintain her composure and act respectfully.

Anaxa waltzed back into the room and took a seat, seemingly unfazed by the awkward situation before him. He carefully placed a metal box on the table and opened it, revealing a well-padded interior that housed a glass syringe filled with a striking bright gold liquid.

He began detailing the syringe's contents, mentioning the various compounds and herbs utilized for alpha stabilizers, along with a few additional ingredients that enhanced its potency.

During this time, I collected blood samples that helped us gain a better understanding of how he may react to medication. I am confident that this current version of the stabilizer will significantly help with his rut."

Mydei listened intently and was now the one gripping the small box on his lap and doing his best to conceal it.

"You can inject this into his thigh or upper arm, whichever is easier for you," Anaxa continued. "However, I strongly recommend administering it while he is lying down or sitting."

Anaxa glanced at the clock on the wall before looking toward the door. "Aglaea should be returning within an hour or two," he said. "In the meantime, you can regroup with your comrades to discuss the search. Cipher and Castorice are currently leading the search, so you can depend on them, your Majesty. After that, you may also attend to your personal preparations." He gestured toward the box that Mydei was attempting to hide.

This caused Hyacine to cover her flushed face with her hands. Mydei, too, had a noticeable blush but maintained his composure as he rose from his seat. "Thank you for your assistance. I hope to return with good news."

As Mydei exited the room, he could faintly hear Hyacine expressing her embarrassment to Anaxa and complaining about how Anaxa was acting the whole time.

Upon seeing Phainon’s condition, Mydei took the opportunity to lecture him about his progress in regaining the weight and muscle he had lost over the past few months.

While they were in the midst of their final round, Phainon conceded defeat, which elicited a smug reaction from Mydei. Phainon, however, continued to attribute his loss to his current health and vowed to challenge Mydei again once he had fully recovered.

In Phainon’s defense, he was indeed in a dire state after enduring his rut without medication for several days, all while getting very little rest. Although he initially exhibited seemingly strong stamina during his rut, that energy faded almost immediately once the medication administered by Mydei began to take effect.

As Phainon was resting on the bed with steam coming off of his person from the tiring activities, Mydei retreated to the kitchen to cook something for them to eat.

A full day had passed with the two remaining in the bedroom, and Mydei insisted that Phainon needed to eat something hearty to compensate for the days he had been unable to do much due to the onset of his rut.

By this time, the knights stationed around Phainon’s estate were finally able to rest, as Aglaea confirmed that the crisis had been averted—for now. The thick wall of pheromones that surrounded Phainon’s estate had finally dissipated, allowing the palace staff to breathe a sigh of relief.

If it had taken longer for Phainon to emerge from that perilous state during his rut, the Imperator herself would have executed the commander responsible for the royal family's protection due to the incident that occurred within the palace grounds.

For now, everyone gave Phainon the space he needed to enjoy at least one good night’s rest before anyone dared to disturb him and Mydei.

“It’s true!” a knight exclaimed, taking a hearty swig of beer as he sat among his fellow knights in the bustling tavern at the Mamoreal Market. “The moment Lord Mydei arrived, the overwhelming stench of pheromones dissipated almost immediately!”

“Most knights stationed there for patrol were betas, yet we still felt chills run down our spines whenever we got too close to the manor itself. And yet Lord Mydei approached without fear. It was incredible!”

“I have never encountered an Alpha with such powerful pheromones. Not even Her Majesty, who already has quite intimidating pheromones, can compare,” one of the more drunk knights slurred loudly.

“Hey, quiet down! Do you really want to get dragged out for treason or something?”

“It truly is strange. What if Lord Phainon is actually an Enigma?”

The group fell silent for a moment, their brows furrowed in deep thought. However, it wasn’t long before they erupted into drunken, hearty laughter.

“An Enigma? Isn’t that just a fairytale?”

“Not to mention that the ones “recorded” in journals are only people of the highest noble birth! I say those cases were simply some olden kings and queens who wanted more recognition than they actually deserved.”

“Who knows? Lord Phainon might not have the purest blood, but he certainly has the purest heart!” The drunkard began to sway, a wide smile spreading across his face.

“Apparently, enigmas can impregnate even alphas, or you know, so the story goes.”

“Isn’t Lord Mydei an alpha? Can you imagine him with babe?”

The table grew silent once more as they pondered.

Soon, they all started nodding in silent agreement. Lord Mydei would be a very gorgeous and mighty presence while carrying a child.

The night deepened, and the cold winter wind swept through the silent city. Its serene ambiance was a result of Hysilen's leadership, as she ensured that the special knights and Kremnoan warriors tasked with finding and apprehending the person who attacked Phainon remained quiet and careful so as not to draw public attention. But not all knights got the memo to remain vigilant.

It was not surprising that the loud voices of the drunken knights allowed some passersby to overhear parts of their conversation.

As the morning light seeped into the bustling streets of Okhema, news of Mydeimos' return had already spread among the people. Many were skeptical of the rumors, as it seemed implausible for Mydeimos to come back, especially after the royal marriage decree had been issued for Phainon just a month earlier.

However, the tavern barmaids themselves confirmed that the knights were discussing the late-night rendezvous of Lord Mydeimos entering Lord Phainon’s estate. They couldn’t provide many details, but they were certain they heard Mydei’s name mentioned at least.

Another group of people claimed to have seen a caravan of dromas displaying Kremnoan flags arrive in the early hours of the morning. This only intensified speculation, as such caravans typically arrive during daylight when crowds can witness them. The timing of this arrival seemed almost deliberate, as if they were trying to conceal their entrance.

Was this a case of political asylum? Did Lord Phainon’s lover return to Okhema to safeguard their relationship?

The Mamoreal Market was already in disarray, and it was barely a few hours past sunrise. Aglaea, with a raging headache, submitted a note to discipline the knights who believed it was wise to spend the previous evening drinking excessively at the tavern after fulfilling a crucial duty.

From what she gathered, no one seemed to realize that Phainon had fallen into a rut, nor did they notice that Mydei had come to alleviate it. This lack of awareness was not surprising, as Mydei was not an omega, and therefore, no one really made the connection.

However, it was becoming increasingly challenging to manage public opinion, especially with the Kremnoan warriors present in Okhema. They were bound to hear the outrageous tales circulating about their king's late-night love affairs and the dramatizations surrounding his love story.

“What do you mean? His Majesty does not wish to be publicly announced as the king?” Aglaea recalled the moment from the previous evening when Hephaestion approached her on behalf of Mydei.

“We cannot presume to know our king's intentions, but he has insisted on remaining an unassuming Kremnoan noble set to wed his highness, Lord Phainon. We hope this arrangement can be maintained for the duration of our stay in the holy city.”

Aglaea struggled to understand why the newly proclaimed king would choose to conceal their identity. Six months ago, this decision may have been justifiable given the circumstances surrounding Mydei's arrival in Okhema. However, now it was challenging to even start drafting a report for the Imperator to explain the situation.

Despite the combined efforts of the Kremnoan warriors, the perpetrator who attacked Phainon remains at large. A few clues regarding their identity have emerged, but their current whereabouts are still unknown. They are starting to suspect that the individual may have fled Okhema immediately following the incident.

The scenario simply did not make sense. It was clearly a targeted attack, and yet there seemed to be a deeper motive to this apart from the initial assumptions they had.

It would seem logical to assume that the attacker was simply an Okheman citizen who was obsessively infatuated with Phainon, unwilling to accept his marriage to a foreigner. After all, Phainon was one of the most eligible bachelors in the country, despite his reputation for keeping romantic advances at a distance.

However, the attack was executed with remarkable precision. The assailant managed to knock out one of the royal attendants and conceal them so they could steal their uniform without anyone noticing. The rut inducer employed was handcrafted using illegal and controlled substances that would be inaccessible to an ordinary citizen. Furthermore, their escape was so swift that by the time the full investigation began, nearly all traces of them had vanished.

This situation did not bode well for Aglaea, and she suspected that a far larger scheme was in play. She could only surmise that it might be connected to the Kremnoans, a suspicion that was not unfounded. However, she would not dare make any accusations at this time without further investigation. Especially considering that Phainon and Mydeimos were now imprinted, she could not afford to antagonize anyone at this moment.

“Lady Aglaea?” Castorice called out for the third time, her voice filled with growing concern.

“Cas?” Aglaea finally snapped back to reality, glancing over to find that Castorice had entered her chamber without her noticing.

“The Kremnoan warriors discovered something, and it appears to be quite serious,” Castorice explained, her expression grave.

The midnight air in Okhema was heavy. The trouble following them would not end any time soon. At the very least, Aglaea hoped that Phainon and Mydei would be prepared for the days ahead.

“Mydei… I’m full,” Phainon whined, pouting with cheeks stuffed with food from Mydei’s relentless feeding.

The two were now seated in the kitchen, surrounded by Mydei’s cooking, which he had prepared while Phainon was out cold.

The feast laid out before Phainon showcased various delicious dishes crafted from random ingredients in his pantry with items he hadn’t even known were there or how to prepare. Mydei had created a meal that was both balanced and hearty, yet it was certainly not suitable for someone still feeling a bit under the weather.

“You’ve barely finished one plate.” Mydei huffed, arms crossed.

Phainon felt defeated as he saw the downcast expression on Mydei’s face. He found it impossible to resist anything his beloved did, especially when it was even the slightest bit adorable.

Never mind the fact that Phainon had been deliberately looking the other way whenever Mydei sneakily added more food to his plate. He was genuinely stuffed and felt as though he couldn’t get up from his seat. But he would be damned if he ever made his beloved sad!

With the last bit of energy he had, he finally forced down the final morsel of food left on his plate. At least this time, with the plate cleaned down to the last crumb, Mydei wouldn't be able to sneak in more food.

Mydei looked a bit more satisfied after seeing Phainon finish the plate, but he remained genuinely concerned about Phainon’s well-being since their last meeting. Although Phainon had regained some weight, Mydei could still see that his strength and stamina were lacking. The fact that a random person had easily taken Phainon down with hardly a fight only heightened Mydei's worries.

What might have happened if help hadn’t arrived in time? The attacker was aware of Phainon's vulnerable state and exploited it to their advantage. The thought of Phainon being assaulted in such a manner filled Mydei with deep anger, evident in the frown that marred his face.

“Is something wrong, Mydei?” Phainon asked, sensing the shift in Mydei’s expression. He got up and wrapped his arms around the man, wanting to comfort him in the embrace.

“I’ll be joining the search team in the morning. You should stay here and get some proper rest,” Mydei said, turning to face the man holding onto him.

“I’m going with you!” Phainon insisted, interrupting Mydei.

“Your pheromones are still balancing out and have not returned to normal.”

“Then you would leave me here all alone? All by myself? On my very lonesome?” Phainon asked with bright blue eyes that pleaded with teary-eyed intensity.

Mydei paused for a moment, not having thought about that.

“I will be so lonely… What if someone comes for me again while I’m alone?”

“I won’t let that happen,” Mydei interjected, his voice rising slightly at the thought of someone approaching Phainon again.

“Then please stay with me?” Phainon pleaded, pulling Mydei closer and wrapping his arms around him tightly, tucking his head into the crook of Mydei’s neck. “Please don’t leave me.”

Mydei’s eyes finally softened as he wrapped his arms around Phainon this time. “I won’t leave you.”

There was a profound sense of longing and regret in those words. Despite Phainon’s typically positive and cheerful demeanor, he was not immune to feelings of rejection and loss. After enduring months of separation and the accompanying persistent pain, he had become increasingly paranoid and anxious at the thought of seeing Mydei again, only to watch him leave once more.

Mydei could feel this, and yet he was also the same.

Phainon knew that their relationship right now was still not free of challenges, and at any point, it might not even reach the hopeful happy ending they wanted. So even at this fleeting moment that they are together without anyone else reminding them of their reality, Phainon wanted to cling to him as much as he could.

The two were definitely determined to maintain their relationship, but there were still hurdles they needed to pass in order to keep themselves in each other’s lives. Being royalty in two opposing nations was one thing, but one being the literal king of one was an entirely different problem. Given Cerydra's nature, it was highly unlikely that she would permit Phainon to become a consort beyond the borders of Okhema.

The public outcry following the sudden marriage proposal announced a month ago elicited a range of mixed reactions. Many Okheman citizens expressed reservations about the Kremnoans, leading to widespread perceptions of arrogance regarding the proposal.

However, now that the people had caught wind of Mydeimos’ secret return to Okhema, reactions were even more mixed and confused. While many rejoiced at the return of Phainon’s beloved, others expressed concern about the potential for renewed conflict between the two nations, especially given that Mydeimos had been forced to leave just six months prior.

The Mamoreal Palace was not helping its case by remaining secretive about the marriage proposal. Who was the high-ranking royal from Castrum Kremnos that proposed to Phainon? Typically, in such public proposals, it is the person being proposed to who must leave their country, a fact that many Okheman citizens found unacceptable.

Is accepting Mydeimos back into Okhema considered an act of defiance against the Kremnoan royal family? So many questions swirled in the voices echoing through the markets, and many awaited news like it was the latest chapter of their favorite bard's tale.

Chapter End Notes

chapters.title: Chapter 25: A Familiar Scent
chapters.html:
Chapter Notes

Flu season really came in strong this year and I’ve been swamped with non-stop overtime at work. This is my first day off in two weeks….

Everyone, please be sure to drink lots of water and take some vitamins. Also always please be mindful of others too! Wear a mask when you’re sick and don’t just spread around the flu by sneezing or coughing in public without covering.

This is a public service announcement from your local(?) underpaid healthcare professional.

With Phainon’s insistence, Mydei ended up staying at the manor with him for at least two more days while Phainon stabilized. During this time, the state of the investigations outside was becoming increasingly concerning.

They had anticipated that Phainon and Mydei would remain cooped up in the manor for no more than a day, but now it seemed they were about to reach three days without any indication of their departure. This situation was becoming increasingly frustrating for those waiting on them, yet no one had the heart to barge in and disrupt their time together.

No one except Anaxa, of course. He had grown tired of everyone tiptoeing around the need to get both Phainon and Mydei’s attention as soon as possible. With full confidence and zero shame, he made his way to the estate.

By the time a knight noticed him, Anaxa was already halfway down the front walkway, and it was too late for anyone to intervene or stop him.

Aglaea was livid when her nymphs reported Anaxa's intrusion, but she found it difficult to stay angry. There was a genuine emergency that required the attention of the two lovebirds huddled inside the manor.

It was Mydei who answered the door for Anaxa, and they exchanged a few words before he went back inside. Anaxa emerged with an odd smile on his face, giving the impression that he was reveling in some kind of success.

The medication he had provided worked splendidly on Phainon, though it came with a few side effects that made Phainon quite lethargic. However, this was an outcome he had anticipated, so he considered it an overwhelming success.

Hyacine and Castorice were out of breath, already waiting for him at the front gates of Phainon’s estate. They had rushed there as soon as they heard the news about “that madman from the Grove” breaking protocol and entering the estate.

“Professor!” Hyacine exclaimed while catching her breath.

Anaxa regained his stoic demeanor and calmly replied, “Gather everyone. We will hold the discussion inside the manor this evening.”

“But Lady Aglaea said…” Castorice trailed off, not wanting to talk back.

“It was Mydeimos’ suggestion, and I concur that it would be best for Phainon to remain inside the manor for the time being. He is still in recovery.” Anaxa chose not to elaborate further, knowing his two students would understand.

“Alright. I will inform the Kremnoan Detachment immediately. Hyacine, could you please go to Lady Aglaea as well?” Castorice and Hyacine exchanged nods and departed promptly.

Anaxa was left focused on jotting down various incomprehensible notes in his booklet, while the knights on duty carefully avoided making eye contact.

It appears that, while the rut suppressant proved effective, it had considerable side effects on Phainon. Mydei mentioned that Phainon was noticeably more moody and clingy, and he was struggling with both his strength and stamina.

The dosage for that specific suppressant was indeed almost ten times stronger than that for regular alphas, but any lower dosage had not been effective for Phainon in the past. The muscle relaxant was certainly impacting his physical condition, and the emotional side effects were likely a consequence of this.

He ultimately agreed to hold the meeting inside the manor rather than allowing Phainon to go out while his attacker remained unfound. Given the alarming findings from the past few days, it was clear that Phainon would be safer in a controlled environment with Mydeimos closely monitoring him.

Mydei refrained from commenting on Phainon’s behavior, understanding that it was likely a side effect of the medication. He was aware that Phainon had a strong preference for close contact and had previously expressed concern about Mydei's occasional disappearances.

But recently, Mydei observed a notable increase in Phainon's paranoia and anxiety, which in turn also worried him. This could also stem from the trauma of his recent attack, prompting Mydei to be particularly attentive to his care during this period.

Mydei made sure to remain within Phainon’s line of sight, releasing soothing pheromones whenever he sensed a spike in Phainon’s anxiety. This was the first time Phainon’s rut was managed with a suppressant, and while he was able to get up after just one day instead of being incapacitated for a whole month, his body still required time to adjust to the initial shock.

“The investigation team will be coming here tonight,” Mydei informed Phainon as he settled back onto the living room couch. Phainon was seated nearby, listening to the conversation with Anaxa while keeping himself hidden from view.

Phainon was puzzled. "Here? Did something happen?"

“It seems so. There were some troubling findings, and they need to speak with us as soon as possible.”

“We could have just met them at the Mamoreal Palace.”

“I can go, but you need to stay here.”

Phainon whined, clinging to Mydei's arm with a pout.

“Wouldn’t this be better? I don’t have to go anywhere." Mydei offered him a gentle smile, playfully pinching his pouting cheek.

Phainon could not argue with that and continued to nuzzle against Mydei. He was aware of how clingy he had been these past few days and felt a bit embarrassed by this uncontrollable urge. However, Mydei always provided him with reassurance, showering him with care and affection.

“Your pheromones are getting thicker again.” Mydei commented, leaning in to sniff at Phainon’s neck.

Phainon blushed lightly at the comment, feeling somewhat self-conscious about his ongoing struggle to control his pheromones. “I-I’ll go take a warm bath,” he stammered.

“Mm… Okay.” Mydei nodded and playfully ruffled Phainon’s hair.

As soon as Phainon moved back, he got up and sprinted away with surprising speed. This didn’t really alarm Mydei since Phainon had definitely been having various mood swings in the past few days. If anything, at least he found Phainon’s reluctance and shy side adorable. He knew that once Phainon was back to his normal self, he would not be able to see this somewhat childlike side.

While Phainon was in the bath, a wave of anxiety washed over him once more. He had ventured off on his own this time, leaving him unable to see where Mydei was. However, he felt embarrassed at the thought of rushing back out now that he was fully nude and submerged in the water.

While he contemplated whether to finish his bath quickly or step outside to check on Mydei, he remained unaware of the quiet footsteps approaching from behind him.

This was the first time Phainon had been on his own in a while, following a long period of being coddled by Mydei. He was still releasing unstable pheromones, charged with nervousness, guilt, fear, and a mix of other emotions. Suddenly, the sound of rustling clothes behind him caught his attention, prompting him to turn around quickly.

His mouth fell open as he watched Mydei enter the room and gradually remove the little clothing he had on. Mydei maintained an intense gaze, never breaking eye contact with Phainon.

Phainon held his breath, his eyes tracing every slow movement Mydei made. Just that morning, as they had awakened, he had left several kiss marks down Mydei’s chest, which were now strikingly visible—bright red against the dim light that illuminated Mydei as he approached.

“M-Mydei?” Phainon finally spoke up as Mydei removed the last article of clothing that concealed his most private parts, revealing more visible red marks scattered across Mydei’s inner thighs. The dim lighting in the room made every kiss and bite shimmer almost as brightly as the red tattoos that adorned Mydei’s body.

“What’s wrong?” Mydei asked in a nonchalant tone, but Phainon sensed the teasing in the way Mydei sensually sauntered toward him, his movements exaggerated and his eye contact intense. Phainon felt a deep awe each time his gaze swept over Mydei’s incredible body. How could Mydei continue to tempt him like this?

Mydei was, in reality, doing nothing whatsoever. Phainon was merely caught up in an extraordinary daydream as he observed the love of his life enter the room, prepared to take a bath as well.

After the long winter had finally passed, today finally felt warm, and they had sweated quite a bit while wrestling around in bed that morning. Mydei had quickly adapted to the bathing customs of the Okheman people and actually looked forward to taking multiple warm and soothing baths each day, which Phainon often encouraged him to enjoy.

This time, Mydei entered the bath on his own initiative after Phainon had rushed off by himself. Although it felt unusual, Mydei understood that Phainon was feeling embarrassed.

Mydei cautiously lowered himself into the water, grimacing at the chilly temperature. Phainon had deliberately turned off the heater to help himself “calm down.”

“I-I’ll turn the heater up!” Phainon exclaimed, looking away as he tried to flee the water again. However, Mydei was faster this time. He grabbed Phainon and pulled him back into the water, shoving him against the edge of the pool.

Phainon was compelled to sit on the step as Mydei turned around and nestled between Phainon’s legs, leaning his back against Phainon’s chest.

It didn’t take longer than five seconds for Mydei to feel something incredibly hard pressing against his back, leaving Phainon too stunned to move or speak. Phainon’s hands remained suspended in the air, unsure of where to place them.

“Still so energetic, huh?” Mydei remarked, casually washing his arms and splashing water over his face and hair. “But that’s too bad. We have guests arriving soon, so stop messing around.”

Mydei reached an arm over his shoulder to gently sweep his hair away from his back, exposing the nape of his neck to Phainon. Several bite marks dotted the area, none deep enough to be permanent, and since Mydei was an alpha, a mate mark was impossible to leave.

The sight of it still left Phainon’s senses tingling, his eyes widening with desire as a thirst parched his throat. His breathing became erratic, and his face flushed with a mix of embarrassment and determination.

Mydei continued to wash himself nonchalantly, his slow movements showcasing every muscle on his back as they flexed and relaxed in clear view of the unmoving man behind him. Occasionally, he would shift back slightly on his seat, grazing against the hardened flesh pressing against him, but he would pull away almost deliberately whenever Phainon seemed ready to make a sound.

Phainon bit his lip, gathering the courage to grip Mydei’s waist in an attempt to still the man’s constant squirming over him. “Mydei, are you teasing me?”

“I told you to stop messing around,” Mydei replied with a scoff. He shifted his position, turning to face Phainon as he settled atop his lap. Cupping water in his hand, he gently splashed it over his chest, revealing to Phainon that most of the blushing red marks from earlier were fading away, as if being washed clean.

This made Phainon’s eyebrows furrow in annoyance, as he despised how quickly his marks were fading. It challenged the internal instinct that most alphas experienced, but Mydei soothed him by rubbing a thumb over his wrinkled brow. “Let’s go get ready before the guests arrive.”

Mydei stood up from the pool and stepped out of the water, using a towel to dry himself off. Phainon, still experiencing an unwanted arousal, curled up against the edge to calm down. They both understood that if they allowed things to escalate, they would end up losing track of time and leaving their guests unattended outside.

While they had grown accustomed to invading each other’s personal space, Mydei believed, based on what Phainon had told him, that this behavior was typical among couples and not inherently sexual. However, Phainon had been engaging in this closeness with a different intention the whole time.

Phainon could only blame himself for being left in the water without attention.

As Phainon took a few minutes to himself in the bath, Mydei changed into fresh clothes and headed straight to the kitchen to prepare food for their guests. Although he recognized that the term “guests” wasn’t entirely accurate since they were gathering for a serious political meeting, he aimed to keep the atmosphere light around Phainon rather than allowing everyone to remain on edge.

Mydei began to worry about the findings of the investigation. He had hoped that while the Kremnoan Detachment assisted in locating the perpetrator, it would mean that he would receive good news in less than a day.

However, a few days later, he receives a cryptic message from Anaxa this morning regarding suspicious findings and a request to speak directly with him and Phainon. This left him feeling uneasy, a discomfort he recognized all too well but often brushed aside in light of his strengths.

If anyone dared to approach Phainon again with the intent to harm him, Mydei vowed upon the Lance of Fury that he would put an end to them right then and there. Lost in his own thoughts, Mydei had become so distracted that the vegetables he was cutting were reduced to irregular chunks, resulting in more pieces than he had intended to use.

It appeared they would be having vegetable stew for dinner that night.

Aglaea arrived first, accompanied by Castorice and Cipher. They were greeted warmly by Phainon at the door and led directly to the dining room, where a lavish feast awaited them. Although surprised by the spread, they felt a wave of relief and happiness upon seeing how lively and cheerful Phainon had become since their last meeting.

Hephaestion and Perdikkas arrived next, accompanied by a personal escort of knights. The rest of their detachment insisted on continuing their patrol with the search party, believing that the two of them would suffice for this meeting.

The two felt undeniably nervous upon their arrival, intimidated by the number of Okheman knights escorting them. However, they soon found themselves relaxing at the sight of their king, who appeared to be in much higher spirits than when they had first come to the kingdom.

Finally, Anaxa arrived with Hyacine. They had taken a bit longer to reach the gathering because they were waiting for their testing results to be completed. Hyacine was particularly thrilled to see that Phainon’s condition had nearly returned to normal.

As they all sat around the table, an air of awkwardness and tension filled the room. They were gathered to discuss something of great importance, but no one wanted to spoil the impressive spread of food laid out before them. Mydei had utilized whatever ingredients were on hand, yet his culinary skills remained unmatched, even among the most discerning Kremnoan mothers back home.

“Let’s enjoy the warm food first before proceeding,” Aglaea suggested with a soft smile.

Everyone agreed, and Castorice added with a soft chuckle, “It’s likely the only chance we have to enjoy food from such an incredible cook that Lord Phainon has been excitedly talking about for months.”

“Cas…!” Phainon felt a flush of embarrassment at the remark, which drew more laughter from the table.

The atmosphere became lighter, and for the next few minutes, everyone felt more at ease. However, they all understood that they needed to address the urgent issue that had been weighing on their minds for the past two days.

As soon as everyone finished eating, Anaxa stood up to begin the discussion. “As most of you know, the Kremnoan Detachment discovered evidence likely left by the perpetrator at their hideout in one of the inns in the kingdom. The skills of this individual were incredibly professional. However, thanks to the trained eyes of the search party, they managed to find suspicious trace amounts of a certain black powder on the ground, along with a torn coat worn by the suspect on the day of the attack, as confirmed by Cipher.”

He directed everyone's attention to Hyacine, who stood up to display a vial containing a small amount of the black powder. The powder was coarse and had a purplish tint, but it did not possess any notable qualities that would raise alarm.

“Initially, we did not think much of this powder. But with the search team wanting to be thorough, they decided to collect samples during their investigation.” Anaxa then shifted his focus to the two Kremnoan Detachment warriors across from him, signaling for them to continue the discussion.

"That day, we arrived while the investigation team was collecting samples of the powder," Hephaestion explained. "Once we entered the room, it didn’t take long for us to recognize a very familiar scent..."

Hyacine rose from her seat and performed a light curtsy before handing the vial to Mydei. He brought the vial closer to his nose to inhale the scent. As the familiar aroma reached his nostrils, his eyes widened, and he found himself unable to speak.

For a moment, Mydei felt a wave crash over him, a cold, bitter wind crawling up his back and leaving goosebumps on his arms. He recognized that scent all too well.

It was the same scent he had noticed from his father when Eurypon began his slow descent into madness. This was the same scent that lingered when he opened the last letter from his mother, Gorgo. An intoxicatingly sweet yet repulsive aroma that permeated the Kremnoan royal palace for years as it spiraled into chaos. A scent that many of the remaining, surviving Kremnoan nobles were now struggling to fight against for their lives.

“We found the same black powder compound mixed into the rut inducer that was used in the attack.”

chapters.title: Chapter 26: Worldbearing
chapters.html:
Chapter Notes

I want to address the rude comment from last chapter first. Although I can see that the comment was likely ragebait or just impatient joking, please never comment like that again on any work. I wish adults had more time to spare, but reality is not that forgiving. There’s a reason why I stopped creating fanworks after starting university back then, and that’s because my job is literally one of the worst ones when it comes to getting lots of “adult time”.

Thank you to everyone who responded to the rude comment, and from now on, I will be automatically deleting any rude comments moving forward. I don’t want any unecessary negativity under my works.

I will be returning early to my old assigned workplace perhaps around mid-December. Hopefully this will revert my schedule back to normal, because I am literally withering away. Currently, I am running on 12-16 hour shifts daily with 3-5 hours of sleep on most days, and it doesn’t help that I’m obsessed with Currency Wars (It’s successfully helping me cope with the ending of 3.7). I’m also sobbing coz I couldn’t get the preorder for Mydei and Phainon Nuis. Does anyone know where to else to order the nuis TT

After the meeting, Phainon and Mydei found themselves alone again in the manor. Phainon struggled to grasp the situation, as the Kremnoan party and even Mydei spoke cryptically about the mysterious black powder. However, it was clear to Phainon that Mydei was extremely stressed and upset.

The pheromones Mydei released were erratic and charged with anger. Phainon felt a choking sensation in his throat from their imprint, and Mydei refused to sit down or relax since everyone had left.

How could Mydei possibly relax? The presence of the black powder raised troubling questions. It was simply inconceivable that it had arrived here by accident, especially considering that the primary ingredient for the mixture was a plant that could only thrive in Kremnoan soil.

So many scenarios raced through Mydei’s mind, and none offered any comfort. Was the drug somehow smuggled out of Castrum Kremnos? How could it have breached Okheman borders so quickly, especially when it was composed of extremely dangerous compounds?

He recalled the recent meetings concerning the council of advisors. Some of those criminals had managed to escape and flee from Castrum Kremnos. Had they intentionally come to Okhema?

The conclusion provided some clarity regarding how the perpetrator had managed to skillfully evade the investigation for several days. However, this realization only intensified Mydei's anger.

Did they seek revenge after being justly arrested and executed? And their chosen target was his fiancé? How could they possibly have discovered that? Unless, of course, there have already been spies lurking within the Okheman walls for quite some time.

Hysilens has been instructed to enhance security for all Okheman royals, particularly for the Imperator herself. It’s uncertain whether anyone else has ingested significant amounts of the black powder. Perdikkas has been working overtime alongside Anaxa and his team to test everyone in the Mamoreal Palace.

The more Mydei pondered the situation, the deeper his scowl became, and his sighs grew louder as he paced around the living room.

Was coming here a mistake? Had he become too selfish and impatient, wanting to be here despite still having unresolved issues in his own country?

The incident was undoubtedly a targeted attack against Phainon, and Mydei couldn’t shake the thought of postponing their relationship once more. How could he risk Phainon’s safety because of a vendetta he had unknowingly brought from home?

“Mydei…” Phainon finally stood up, crept up behind Mydei, and wrapped his arms around him in a tight hug. “Everything is going to be fine.” He pressed a gentle kiss to the back of Mydei’s head, his soft hair brushing against Phainon’s cheeks ever so slightly.

Mydei struggled to find his voice, but gradually, the tension in his body began to dissolve in Phainon's warm embrace. “That powder… it was the cause of my father's madness. It also led to my mother's death and nearly brought down the entire Kremnoan empire.”

Phainon had already suspected the truth, but hearing Mydei confirm it weighed heavily on his heart.

“And now it’s trying to take you away too,” Mydei said, his voice barely above a whisper, yet Phainon heard him loud and clear.

Phainon turned their bodies to face each other, gently cradling Mydei's face in his hands. “But I’m right here! If you think that’s enough to make me leave, you’re sorely mistaken.” He joked with a playful laugh, hoping to draw Mydei out of his seriousness.

“HKS…” Mydei scoffed, letting out a weary laugh. “I just can’t bear the thought of seeing you in pain again.”

He couldn’t bear the thought of losing Phainon again. The wound he never confronted after losing the young Khaslana all those years ago still left a painful sensation in his chest whenever he recalled it. Additionally, the memory of how Phainon had suffered for several months after his return to Castrum Kremnos was a source of deep regret for him.

“I promise that in the next few days, I’ll be back to normal.” Phainon leaned in closer, their lips almost touching. “And this time, I will protect you too. You don’t have to handle everything on your own, okay?”

“We’ll see about that. You’re so thin and lightweight that I could lift you with one arm right now,” Mydei said with a smirk, already feeling a sense of relief as the anger subsided.

Phainon gasped and puffed out his cheeks, ready to argue. However, Mydei silenced him by pressing their lips together firmly this time.

The two paused for a long moment, sharing a gentle and loving kiss. It wasn’t a kiss that ignited passion or left them feeling heated and handsy. Instead, it was careful and comforting. They spent the remainder of the day wrapped in each other’s arms, remaining close until they both felt better.

A few days passed, and there were still no leads in finding the perpetrator. At this point, the search party was certain that the attacker had fled Okhema. The citizens were growing increasingly distressed by the heightened military presence and the sudden inspections of their homes, which occurred without warrants or explanations regarding what the knights were seeking.

To alleviate the growing unease among the public, the military presence throughout the kingdom was returned to normal. All checkpoints leading in and out of Okhema, however, underwent stricter scrutiny. Merchants and travelers now faced more thorough inspections, and many were denied entry into the Holy City unless they presented complete paperwork with accurate information. Any suspicious cargo was confiscated at the gates, and merchants would be compensated if no illegal items were discovered in their confiscated goods.

Tension still hung over the kingdom due to the Mamoreal Palace's unusual secrecy, with no clear reasons communicated to the public. Even the lower-ranking knights were left in the dark about the situation.

This turn of events was not particularly surprising given the recent developments. Following the testing conducted by Perdikkas and Anaxa’s team, several members of the royal family were found to have trace amounts of the black powder in their systems.

Even the Imperator herself tested positive, despite having all her meals inspected by Hysilens at all times.

Because the situation was discovered early, the symptoms of madness had not yet manifested. However, this did little to alleviate their fears, as it had just been proven that the security of Okhema was severely compromised. If they hadn't escalated the incident with Phainon, they would have remained unaware of the dangers they faced.

Phainon’s intake of the black powder poison was the most concentrated. However, he managed to endure the effects, even while experiencing his rut. It was widely agreed that the attack on Phainon was deliberate, as it was evident they sought to induce his rut and potentially transport him elsewhere while he was vulnerable and unable to protect himself.

It was lucky, thanks to Aglaea’s foresight, that she always left a nymph close to Phainon’s house and that Cipher was ready to charge at a moment's notice should an emergency happen. At the very least, the perpetrator was not knowledgeable enough to learn of these safeties in place since it always appeared that Phainon was isolated and unguarded despite being a royal family member.

Okhema’s royal court has been deeply divided since the discovery of the black powder and the testing results that showed several family members tested positive. While some were relieved that the drug was identified early, many voiced their concerns and distrust toward the Kremnoan party that had arrived in the Holy City.

The arrival of this mystery drug in Okhema was perplexing, especially since it happened suspiciously when the royal family had become entangled with the so-called “barbarians” from Kremnos. As a result, they found themselves to be under attack.

Although no one dared to openly accuse Cerydra, all eyes were on Phainon, who was clearly under attack. To the royal court, there seemed to be no justification for Phainon to accept a proposal from Castrum Kremnos after the failure of the first engagement. However, they believed that his decision to accept this second engagement was the catalyst for the current situation.

Some even questioned Phainon’s sanity for desiring to marry a dubious alpha man from Castrum Kremnos, as if he were being enchanted or poisoned into feeling attracted to him.

Fortunately, neither Phainon nor Mydei was present during this time, but the members of the Kremnoan Detachment overheard everything. They recognized the animosity and fear in the royal court, but it was disheartening to realize that their efforts to assist in the situation were yielding no positive results.

Their situation was unfavorable, as they were present under the pretense of being escorts for a Kremnoan bride rather than as warriors directly commanded by their king. Although Aglaea assured them they would be protected under Okhema, regardless of the royal court’s remarks, they began to feel ostracized and unwelcome.

If it weren’t for their unwavering loyalty to their king, Mydeimos, they would have already packed their bags and departed. Surely, this noisy royal court can handle the crisis on their own, concerning a chemical compound that only Kremnoan scholars are familiar with, right?

After those few days, most people chose to relax and ignore the ongoing crisis. However, since the issues remain unresolved and many individuals are still on edge, the engagement has been postponed once again until further notice.

The news made Phainon very disheartened. It felt unfair that the royal court was once again trying to control his life. They had previously assigned him this responsibility, and now they were attempting to take it back. How was that fair?

While Phainon worried about that, he was unable to voice his dissatisfaction very much, as his attention was split with how he was getting whipped back into shape with Mydei’s strict guidance.

He underestimated the strictness of Mydei's training plan. The exercise regimen proved to be the most challenging he had ever faced, far more difficult than his previous soldier training. Mydei was relentless, insisting that he complete every set without exception. Additionally, Phainon's diet was revamped to optimize his training results. Although the food remained delicious and satisfying, he found himself burning through most of it as his workouts progressed.

At first, Phainon felt overwhelmed, but he soon realized that his efforts were successfully distracting Mydei from stressors in other areas. He persevered, determined not to disappoint Mydei. However, if he were honest with himself, he would acknowledge that his motivation to give his all stemmed from Mydei's insistence on postponing any nighttime activities until Phainon’s overall health improved. Despite his whining and begging, Mydei remained steadfast in his commitment to prioritize Phainon’s health above all else.

The results were impressive! After just a few days of intense training, Phainon had nearly regained his muscle tone, and his stamina was back to normal. His complexion appeared healthier, and even the pheromones surrounding him became more balanced and relaxed.

Mydei felt a sense of pride in his efforts and was relieved to see Phainon returning to his usual self. Phainon’s mood and emotional state had improved significantly, which created a more comfortable atmosphere for both of them.

“Can I get my reward now?” Phainon asked as he crawled on top of Mydei on the bed. He had been complaining about it all day after completing his strict ten-day training plan.

The man was shamelessly shirtless, positioning his arms on either side of Mydei. He noticed Mydei’s gaze wandering over his newly toned body, and it filled him with a sense of satisfaction to see that his efforts were yielding such positive results.

However, Mydei was not easily swayed or fooled by Phainon’s playful antics. “I think you could use another week of training,” he replied, his tone flat and unimpressed, his eyes scrutinizing the state of Phainon’s torso.

“Mydei…” Phainon whined again, flopping onto Mydei and attempting to wrap him in a hug.

“I’m just kidding,” Mydei chuckled, though he quickly cleared his throat to adopt a more serious tone. “We will be meeting with the Imperator tomorrow, so we need to get to bed early.”

Phainon understood precisely what Mydei meant. Neither of them had self-control when it came to each other. They knew they could not afford to be late or appear worn out and disheveled in front of Cerydra. It was already very late into the night, and the best thing they could do was sleep.

“It’s not fair…” Phainon said sadly, burying his face in the pillow while remaining on top of Mydei.

“What's unfair? Aren't you excited to finally leave the estate after such a long time?”

“It’s not that. It’s about our engagement. They said it would be postponed indefinitely. How is that fair?”

Mydei agreed but didn’t want to upset Phainon. After all, royal engagements were significant political matters. They would involve grand celebrations and numerous planned activities in anticipation of the wedding.

In the current political climate, organizing grand celebrations would be challenging, as many were still uneasy about the nation's safety. While the public would likely embrace and enjoy such festivities, the aristocratic circles would undoubtedly highlight the underlying tensions and cause the overall celebrations to be strained.

Of course, there was another, more pressing issue—the very reason they would be meeting with Cerydra in the morning.

Mydeimos was a king.

If this marriage occurs, the most logical outcome would be for Phainon to abandon his position in Okhema and assume the role of king consort for Mydei.

The implications of this situation would not only impact the political standing of Castrum Kremnos and Okhema within Amphoreus, but it would also create tension in Phainon's relationships with the other members of the Okheman royal family.

In no scenario would Cerydra ever agree to the idea of Phainon leaving his position in Okhema to be sent away to a different nation, as if they were the ones in need. Wars would erupt before the great Imperator of Amphoreus would tolerate such disrespect in her royal court.

Phainon felt uncertain about what would transpire during their conversation with Cerydra the next day, yet he held onto the hope that she would still grant her blessing for their marriage, regardless of the circumstances.

Mydei was less worried about the situation, which helped ease Phainon's own anxiety. They had no way of knowing how Cerydra would truly react when they faced her, and the only way to find out was to confront her directly and seek her answer. Mydei even joked about switching roles and becoming Phainon's consort instead. The mere thought sent shivers down Phainon's spine as he envisioned the army of Kremnoan soldiers, their spears raised against him.

“You haven’t even proposed to me again,” Mydei pointed out with a yawn, the stillness of the night making him feel increasingly drowsy.

Hearing this, Phainon jumped out of bed with remarkable speed, startling Mydei and shaking him from his drowsiness.

“Where are you going?” Mydei glared at him, annoyed by the sudden jolt from his drowsiness.

Phainon began rummaging through the drawers next to the bed, pulling out various random items and trinkets he had collected over the years. Whether it was an obscure novelty item or an ancient artifact, Phainon took joy in gathering these curiosities and displaying them around the house.

By the time Phainon located the box he had been searching for, Mydei had already propped himself up on the side of the bed, stretching his arms and emitting a loud yawn.

“Everything has been moving so fast over the past few days that I completely forgot about it,” Phainon admitted shyly, lowering his head in shame as he presented the box to Mydei while kneeling on the floor in front of him.

“What's this?” Mydei asked, taking the box and carefully opening it. His eyes widened as they darted between the items inside and Phainon, who remained kneeling with his head bowed.

Inside the box were two almost identical signet rings. One was a ring that Mydei recognized all too well: his mother’s ring. He recalled sending this ring along with the sealed proposal announcement nearly two months ago.

The ring beside it was another intricately crafted gold piece, but instead of featuring the symbol of Nikador like his mother’s ring, it displayed the emblem of Kephale, the Worldbearing titan.

“I asked the best craftsman in Okhema to make an identical ring so that we could match.” Phainon shyly admitted, “I-I hope that’s okay…?”

The craftsmanship was undeniably exceptional, as Mydei would easily be convinced if someone claimed that both rings were crafted by the same artisan using the same type of gold.

He set the box aside and pulled Phainon up by the arm, urging him to stand and stop acting like a dog being punished. Taking his mother’s ring, he held Phainon’s hand and slid the ring onto his finger. “Marry me, Phainon… Khaslana of Aedes Elysia.”

Phainon was taken aback and rendered speechless by the gesture, momentarily forgetting that he was supposed to be the one proposing. Hearing the name of his hometown after so many years caught him off guard. He never imagined anyone would remember that place after it was destroyed all those years ago. Yet, he recalled that it was where he had met Mydei as a child. While the rest of the world may have forgotten his home, the person who mattered most to him had not.

Tears streamed down his face as he nodded vigorously in agreement to the proposal of marriage.

The ring slid onto Phainon’s fingers like a perfect fit, which were longer and more slender, bringing a smile to Mydei’s face. In contrast, Mydei’s own fingers were considerably larger and thicker, so the ring had never fit him when he received it back recently. However, he couldn't help but marvel at how destiny seemed to work, ensuring that the ring would be a perfect fit for his future partner instead.

After seeing the beautiful smile on Mydei’s face, Phainon regained his senses and reached for the Worldbearing ring. With trembling hands, he took Mydei’s relaxed hand and attempted to slide the ring onto his finger.

“How did you know my ring size?” Mydei marveled at how perfectly the ring fit him, lifting his arm to admire it.

“When we were in Castrum Kremnos, I took some thread from my coat and tied it around your finger while you were asleep,” Phainon admitted. He chose not to mention the number of attempts it took or how he struggled for nearly an hour because Mydei kept moving or the thread kept snapping.

Mydei lifted both arms, signaling for Phainon to come closer for a hug. Without hesitation, Phainon leaped into Mydei's embrace, and they both tumbled onto the bed, erupting into laughter.

“No take-backs, okay?” Phainon joked, though his attempt at humor fell flat as Mydei noticed the tears glistening in his eyes.

“No take-backs.” Mydei tightened his embrace, adjusting their positions so they could finally settle in for the much-needed sleep.
